rules.rule_name: Program Initialization
rules.rule_description: On every program entry, all processing flags are reset to their default states and all message fields are cleared to ensure a clean processing environment.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
1: Program Initialization
Set all flags and clear messages

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List program has been invoked
acceptance_criteria.When: The program begins execution
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error flag is set to OFF, the end-of-file indicator is set to NOT-EOF, the next-page indicator is set to TRUE, the screen erase flag is set to YES, the message field is cleared to spaces, the screen error message field is cleared to spaces, and the cursor is positioned at the User ID input field

rules.rule_name: Session Validation
rules.rule_description: The program verifies that a valid user session exists before allowing access to the User List screen. If no session context is present, the user is redirected to the Sign-On screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
2: Session Validation
Valid user session exists?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List program has been invoked
acceptance_criteria.When: No communication area is passed to the program (session length equals zero)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The target program is set to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) and control is transferred to that screen, preventing access to the User List

rules.rule_name: First-Time Screen Display Detection
rules.rule_description: The program distinguishes between the first entry and subsequent re-entries to determine whether to auto-load the user list or to process user input from the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
3: First-Time Screen Display
First entry into program?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid user session exists and the communication area is available
acceptance_criteria.When: The program re-entry flag in the communication area is NOT set (first-time entry)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program marks itself as re-enterable, clears the screen output area to low-values, automatically processes the Enter key logic to load the first page of users, and displays the User List screen

rules.rule_name: User Input Reception
rules.rule_description: On re-entry to the program, the system reads all input data entered by the user from the User List screen before processing any actions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
4: User Input Reception
Receive screen input from user

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid user session exists and the program has been previously displayed to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The user submits the screen by pressing any key
acceptance_criteria.Then: All screen input data including selection codes, User ID search field, and the function key pressed are received from the terminal into the program's input area for processing

rules.rule_name: Function Key Routing
rules.rule_description: The program routes processing to the appropriate function based on which key the user pressed: Enter for selection/search, PF3 for menu return, PF7 for page backward, PF8 for page forward, or any other key triggers an invalid key error.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
5: Function Key Routing
Which key was pressed?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the User List screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The program evaluates the key pressed by the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: If ENTER was pressed, user selection and search processing is performed; if PF3 was pressed, the user is navigated to the Admin Menu (COADM01C); if PF7 was pressed, backward page navigation is performed; if PF8 was pressed, forward page navigation is performed; if any other key was pressed, an invalid key error message is displayed

rules.rule_name: Invalid Key Handling
rules.rule_description: When the user presses an unsupported function key, the system displays an error message and refreshes the screen without making any changes to the displayed data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
6: Invalid Key Handling
Display 'Invalid key' message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the User List screen
acceptance_criteria.When: A key other than ENTER, PF3, PF7, or PF8 is pressed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error flag is set to 'Y', the cursor is positioned at the User ID input field, the message 'Invalid key pressed' (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) is displayed on the screen, and the screen is refreshed without erasing existing content

rules.rule_name: Navigation to Admin Menu
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF3, the system transfers control to the Administration Menu program, passing the current session context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
7: Navigation to Admin Menu
Transfer to COADM01C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing the User List screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF3
acceptance_criteria.Then: The target program is set to the Administration Menu (COADM01C), the current transaction ID and program name are recorded in the communication area, and control is immediately transferred to the Administration Menu with the full session context

rules.rule_name: User Selection Detection
rules.rule_description: When the user presses ENTER, the system scans all 10 displayed user rows in order (row 1 through row 10) to find the first row where a selection code has been entered.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
8: User Selection Detection
Scan all 10 rows for selection code

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the User List screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system scans selection fields for rows 1 through 10 sequentially
acceptance_criteria.Then: The first row (lowest row number) whose selection field is not blank and not low-values is identified; the selection code from that row is captured into the user selection flag, and the User ID from that same row is captured as the selected user; if no row has a selection code entered, both the selection flag and selected user ID are cleared to spaces

rules.rule_name: Navigate to Update User
rules.rule_description: When the user enters 'U' or 'u' as the selection code next to a user, the system transfers control to the Update User program with the selected user's ID.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
9: Navigate to Update User
Transfer to COUSR02C with User ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a selection code on the User List screen and pressed ENTER
acceptance_criteria.When: The selection code is 'U' or 'u' and a valid User ID is associated with the selected row
acceptance_criteria.Then: The target program is set to the Update User screen (COUSR02C), the current transaction ID is recorded as the originating transaction, the current program name is recorded as the originating program, the program context is set to 0, and control is immediately transferred to COUSR02C with the full session context including the selected User ID

rules.rule_name: Navigate to Delete User
rules.rule_description: When the user enters 'D' or 'd' as the selection code next to a user, the system transfers control to the Delete User program with the selected user's ID.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
10: Navigate to Delete User
Transfer to COUSR03C with User ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a selection code on the User List screen and pressed ENTER
acceptance_criteria.When: The selection code is 'D' or 'd' and a valid User ID is associated with the selected row
acceptance_criteria.Then: The target program is set to the Delete User screen (COUSR03C), the current transaction ID is recorded as the originating transaction, the current program name is recorded as the originating program, the program context is set to 0, and control is immediately transferred to COUSR03C with the full session context including the selected User ID

rules.rule_name: Invalid Selection Validation
rules.rule_description: When the user enters a selection code that is not 'U', 'u', 'D', or 'd', the system displays an error message indicating the valid selection values.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
11: Invalid Selection Validation
Display 'Invalid selection' message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered a selection code on the User List screen and pressed ENTER
acceptance_criteria.When: The selection code entered is not 'U', 'u', 'D', or 'd' (i.e., any other non-blank, non-low-value character)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error message 'Invalid selection. Valid values are U and D' is displayed on the screen, the cursor is positioned at the User ID input field, and no navigation to another program occurs

rules.rule_name: User ID Search Criteria Handling
rules.rule_description: After processing any user selection, the system captures the User ID search field value to determine the starting point for loading the user list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
12: User ID Search Criteria Handling
Capture search field value

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the User List screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the User ID search input field
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the User ID search field is blank or low-values, the browse start key is set to low-values (beginning of the user directory); if the User ID search field contains a value, that value is used as the browse start key to position the list at that specific user

rules.rule_name: Page Forward Navigation via Enter Key
rules.rule_description: When the user presses ENTER, the page counter is reset to zero before loading the first page of results based on the search criteria entered.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
13: Page Forward Navigation Enter Key
Reset page number, load next page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the User List screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to load the user list
acceptance_criteria.Then: The page number counter is reset to 0, and forward page loading is performed starting from the User ID search key position, effectively loading the first page of results matching the search criteria

rules.rule_name: Page Backward Navigation Guard
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF7 to go to the previous page, the system checks whether the user is already on the first page before attempting backward navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
14: Page Backward Navigation PF7
Page number greater than 1?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF7 on the User List screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the current page number
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the current page number is greater than 1, backward page loading is performed using the first User ID on the current page as the browse start key; if the current page number is 1 or less, the message 'You are already at the top of the page...' is displayed and the screen is refreshed without changing the displayed data

rules.rule_name: Page Forward Navigation Guard
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF8 to go to the next page, the system checks whether additional pages of users exist before attempting forward navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
15: Page Forward Navigation PF8
Next page exists?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF8 on the User List screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the next-page availability indicator
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the next-page indicator is set to YES (more records exist beyond the current page), forward page loading is performed using the last User ID on the current page as the browse start key; if the next-page indicator is set to NO, the message 'You are already at the bottom of the page...' is displayed and the screen is refreshed without changing the displayed data

rules.rule_name: Forward Page Data Loading
rules.rule_description: The system reads up to 10 user records forward from the User Security file starting at the specified browse key position to populate the current page of the user list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
16: Forward Page Data Loading
Read next page of records

acceptance_criteria.Given: A forward page load has been triggered (by ENTER or PF8)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system browses the User Security file starting from the specified User ID key position
acceptance_criteria.Then: The browse is opened at the specified start key; if the trigger was not ENTER, PF7, or PF3, one record is skipped forward before reading; all 10 display rows are cleared; up to 10 user records are read sequentially forward from the User Security file; each record's User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type are populated into the corresponding screen row; after filling rows, one additional record read is attempted to determine if more pages exist; the browse is then closed

rules.rule_name: Backward Page Data Loading
rules.rule_description: The system reads up to 10 user records backward from the User Security file starting at the specified browse key position to populate the previous page of the user list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
17: Backward Page Data Loading
Read records in reverse order

acceptance_criteria.Given: A backward page load has been triggered (by PF7) and the current page number is greater than 1
acceptance_criteria.When: The system browses the User Security file backward starting from the first User ID on the current page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The browse is opened at the first User ID of the current page; if the trigger was not ENTER or PF8, one record is skipped backward before reading; all 10 display rows are cleared; up to 10 user records are read sequentially backward from the User Security file; each record's User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type are populated into screen rows filling from row 10 down to row 1 (reverse order); after filling rows, one additional record read backward is attempted to determine page number adjustment; the browse is then closed

rules.rule_name: Screen Row Initialization
rules.rule_description: Before populating the user list with new data, all 10 display rows are cleared to spaces to prevent stale data from a previous page from remaining visible.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
18: Screen Row Initialization
Clear all 10 user rows

acceptance_criteria.Given: A page load (forward or backward) is about to populate the screen with user records
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initializes the display rows prior to reading records
acceptance_criteria.Then: For each of the 10 display rows (rows 1 through 10), the User ID field, First Name field, Last Name field, and User Type field are all set to spaces, ensuring no residual data from a previous page remains on the screen

rules.rule_name: User Record Population
rules.rule_description: Each user record read from the User Security file is mapped to the corresponding display row on the screen, showing the user's ID, first name, last name, and user type.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
19: User Record Population
Fill rows with user data

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully read from the User Security file during a page load
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the screen row corresponding to the current row index (1 through 10)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID from the record is placed in the User ID field of the corresponding row; the First Name from the record is placed in the First Name field; the Last Name from the record is placed in the Last Name field; the User Type from the record is placed in the User Type field; if the row index does not match 1 through 10, no action is taken

rules.rule_name: Page Number Tracking
rules.rule_description: The system maintains an accurate page number counter that is incremented during forward navigation and decremented during backward navigation, and displays it on the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
20: Page Number Tracking
Update and display page number

acceptance_criteria.Given: A page load (forward or backward) has completed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system updates the page number after loading records
acceptance_criteria.Then: For forward navigation: the page number is incremented by 1 if at least one record was read (index greater than 1); for backward navigation: if more records exist before the current page and the page number is greater than 1, the page number is decremented by 1, otherwise the page number is set to 1; the updated page number is then displayed in the page number field on the screen

rules.rule_name: Next Page Availability Indicator
rules.rule_description: After loading a full page of 10 users, the system attempts to read one additional record to determine whether a next page of users is available, controlling whether PF8 navigation is permitted.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
21: Next Page Availability Indicator
Check if more records exist

acceptance_criteria.Given: A forward page load has completed reading up to 10 user records
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to read one additional record beyond the 10 displayed
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the additional record read is successful (more users exist in the file), the next-page indicator is set to YES, enabling PF8 forward navigation; if the additional record read reaches end-of-file (no more users exist), the next-page indicator is set to NO, disabling PF8 forward navigation; if fewer than 10 records were read (end-of-file reached during the main read loop), the next-page indicator is also set to NO

rules.rule_name: First and Last User ID Tracking
rules.rule_description: The system records the User ID of the first and last users displayed on the current page to serve as anchor points for subsequent forward and backward page navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
22: First and Last User ID Tracking
Store first and last user IDs

acceptance_criteria.Given: User records are being populated into the display rows during a page load
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates row 1 and row 10 of the display
acceptance_criteria.Then: When row 1 is populated, the User ID of that record is saved as the 'first user on page' anchor value in the communication area; when row 10 is populated, the User ID of that record is saved as the 'last user on page' anchor value in the communication area; these anchor values are used as browse start keys for PF7 (backward) and PF8 (forward) navigation respectively

rules.rule_name: Screen Header Population
rules.rule_description: Before sending the User List screen to the terminal, the system populates the screen header with current application context information including titles, transaction details, and the current date and time.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
23: Screen Header Population
Populate title, date, time, program info

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is about to be sent to the terminal
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the screen header fields
acceptance_criteria.Then: The first application title (CCDA-TITLE01) is placed in the title 1 field; the second application title (CCDA-TITLE02) is placed in the title 2 field; the current transaction ID is placed in the transaction name field; the current program name is placed in the program name field; the current date is formatted as MM/DD/YY and placed in the date field; the current time is formatted as HH:MM:SS and placed in the time field

rules.rule_name: User List Screen Display
rules.rule_description: The system sends the fully populated User List screen to the user's terminal, with the display mode (full erase or overlay) determined by the screen erase flag.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
24: User List Screen Display
Send populated screen to terminal

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen header has been populated and the user list data is ready for display
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the User List screen to the terminal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current message (error or informational) is placed in the screen message field; if the screen erase flag is set to YES, the screen is sent with a full terminal erase (clearing any previous content) and the cursor is positioned; if the screen erase flag is set to NO, the screen is sent as an overlay without erasing existing terminal content, with the cursor positioned

rules.rule_name: Session State Preservation
rules.rule_description: At the end of each program execution cycle, the system returns control to CICS while preserving the complete session state in the communication area so that the next user interaction can resume from the correct context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
27: Session State Preservation
Return control with updated comm area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has completed processing the current user interaction
acceptance_criteria.When: The program returns control to CICS
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control is returned to CICS with the current transaction ID specified for the next invocation, and the full communication area (containing page number, first/last user IDs on page, selected user, re-entry flag, next-page indicator, and all other session state) is passed back to CICS to be available on the next user interaction

key_functionalities.title: Program Initialization
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Program Initialization])
    B[Turn OFF Error Flag\nNo errors at start]
    C[Set File Status to\nNot End-of-File\nRecords available to read]
    D[Set Next Page Flag to NO\nNo additional pages assumed initially]
    E[Set Screen Erase Flag to YES\nScreen will be fully refreshed]
    F[Clear General Message Field\nNo messages to display]
    G[Clear Error Message Field\nNo error messages to display]
    H[Set User ID Search Field\nto default entry position]
    I([Initialization Complete\nReady for Session Validation])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G
    G --> H
    H --> I

rules.rule_name: Initialize Error Flag to No-Error State
rules.rule_description: At the start of every program execution cycle, the error flag must be set to OFF to ensure no residual error state from a previous interaction affects the current session processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Turn OFF Error Flag
No errors at start

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List Management program begins a new execution cycle
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initializes its processing environment
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error flag must be set to OFF, indicating no errors are present and all subsequent processing should proceed normally without any pre-existing error condition

rules.rule_name: Initialize User Security File Status to Records Available
rules.rule_description: At the start of every program execution cycle, the User Security file read status must be set to 'Not End-of-File' to indicate that user records are available for retrieval and display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set File Status to
Not End-of-File
Records available to read

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List Management program begins a new execution cycle
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initializes its processing environment
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User Security file status must be set to 'Not End-of-File', signaling that user records are available to be read and displayed on the User List screen

rules.rule_name: Initialize Next Page Availability Flag to No Additional Pages
rules.rule_description: At the start of every program execution cycle, the next-page availability flag must be set to NO, meaning the system assumes by default that no additional pages of user records exist beyond the current view until confirmed otherwise during data retrieval.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Next Page Flag to NO
No additional pages assumed initially

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List Management program begins a new execution cycle
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initializes its processing environment
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next-page flag must be set to NO, indicating that no further pages of user records are assumed to be available until the data retrieval process confirms additional records exist

rules.rule_name: Initialize Screen Refresh Mode to Full Erase
rules.rule_description: At the start of every program execution cycle, the screen erase flag must be set to YES so that when the User List screen is sent to the user, the entire screen is fully cleared and redrawn, preventing any stale data from a previous display from remaining visible.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Screen Erase Flag to YES
Screen will be fully refreshed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List Management program begins a new execution cycle
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initializes its processing environment
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen erase flag must be set to YES, ensuring the User List screen will be fully erased and refreshed when displayed, so no residual data from a prior screen interaction remains visible to the user

rules.rule_name: Clear General Message Field at Program Start
rules.rule_description: At the start of every program execution cycle, the general message field must be cleared to spaces so that no informational or status message from a prior interaction is inadvertently displayed to the user during the current session.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Clear General Message Field
No messages to display

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List Management program begins a new execution cycle
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initializes its processing environment
acceptance_criteria.Then: The general message field (WS-MESSAGE) must be set to spaces, ensuring no leftover message from a previous user interaction is carried forward and displayed on the current screen

rules.rule_name: Clear Error Message Display Field at Program Start
rules.rule_description: At the start of every program execution cycle, the error message display field on the User List screen must be cleared to spaces so that no error message from a prior interaction is shown to the user at the beginning of the current processing cycle.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Clear Error Message Field
No error messages to display

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List Management program begins a new execution cycle
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initializes its processing environment
acceptance_criteria.Then: The error message output field (ERRMSGO) on the User List screen must be set to spaces, ensuring no prior error message is visible to the user when the screen is rendered in the current cycle

rules.rule_name: Set User ID Search Field to Default Entry Position
rules.rule_description: At the start of every program execution cycle, the User ID input field on the User List screen must be set to its default cursor entry position, directing the user's cursor to the User ID search field as the primary input point for filtering or searching users.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set User ID Search Field
to default entry position

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List Management program begins a new execution cycle
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initializes its processing environment
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID input field length indicator (USRIDINL) must be set to -1, positioning the screen cursor at the User ID search field so the user can immediately begin entering a User ID to search or filter the user list

key_functionalities.title: Session Validation
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start Session Validation])
    B{Does a valid user\nsession exist?}
    C[Set destination\nto Sign-On Screen\nCOSGN00C]
    D[Redirect user to\nSign-On Screen]
    E([Proceed to\nProgram Processing])

    A --> B
    B -->|No Active Session| C
    C --> D
    D --> ([End])
    B -->|Active Session Exists| E

rules.rule_name: Detect Missing User Session and Set Sign-On Destination
rules.rule_description: When the User List screen is invoked, the system checks whether an active user session exists by verifying the presence of a communication area. If no session is found, the system designates the Sign-On screen as the redirect destination before transferring control.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Does a valid user session exist?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the User List screen and no active session communication area is present (communication area length equals zero)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether a valid session context exists
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) and initiates a redirect to that screen, ending the current program execution

rules.rule_name: Load Active Session Data When Valid Session Exists
rules.rule_description: When a valid user session is detected (communication area is present), the system loads the session context data from the communication area to enable further processing of the User List screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Active Session Exists

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user accesses the User List screen and an active session communication area exists (communication area length is greater than zero)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system confirms the presence of a valid session
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system loads the full session context (including program state, navigation flags, selected user details, and page information) from the communication area into the working session data, and proceeds to program processing

rules.rule_name: Redirect User to Sign-On Screen When No Session Exists
rules.rule_description: When no active session exists, the system transfers control to the Sign-On screen. If no destination program has been explicitly set, the system defaults the destination to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) before redirecting. The current program's transaction ID and program name are recorded as the originating context before the transfer.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Redirect user to Sign-On Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined that no valid user session exists and the destination program has been set to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C); additionally, if the destination program is blank or unset at the time of redirect, it defaults to COSGN00C
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the redirect to the previous or designated screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the current transaction ID as the originating transaction, records the current program name as the originating program, resets the program context to zero, and transfers full control to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) passing the current session communication area, terminating execution of the User List program

key_functionalities.title: First
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([First-Time Screen Display Start])
    B[Mark Program as Re-Entered\nSo next interaction is treated as a return visit]
    C[Clear Screen Output Area\nReset all screen fields to empty]
    D[Set User ID Search to Beginning\nNo search criteria - start from first user]
    E[Reset Page Number to Zero]
    F[Open Browse on User Security File\nStarting from the very first user record]
    G[Clear All 10 User Rows on Screen\nRemove any previous data]
    H[Read Up to 10 User Records\nSequentially from the beginning]
    I[Populate Screen Rows\nFill each row with User ID, First Name,\nLast Name, and User Type]
    J[Track First and Last User ID\nStore for future page navigation]
    K[Check if More Records Exist\nRead one extra record to detect next page]
    L[Set Page Number to 1\nIncrement from zero after loading]
    M[Populate Screen Header\nApplication title, date, time, program name]
    N[Display User List Screen\nShow first page of users to the user]
    O([First-Time Screen Display End])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G
    G --> H
    H --> I
    I --> J
    J --> K
    K --> L
    L --> M
    M --> N
    N --> O

rules.rule_name: Mark Program as Re-Entered on First Visit
rules.rule_description: On the very first time a user enters the User List screen, the program must mark itself as re-entered so that any subsequent interaction by the same user is treated as a return visit rather than a fresh launch, and the screen output area is fully cleared to remove any residual data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Mark Program as Re-Entered
So next interaction is treated as a return visit

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is being accessed for the first time within the current session (the program has not yet been marked as re-entered)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initializes the first-time screen display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The program must be flagged as re-entered (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER = TRUE) so that all future interactions within this session are treated as return visits, AND the entire screen output area (COUSR0AO) must be reset to LOW-VALUES to ensure no stale data is displayed

rules.rule_name: Set User ID Search Starting Point to Beginning of User Directory
rules.rule_description: When loading the user list for the first time, if no User ID search value has been entered by the user, the browse must start from the very beginning of the User Security file. If a User ID has been entered, that value is used as the starting point for the browse.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set User ID Search to Beginning
No search criteria - start from first user

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is being loaded for the first time and the User ID input field (USRIDINI) on the screen is either blank (SPACES) or empty (LOW-VALUES)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines the starting point for browsing the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The search key (SEC-USR-ID) must be set to LOW-VALUES so that the browse begins from the very first record in the User Security file; if the User ID input field contains a value, that value must be moved to SEC-USR-ID to start the browse from that specific user

rules.rule_name: Reset Page Number to Zero Before Loading First Page
rules.rule_description: Before loading the first page of users, the page counter must be reset to zero so that after the first page is successfully loaded, the page number is correctly incremented to 1.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reset Page Number to Zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is being loaded for the first time and the page forward process is about to begin
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to load the first page of users
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) must be set to 0 so that after the first page load increments it, the displayed page number correctly shows 1

rules.rule_name: Open Browse on User Security File from Starting Position
rules.rule_description: To retrieve the list of users, the system must open a sequential browse on the User Security file starting from the determined search key position. This establishes the read cursor for subsequent sequential reads of user records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Open Browse on User Security File
Starting from the very first user record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The search starting key (SEC-USR-ID) has been set to either LOW-VALUES (start of file) or a specific User ID value
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initiates the user list retrieval process
acceptance_criteria.Then: A browse must be opened on the User Security file (WS-USRSEC-FILE) positioned at the record matching or immediately following the SEC-USR-ID key, enabling sequential forward reading of user records from that position

rules.rule_name: Clear All 10 User Display Rows Before Populating New Data
rules.rule_description: Before populating the screen with newly retrieved user records, all 10 display rows must be cleared to spaces to ensure no stale or residual user data from a previous page is visible on the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Clear All 10 User Rows on Screen
Remove any previous data

acceptance_criteria.Given: The browse on the User Security file has been successfully opened and the system is about to populate the screen with user records
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the screen rows for new data
acceptance_criteria.Then: All 10 user display rows (rows 1 through 10) must have their User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type fields set to SPACES, ensuring a clean slate before new user data is loaded

rules.rule_name: Read Up to 10 User Records Sequentially for Display
rules.rule_description: The system reads user records one at a time from the User Security file in forward sequence, populating each screen row in order, until either 10 rows are filled, the end of the file is reached, or an error occurs.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Read Up to 10 User Records
Sequentially from the beginning

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User Security file browse is open, all 10 screen rows have been cleared, and the row index (WS-IDX) is set to 1
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sequentially reads user records from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must read the next user record and populate the corresponding screen row, then increment the row index by 1; this process must continue until the row index reaches 11 (10 rows filled), the end of the User Security file is reached, or a retrieval error occurs — whichever happens first

rules.rule_name: Populate Each Screen Row with User Details
rules.rule_description: For each user record successfully read from the User Security file, the system maps the user's details — User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type — to the corresponding screen display row (1 through 10).
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Populate Screen Rows
Fill each row with User ID, First Name,
Last Name, and User Type

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully read from the User Security file and the current row index (WS-IDX) is between 1 and 10
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the screen row corresponding to the current row index
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID (SEC-USR-ID) must be moved to the User ID display field of the matching row (USRID01I through USRID10I); the First Name (SEC-USR-FNAME) must be moved to the First Name field (FNAME01I through FNAME10I); the Last Name (SEC-USR-LNAME) must be moved to the Last Name field (LNAME01I through LNAME10I); and the User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE) must be moved to the User Type field (UTYPE01I through UTYPE10I) of the corresponding row

rules.rule_name: Track First and Last User ID on Current Page for Navigation
rules.rule_description: To support accurate forward and backward page navigation, the system must record the User ID of the first user displayed (row 1) and the User ID of the last user displayed (row 10) on the current page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Track First and Last User ID
Store for future page navigation

acceptance_criteria.Given: User records are being populated into the screen rows
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates row 1 or row 10 with a user record
acceptance_criteria.Then: When populating row 1, the User ID (SEC-USR-ID) must also be saved to CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST to mark the first user on the current page; when populating row 10, the User ID (SEC-USR-ID) must also be saved to CDEMO-CU00-USRID-LAST to mark the last user on the current page — these values are used as anchors for subsequent page forward and backward navigation

rules.rule_name: Detect Whether Additional Pages of Users Exist
rules.rule_description: After filling up to 10 rows, the system attempts to read one additional record beyond the current page to determine whether more users exist. This controls whether the PF8 (next page) navigation option is available to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Check if More Records Exist
Read one extra record to detect next page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has finished reading up to 10 user records and populating the screen rows
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks for the existence of additional user records beyond the current page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must attempt to read one more record from the User Security file; if the read is successful and the record exists (USER-SEC-NOT-EOF is TRUE and no error), the next-page indicator (NEXT-PAGE) must be set to YES, indicating more pages are available; if the read returns end-of-file or an error, the next-page indicator must be set to NO, indicating the current page is the last page

rules.rule_name: Increment Page Number After Successfully Loading a Page
rules.rule_description: After successfully loading user records onto the screen, the page number counter is incremented by 1. Since the counter starts at 0 before the first page load, this results in the page number being set to 1 after the first page is displayed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Page Number to 1
Increment from zero after loading

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed reading user records for the current page (at least one record was read, WS-IDX is greater than 1) and the page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) was initialized to 0 before the first load
acceptance_criteria.When: The system finalizes the page load after reading records
acceptance_criteria.Then: The page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) must be incremented by 1 (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM = CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM + 1), resulting in a page number of 1 for the first page load, and the updated page number must be moved to the page number display field (PAGENUMI) on the screen

rules.rule_name: Display User List Screen with Full Screen Refresh
rules.rule_description: After all user data and header information have been prepared, the User List screen is sent to the user with a full erase to ensure a clean display of the first page of users.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Display User List Screen
Show first page of users to the user

acceptance_criteria.Given: All 10 screen rows have been populated with user data (or cleared if fewer than 10 users exist), the page number has been set, and the screen header has been populated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the User List screen to the user for the first-time display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen must be sent using the COUSR0A map from the COUSR00 mapset with the ERASE option active (SEND-ERASE-YES = TRUE), ensuring the entire screen is refreshed; any informational or error message stored in WS-MESSAGE must be displayed in the error message field (ERRMSGO) on the screen

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Header with Application and Session Information
rules.rule_description: Before displaying the User List screen, the screen header must be populated with the application titles, the current transaction ID, the current program name, the current date formatted as MM/DD/YY, and the current time formatted as HH:MM:SS.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Populate Screen Header
Application title, date, time, program name

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is about to send the User List screen to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen header information is being prepared
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen header must be populated with: the application title line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) in TITLE01O, the application title line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) in TITLE02O, the current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) in TRNNAMEO, the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) in PGMNAMEO, the current date formatted as MM/DD/YY (derived from the system date) in CURDATEO, and the current time formatted as HH:MM:SS (derived from the system time) in CURTIMEO

key_functionalities.title: User Input Reception
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([User Interacts with User List Screen])
    B[User May Enter a Selection Code\n next to one or more listed users\n Valid values: U = Update, D = Delete]
    C[User May Enter a User ID\nin the Search Field\nto filter the list]
    D[User Presses a Function Key\nEnter, PF3, PF7, PF8, or Other]
    E[System Captures All Screen Input\n- Selection flags for up to 10 rows\n- User ID per each listed row\n- User ID search criteria\n- Function key pressed]
    F([Route to Appropriate Processing\nbased on Key Pressed])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F

rules.rule_name: Capture All User List Screen Input
rules.rule_description: When the user submits the User List screen, the system must capture all input fields including selection codes entered next to any of the 10 listed users, the User ID associated with each listed row, any User ID entered in the search field, and the function key pressed by the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
System Captures All Screen Input
- Selection flags for up to 10 rows
- User ID per each listed row
- User ID search criteria
- Function key pressed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen and has previously visited it at least once (the screen is in re-entry mode)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user submits the screen by pressing any key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system captures all screen input into the internal input map (COUSR0AI), including: selection flag fields for all 10 user rows (SEL0001I through SEL0010I), the User ID displayed on each of the 10 rows (USRID01I through USRID10I), the User ID entered in the search/filter field (USRIDINI), and the identity of the function key pressed (EIBAID)

rules.rule_name: User Enters Selection Code Next to a Listed User
rules.rule_description: The user may enter a selection action code in the selection field next to any of the 10 displayed users. The system scans rows 1 through 10 in order and processes only the first row where a non-blank, non-empty selection code is found. The selected action code and the corresponding User ID are captured for subsequent processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
User May Enter a Selection Code
 next to one or more listed users
 Valid values: U = Update, D = Delete

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is displaying up to 10 users and the user has entered a selection code in one or more selection fields
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the Enter key action and evaluates the selection fields
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system scans selection fields SEL0001I through SEL0010I in sequential order (row 1 first, row 10 last); the first selection field that is not blank and not empty is identified; the selection action code from that field is stored as the User Selection Flag (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG); the User ID from the corresponding row (USRID01I through USRID10I) is stored as the Selected User (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED); all subsequent selection fields are ignored; if no selection field contains a value, both the User Selection Flag and Selected User are set to spaces

rules.rule_name: First Non-Blank Selection Takes Priority
rules.rule_description: If the user enters selection codes next to multiple users on the same screen, only the selection code on the lowest-numbered row (closest to row 1) is acted upon. All other selection entries are disregarded.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
User May Enter a Selection Code
 next to one or more listed users
 Valid values: U = Update, D = Delete

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is displayed with up to 10 user rows and the user has entered selection codes next to more than one user
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the selection fields upon pressing Enter
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system processes only the first row (lowest row number from 1 to 10) where the selection field is not blank and not empty; the selection code and User ID from that row are captured; selection codes entered on any other rows are ignored entirely

rules.rule_name: User Enters User ID in Search Field to Filter List
rules.rule_description: The user may type a User ID in the search field to start the displayed list from that specific user. If the search field is left blank or empty, the system starts the list from the very beginning of the user directory.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
User May Enter a User ID
in the Search Field
to filter the list

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen and the search field (USRIDINI) is available for input
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses Enter and the system processes the search criteria
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the User ID search field (USRIDINI) contains a value that is not blank and not empty, that value is used as the starting point (SEC-USR-ID) for browsing the user directory; if the User ID search field is blank or empty, the browse starting point (SEC-USR-ID) is set to LOW-VALUES, causing the list to start from the very first user in the directory

rules.rule_name: Route Processing Based on Function Key Pressed
rules.rule_description: After capturing screen input, the system determines which processing path to follow based on the function key the user pressed. Each supported key triggers a distinct business operation, and any unsupported key results in an error message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Route to Appropriate Processing
based on Key Pressed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the User List screen and all input has been captured
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the function key pressed (EIBAID)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the user pressed Enter, the system performs user selection and list search processing (PROCESS-ENTER-KEY); if the user pressed PF3, the system navigates back to the Administration Menu (COADM01C); if the user pressed PF7, the system performs backward page navigation (PROCESS-PF7-KEY); if the user pressed PF8, the system performs forward page navigation (PROCESS-PF8-KEY); if the user pressed any other key, the system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets cursor focus to the User ID input field, displays the invalid key error message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY), and refreshes the User List screen without changing any data

rules.rule_name: Invalid Function Key Pressed on User List Screen
rules.rule_description: Only the function keys Enter, PF3, PF7, and PF8 are valid on the User List screen. If the user presses any other key, the system displays an error message and refreshes the screen without performing any data changes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
User Presses a Function Key
Enter, PF3, PF7, PF8, or Other

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses a function key that is not Enter, PF3, PF7, or PF8
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error indicator to 'Y' (WS-ERR-FLG), positions the cursor on the User ID input field (USRIDINL set to -1), displays the standard invalid key error message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) in the message area of the screen, and re-displays the User List screen with the existing data unchanged

rules.rule_name: Screen Input Reception Only on Re-Entry
rules.rule_description: The system only receives and processes screen input from the user on subsequent visits to the User List screen. On the very first visit, the screen is initialized and displayed without reading any user input.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
System Captures All Screen Input
- Selection flags for up to 10 rows
- User ID per each listed row
- User ID search criteria
- Function key pressed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has navigated to the User List screen with a valid session
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether this is the first visit or a return visit to the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: If this is the first visit (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is not set), the system marks the screen as re-enterable, clears the screen output area, and directly loads and displays the user list without receiving any screen input; if this is a return visit (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is already set), the system receives the screen input from the user before proceeding to evaluate the function key and process the request

key_functionalities.title: Function Key Routing
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([User Submits Input on User List Screen])
    B{Which Function Key\nWas Pressed?}
    C[Process User Selections\nand Page Navigation\nEnter Key Logic]
    D[Return to\nAdministration Menu\nCOADM01C]
    E[Navigate to\nPrevious Page\nPF7 Logic]
    F[Navigate to\nNext Page\nPF8 Logic]
    G[Display Error Message\n'Invalid Key']
    H([Continue Processing])

    A --> B
    B -->|Enter Key| C
    B -->|PF3 - Back| D
    B -->|PF7 - Page Up| E
    B -->|PF8 - Page Down| F
    B -->|Any Other Key| G
    C --> H
    D --> H
    E --> H
    F --> H
    G --> H

rules.rule_name: Route Enter Key Press to User Selection and Page Navigation Processing
rules.rule_description: When the user presses the Enter key on the User List screen, the system routes processing to the Enter Key logic which handles user row selections and page navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Process User Selections and Page Navigation Enter Key Logic

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen and has an active session with a valid communication area loaded
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the Enter key to submit their input
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system routes control to the Enter Key processing logic (PROCESS-ENTER-KEY) which evaluates any user row selections made and performs page navigation accordingly

rules.rule_name: Route PF3 Key Press to Return to Administration Menu
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF3 on the User List screen, the system navigates back to the Administration Menu program (COADM01C), passing the current session context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Return to Administration Menu COADM01C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen and has an active session with a valid communication area loaded
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the target program to 'COADM01C', records the current transaction ID and program name as the originating context, resets the program context to zero, and transfers control to the Administration Menu program (COADM01C) passing the full session communication area

rules.rule_name: Route PF7 Key Press to Previous Page Navigation Logic
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF7 on the User List screen, the system routes processing to the previous page navigation logic to display the prior set of users.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Navigate to Previous Page PF7 Logic

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen and has an active session with a valid communication area loaded
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF7 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system routes control to the PF7 key processing logic (PROCESS-PF7-KEY) which handles backward page navigation through the user list

rules.rule_name: Route PF8 Key Press to Next Page Navigation Logic
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF8 on the User List screen, the system routes processing to the next page navigation logic to display the following set of users.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Navigate to Next Page PF8 Logic

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen and has an active session with a valid communication area loaded
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF8 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system routes control to the PF8 key processing logic (PROCESS-PF8-KEY) which handles forward page navigation through the user list

rules.rule_name: Display Invalid Key Error for Unsupported Function Key Press
rules.rule_description: When the user presses any function key other than Enter, PF3, PF7, or PF8 on the User List screen, the system displays an invalid key error message and refreshes the screen without making any changes to the displayed data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Error Message 'Invalid Key'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen and has an active session with a valid communication area loaded
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses any key that is not Enter, PF3, PF7, or PF8
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', positions the cursor on the User ID input field, displays the standard invalid key error message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) in the screen error message area, and refreshes the User List screen showing the error message without altering any user data currently displayed

key_functionalities.title: Invalid Key Handling
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([User Presses a Key])
    B{Is the key a\nsupported function key?\nEnter, PF3, PF7, PF8}
    C[Set Error Flag ON]
    D[Set Message to 'Invalid key']
    E[Display User List Screen\nwith Error Message]
    F([Wait for Next User Input])

    A --> B
    B -->|No - Unsupported Key| C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    B -->|Yes - Supported Key| F

rules.rule_name: Supported Function Key Identification for User List Screen
rules.rule_description: Defines which keyboard function keys are valid and accepted on the User List screen. Only Enter, PF3, PF7, and PF8 are recognized as supported actions. Any other key press is treated as invalid.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is the key a supported function key? Enter, PF3, PF7, PF8

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen and has already interacted with it at least once (screen is in re-entry mode)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses any keyboard key to submit an action
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system evaluates the key pressed and routes to the appropriate action only if it is one of the four supported keys: Enter (submit/search), PF3 (return to Admin Menu), PF7 (page backward), or PF8 (page forward). Any other key is considered unsupported and triggers the invalid key handling process.

rules.rule_name: Error Flag Activation on Invalid Key Press
rules.rule_description: When a user presses an unsupported key on the User List screen, the system activates the error flag to indicate that an invalid action was attempted. This flag signals that the current interaction contains an error that must be communicated back to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Error Flag ON

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen in re-entry mode
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses a key that is not Enter, PF3, PF7, or PF8
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y' (ON), marking the current interaction as erroneous so that subsequent screen display logic is aware an error condition exists

rules.rule_name: Invalid Key Error Message Assignment
rules.rule_description: When an unsupported key is pressed on the User List screen, the system assigns the standard invalid key message to the screen message field. This message is sourced from the application's centrally defined message constants (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) to ensure consistent messaging across the application.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Message to 'Invalid key'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen in re-entry mode and the error flag has been set to ON
acceptance_criteria.When: The user has pressed a key that is not one of the supported keys (Enter, PF3, PF7, PF8)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system assigns the standard application-defined invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) to the screen message field (WS-MESSAGE), which will be displayed to the user as feedback

rules.rule_name: User List Screen Redisplay with Invalid Key Error
rules.rule_description: After detecting an invalid key press and setting the error message, the system redisplays the User List screen to the user with the error message visible. The screen is sent with the cursor positioned at the User ID input field, and the existing user list data remains intact so the user can correct their action without losing context.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display User List Screen with Error Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen, the error flag is set to ON, and the invalid key error message has been assigned to the message field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the User List screen after an invalid key press
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the User List screen with: (1) the invalid key error message shown in the error message area, (2) the cursor positioned at the User ID input field, (3) the screen header populated with current application titles, transaction ID, program name, current date in MM/DD/YY format, and current time in HH:MM:SS format, and (4) the existing user list data preserved so the user can see the current page and make a valid selection or key press

key_functionalities.title: Navigation to Admin Menu
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([User Presses PF3])
    B[Set Destination as\nAdministration Menu\nCOADM01C]
    C{Destination\nProgram Valid?}
    D[Default to\nSign-On Screen\nCOSGN00C]
    E[Record Current Program\nand Transaction Details]
    F([Transfer Control to\nAdministration Menu])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C -->|Destination is Blank| D
    C -->|Destination is Valid| E
    D --> E
    E --> F

rules.rule_name: Set Destination to Administration Menu on PF3
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF3 on the User List screen, the system designates the Administration Menu (COADM01C) as the target destination for navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Destination as Administration Menu COADM01C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen with an active session
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Administration Menu screen identified as COADM01C and initiates the return-to-previous-screen navigation process

rules.rule_name: Default Navigation Target to Sign-On Screen When Destination is Blank
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control, the system validates that a destination program has been set. If the destination is blank or uninitialized, the system defaults the navigation target to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) to ensure the user is always directed to a valid screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Default to Sign-On Screen COSGN00C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The navigation process has been initiated and the destination program field is being evaluated
acceptance_criteria.When: The destination program value is blank (spaces) or uninitialized (low-values)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system overrides the destination and sets it to the Sign-On screen identified as COSGN00C, ensuring no navigation occurs to an undefined screen

rules.rule_name: Record Current Program and Transaction Context Before Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to another screen, the system captures and stores the current transaction identifier, current program name, and resets the program context to zero. This information is passed via the communication area so the destination screen knows where the user navigated from.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record Current Program and Transaction Details

acceptance_criteria.Given: The destination program has been validated and is ready for navigation
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is preparing to transfer control to the destination screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the current transaction ID into the 'from transaction' field, records the current program name into the 'from program' field, and sets the program context to zero — all stored in the shared communication area for use by the destination screen

rules.rule_name: Transfer Control to Administration Menu
rules.rule_description: After recording the navigation context, the system transfers full control to the designated destination program (Administration Menu COADM01C or defaulted Sign-On screen COSGN00C), passing the complete session communication area so the destination screen has access to all current session data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer Control to Administration Menu

acceptance_criteria.Given: The destination program has been set (either COADM01C or defaulted to COSGN00C) and the current program and transaction details have been recorded in the communication area
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the control transfer
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system transfers full control to the destination program and passes the entire session communication area (containing user session data, navigation context, and program details) to the destination screen, terminating execution of the current User List program

key_functionalities.title: User Selection Detection

rules.rule_name: Sequential Row Scan to Detect First User Selection
rules.rule_description: When the Enter key is pressed on the User List screen, the system scans all 10 displayed user rows in order from Row 1 to Row 10. The first row that contains a non-blank, non-empty selection code is captured along with its associated User ID. Only the first such entry is acted upon; all subsequent rows are ignored.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Row 1: Selection code entered? ... Row 10: Selection code entered?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is displayed with up to 10 user rows, and the user has pressed the Enter key
acceptance_criteria.When: The system scans selection fields for rows 1 through 10 sequentially and finds the first row where the selection code is not blank and not empty
acceptance_criteria.Then: The selection code and the User ID from that first non-blank row are captured into the active selection variables; scanning stops at the first match and no further rows are evaluated

rules.rule_name: No Selection Made - Clear Selection Data
rules.rule_description: If the user presses Enter without entering a selection code on any of the 10 displayed rows, the system clears the selection code and selected User ID fields, indicating no user action was requested.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear selection code and User ID - No selection made

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is displayed with up to 10 user rows and the user has pressed the Enter key
acceptance_criteria.When: None of the 10 selection fields (Row 1 through Row 10) contain a non-blank, non-empty value
acceptance_criteria.Then: The selection code field and the selected User ID field are both cleared to spaces, and the system proceeds to the search and page-forward operation without navigating to any user action screen

rules.rule_name: Validate That Both Selection Code and User ID Are Present Before Processing
rules.rule_description: Before processing a user's selection action, the system verifies that both a selection code and a User ID have been successfully captured. If either is missing or blank, the system bypasses the action routing and proceeds directly to the search and page-forward operation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Valid selection code and User ID captured?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed scanning all 10 rows after the Enter key was pressed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the captured selection code is non-blank and non-empty AND the captured User ID is non-blank and non-empty
acceptance_criteria.Then: If both the selection code and User ID are present and non-blank, the system proceeds to evaluate the action code; if either is blank or empty, the system skips action routing and proceeds directly to the search and page-forward operation

rules.rule_name: Navigate to Update User Screen When 'U' is Selected
rules.rule_description: When a user enters 'U' or 'u' as the selection code next to a listed user, the system navigates to the Update User screen, passing the selected User ID and current session context so the administrator can modify that user's details.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: U or u - Navigate to Update User - COUSR02C

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid selection code and User ID have been captured from the User List screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The captured selection code is 'U' (uppercase) or 'u' (lowercase)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the target program to the Update User program (COUSR02C), records the current transaction ID and program name as the originating context, resets the program context to zero, and transfers control to the Update User program with the full session communication area

rules.rule_name: Navigate to Delete User Screen When 'D' is Selected
rules.rule_description: When a user enters 'D' or 'd' as the selection code next to a listed user, the system navigates to the Delete User screen, passing the selected User ID and current session context so the administrator can remove that user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: D or d - Navigate to Delete User - COUSR03C

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid selection code and User ID have been captured from the User List screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The captured selection code is 'D' (uppercase) or 'd' (lowercase)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the target program to the Delete User program (COUSR03C), records the current transaction ID and program name as the originating context, resets the program context to zero, and transfers control to the Delete User program with the full session communication area

rules.rule_name: Reject Invalid Selection Code with Error Message
rules.rule_description: If the user enters a selection code that is neither 'U', 'u', 'D', nor 'd', the system rejects the action and displays an error message informing the user that only 'U' (Update) and 'D' (Delete) are valid selection codes. The system then proceeds to refresh the user list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Other - Display 'Invalid selection. Valid values are U and D'

acceptance_criteria.Given: A valid selection code and User ID have been captured from the User List screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The captured selection code is any value other than 'U', 'u', 'D', or 'd'
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the error message 'Invalid selection. Valid values are U and D' on the screen, does not navigate to any user action screen, and proceeds to the search and page-forward operation to refresh the user list

rules.rule_name: Proceed to User List Search and Page Forward After Selection Processing
rules.rule_description: After completing selection code processing — whether no selection was made, an invalid selection code was entered, or a valid selection was processed but did not result in navigation — the system proceeds to execute the user list search and page-forward operation to display or refresh the user list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Proceed to Search/Page Forward

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Enter key was pressed on the User List screen and selection code processing has completed
acceptance_criteria.When: Either no selection was made across all 10 rows, or an invalid selection code was entered, or the selection processing did not result in navigation to another screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the User ID search key based on the value entered in the User ID search field (using the start of the file if the field is blank), resets the page number to zero, and performs the page-forward operation to load and display the user list

sub_functionalities.title: Valid selection code and User ID captured? → What is the selection code? (U/u → Navigate to Update User COUSR02C, D/d → Navigate to Delete User COUSR03C, Other → Display Invalid Selection message) → Continue to Search/Page Processing
sub_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Enter Key Pressed])
    B{Valid Selection Code\nAND User ID both captured?}
    C{What is the\nSelection Code?}
    D[Navigate to Update User\nProgram: COUSR02C\nPassing Selected User ID]
    E[Navigate to Delete User\nProgram: COUSR03C\nPassing Selected User ID]
    F[Display Error Message\n'Invalid selection.\nValid values are U and D']
    G[Continue to\nSearch / Page Processing]
    H([End - Control Transferred\nto Update User Program])
    I([End - Control Transferred\nto Delete User Program])

    A --> B
    B -->|No - No selection made| G
    B -->|Yes| C
    C -->|U or u| D
    C -->|D or d| E
    C -->|Any Other Value| F
    D --> H
    E --> I
    F --> G

rules.rule_name: Capture First Non-Blank User Selection from List
rules.rule_description: When the user presses Enter on the User List screen, the system scans all 10 displayed user rows in order (row 1 through row 10) and captures the selection code and corresponding User ID from the first row where a non-blank selection code has been entered. If no row has a selection code entered, both the selection flag and selected user ID are cleared.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Valid Selection Code AND User ID both captured?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is displaying up to 10 users, each with a selectable action field (SEL) and a corresponding User ID field (USRID), and the user has pressed the Enter key
acceptance_criteria.When: The system scans selection fields SEL0001 through SEL0010 in sequential order from row 1 to row 10 and finds the first row where the selection field contains a value that is neither blank (spaces) nor empty (low-values)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system captures the selection code from that row into the User Selection Flag (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG) and the User ID from the same row into the Selected User ID (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED); if no row has a non-blank selection code, both the User Selection Flag and Selected User ID are set to spaces

rules.rule_name: Validate That Both Selection Code and User ID Are Present Before Processing
rules.rule_description: Before routing the user to an action screen, the system verifies that both a selection code and a User ID have been successfully captured. If either is missing or blank, the system bypasses action routing and proceeds directly to search and page processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Valid Selection Code AND User ID both captured?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed scanning all 10 selection rows after the user pressed Enter
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the User Selection Flag (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG) is not blank or empty AND the Selected User ID (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED) is not blank or empty
acceptance_criteria.Then: If both the User Selection Flag and the Selected User ID contain valid non-blank, non-empty values, the system proceeds to evaluate the selection code for action routing; if either value is blank or empty, the system skips action routing and continues directly to search and page processing

rules.rule_name: Navigate to Update User Screen When 'U' Is Selected
rules.rule_description: When a user enters 'U' or 'u' as the selection code next to a user on the list, the system transfers control to the Update User program, passing the selected User ID and current session context so the administrator can update that user's details.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: U or u → Navigate to Update User Program: COUSR02C Passing Selected User ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: Both the User Selection Flag and the Selected User ID have been captured with valid non-blank values, and the User Selection Flag contains the value 'U' or 'u' (case-insensitive)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the User Selection Flag and matches it to 'U' or 'u'
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the target program to 'COUSR02C' (Update User), records the current transaction ID as the originating transaction, records the current program name as the originating program, sets the program context to 0, and transfers full control to the Update User program (COUSR02C) passing the complete session communication area including the selected User ID; the current program ends and does not continue further processing

rules.rule_name: Navigate to Delete User Screen When 'D' Is Selected
rules.rule_description: When a user enters 'D' or 'd' as the selection code next to a user on the list, the system transfers control to the Delete User program, passing the selected User ID and current session context so the administrator can delete that user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: D or d → Navigate to Delete User Program: COUSR03C Passing Selected User ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: Both the User Selection Flag and the Selected User ID have been captured with valid non-blank values, and the User Selection Flag contains the value 'D' or 'd' (case-insensitive)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the User Selection Flag and matches it to 'D' or 'd'
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the target program to 'COUSR03C' (Delete User), records the current transaction ID as the originating transaction, records the current program name as the originating program, sets the program context to 0, and transfers full control to the Delete User program (COUSR03C) passing the complete session communication area including the selected User ID; the current program ends and does not continue further processing

rules.rule_name: Display Error for Invalid Selection Code Entry
rules.rule_description: When a user enters a selection code that is not 'U', 'u', 'D', or 'd', the system rejects the action, displays an error message informing the user of the valid options, and continues to search and page processing without navigating away from the User List screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Any Other Value → Display Error Message 'Invalid selection. Valid values are U and D'

acceptance_criteria.Given: Both the User Selection Flag and the Selected User ID have been captured with valid non-blank values, and the User Selection Flag contains a value other than 'U', 'u', 'D', or 'd'
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the User Selection Flag and finds no match to any valid selection code
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the error message 'Invalid selection. Valid values are U and D' on the screen, sets the cursor focus to the User ID input field, and continues to search and page processing without transferring control to any other program

rules.rule_name: Bypass Action Routing and Proceed to Page Processing When No Selection Is Made
rules.rule_description: When the user presses Enter without entering any selection code next to any of the displayed users, the system skips all action routing logic and proceeds directly to search and page processing to refresh or filter the user list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No - No selection made → Continue to Search / Page Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed the Enter key on the User List screen and all 10 selection fields (SEL0001 through SEL0010) are blank or empty
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines that the User Selection Flag (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG) is blank or empty OR the Selected User ID (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED) is blank or empty after scanning all rows
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system does not attempt any action routing, clears both the User Selection Flag and the Selected User ID to spaces, and proceeds directly to search and page processing to load and display the user list

key_functionalities.title: Navigate to Update User
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Enter: User Selection Detected]) 
    B{Is selection flag\n'U' or 'u'?}
    C[Record current program\nand transaction as origin]
    D[Set destination program\nto Update User - COUSR02C]
    E[Pass selected User ID\nin communication area]
    F[Transfer control to\nUpdate User Screen\nCOUSR02C]
    G([End: Control passed to\nUpdate User Program])
    H([Exit: Not an Update\nSelection - Continue])

    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - Update Selected| C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G
    B -->|No - Different Selection| H

rules.rule_name: Identify Update User Selection
rules.rule_description: Determine whether the action code entered by the user next to a user record is an Update request, accepting both uppercase 'U' and lowercase 'u' as valid update indicators.
