rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is selection flag 'U' or 'u'?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user has entered a selection code next to one of the displayed user records on the User List screen, and the selection code has been captured into the selection flag field
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the captured selection flag and finds it equals 'U' (uppercase) or 'u' (lowercase)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system identifies this as an Update User request and proceeds to set up the navigation to the Update User screen; if the selection flag is neither 'U' nor 'u', the Update User navigation path is not taken

rules.rule_name: Record Origin Program and Transaction for Update Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the Update User program, the system records the current program name and transaction ID as the originating source so that the Update User program knows where to return after completing its operation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record current program and transaction as origin

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected 'U' or 'u' next to a user record on the User List screen, and the system has confirmed this is an Update User request
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to navigate to the Update User program
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the current transaction ID into the 'From Transaction' field of the communication area, and records the current program name into the 'From Program' field of the communication area, so the Update User program can identify its caller

rules.rule_name: Set Update User as Destination Program
rules.rule_description: When an Update action is confirmed, the system designates the Update User program (COUSR02C) as the target destination for the navigation transfer.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set destination program to Update User - COUSR02C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected 'U' or 'u' next to a user record, and the origin program and transaction have been recorded in the communication area
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sets up the navigation destination
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program identifier in the communication area to 'COUSR02C' (Update User Program)

rules.rule_name: Pass Selected User ID to Update User Program
rules.rule_description: The User ID of the record selected for update is passed through the shared communication area to the Update User program, so it knows which user record to load and present for editing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Pass selected User ID in communication area

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has selected 'U' or 'u' next to a specific user record on the User List screen, and the destination program has been set to COUSR02C
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the communication area for the transfer
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system places the selected User ID into the 'User Selected' field of the communication area, and places the selection flag ('U' or 'u') into the 'User Selection Flag' field, and sets the program context to zero indicating a fresh invocation, so the Update User program receives the correct user to process

rules.rule_name: Transfer Control to Update User Program
rules.rule_description: After all navigation parameters are set, the system transfers full control to the Update User program (COUSR02C), passing the complete communication area containing the selected user's details, origin program, and transaction information.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer control to Update User Screen COUSR02C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The communication area has been populated with the selected User ID, selection flag, origin transaction ID, origin program name, destination program name (COUSR02C), and program context set to zero
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the program transfer
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control is fully transferred to the Update User program (COUSR02C) along with the entire communication area; the User List program (COUSR00C) is no longer active and the Update User program takes over the user's session

key_functionalities.title: Navigate to Delete User
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Enter Key Pressed])
    B[Scan all 10 screen rows\nfor user selection input]
    C{Was a selection code\nentered next to a user?}
    D{Is the selection\ncode 'D' or 'd'?}
    E[Capture the selected\nUser ID from that row]
    F[Set destination program\nto Delete User - COUSR03C]
    G[Record current program\nand transaction details\nfor return navigation]
    H[Transfer control to\nDelete User Program\npassing selected User ID]
    I[Continue with\nother processing]

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C -->|Yes - Selection Found| E
    C -->|No Selection| I
    E --> D
    D -->|Yes - Delete Selected| F
    D -->|No - Other Code| I
    F --> G

rules.rule_name: Scan All Screen Rows to Identify User Selection
rules.rule_description: When the Enter key is pressed on the User List screen, the system scans all 10 displayed user rows in order (row 1 through row 10) to find the first row where the user has entered a selection code. Only the first non-blank selection found is processed; all subsequent selections are ignored.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Scan all 10 screen rows for user selection input

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is displaying up to 10 user records, each with a selection input field (SEL0001 through SEL0010) and a corresponding User ID field (USRID01 through USRID10)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses the Enter key after entering a selection code next to one or more user records
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system scans selection fields SEL0001 through SEL0010 sequentially and captures the selection code and User ID from the FIRST row where the selection field is not blank and not empty. If no selection field contains a value, both the selection flag and the selected User ID are cleared to spaces.

rules.rule_name: Capture Selected User ID from the Chosen Row
rules.rule_description: Once the first non-blank selection row is identified, the system captures both the action code entered by the user and the User ID associated with that row, storing them for subsequent processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture the selected User ID from that row

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has identified a screen row (1 through 10) where the user has entered a non-blank, non-empty selection code next to a displayed user record
acceptance_criteria.When: The selection code and User ID are read from that specific row
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system stores the entered selection code into the User Selection Flag (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG) and stores the corresponding User ID from that row (USRID01 through USRID10) into the Selected User ID field (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED)

rules.rule_name: Validate Delete Action Selection Code
rules.rule_description: After a selection has been captured, the system validates whether the entered action code represents a Delete request. The delete action is recognized only when the selection code is the letter 'D' (uppercase or lowercase), and a valid User ID has been captured alongside it.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is the selection code 'D' or 'd'?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A selection code has been captured from the User List screen and stored in the User Selection Flag (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG), and a non-blank User ID has been stored in the Selected User ID field (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the captured selection code
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the selection code is 'D' or 'd' AND the Selected User ID is not blank or empty, the system proceeds with the Delete User action. If the selection code is neither 'D' nor 'd', the delete action is not triggered and processing continues with other logic.

rules.rule_name: Set Destination Program to Delete User
rules.rule_description: When a valid Delete action code ('D' or 'd') is confirmed for a selected user, the system designates the Delete User program (COUSR03C) as the target destination for the navigation transfer.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set destination program to Delete User - COUSR03C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered 'D' or 'd' as the selection code next to a user record on the User List screen, and a valid User ID has been captured
acceptance_criteria.When: The system confirms the selection code is 'D' or 'd'
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program identifier to 'COUSR03C' (Delete User Program) in the navigation target field (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM)

rules.rule_name: Record Current Program and Transaction for Return Navigation
rules.rule_description: Before transferring control to the Delete User program, the system records the identity of the current program and transaction so that the Delete User program can navigate back to the User List screen upon completion.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Record current program and transaction details for return navigation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has confirmed a Delete action and has set the destination program to COUSR03C
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to transfer control to the Delete User program
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system records the current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) into the originating transaction field (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), records the current Program Name (WS-PGMNAME) into the originating program field (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), and sets the Program Context indicator (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) to zero to indicate a fresh entry into the target program

rules.rule_name: Transfer Control to Delete User Program with Selected User ID
rules.rule_description: After recording navigation details, the system transfers full control to the Delete User program (COUSR03C), passing the complete session context including the selected User ID, so the Delete User program can operate on the correct user record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Transfer control to Delete User Program passing selected User ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The destination program has been set to COUSR03C, the current program and transaction details have been recorded in the session context (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), and the selected User ID is stored in CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED within the session context
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the program transfer
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control is fully transferred to the Delete User program (COUSR03C) and the complete session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) — containing the selected User ID, originating program, originating transaction, and program context — is passed to the Delete User program. The current User List program ceases execution.

rules.rule_name: Detect User Selection from List
rules.rule_description: The system scans all 10 user rows on the User List screen to determine whether the user has entered a selection code next to any displayed user record. The first non-blank, non-low-value selection field found (rows 1 through 10, in order) is treated as the active selection.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is a selection code entered next to a user record?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is displayed with up to 10 user records, and the user has pressed the Enter key
acceptance_criteria.When: The system scans selection fields SEL0001 through SEL0010 in order from row 1 to row 10 and finds the first field that is not blank and not empty
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system captures that selection code and the corresponding User ID from the same row as the active selection, and proceeds to evaluate the selection code; if no selection field contains a value, the selection flag and selected user ID are cleared and the system proceeds directly to search and page processing without any navigation

rules.rule_name: Navigate to Update User Screen
rules.rule_description: When a user enters the selection code 'U' or 'u' next to a displayed user record and presses Enter, the system navigates to the Update User screen, passing the selected user's information for update processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Navigate to Update User COUSR02C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is displayed with user records, and the user has entered a selection code next to one of the displayed user records
acceptance_criteria.When: The selection code entered is 'U' (uppercase) or 'u' (lowercase) and the corresponding User ID is not blank
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the target program to COUSR02C (Update User), records the current transaction ID and program name as the originating context, resets the program context to 0, and transfers control to the Update User program passing the full session communication area

rules.rule_name: Navigate to Delete User Screen
rules.rule_description: When a user enters the selection code 'D' or 'd' next to a displayed user record and presses Enter, the system navigates to the Delete User screen, passing the selected user's information for deletion processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Navigate to Delete User COUSR03C

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is displayed with user records, and the user has entered a selection code next to one of the displayed user records
acceptance_criteria.When: The selection code entered is 'D' (uppercase) or 'd' (lowercase) and the corresponding User ID is not blank
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the target program to COUSR03C (Delete User), records the current transaction ID and program name as the originating context, resets the program context to 0, and transfers control to the Delete User program passing the full session communication area

rules.rule_name: Invalid Selection Code Validation
rules.rule_description: When a user enters a selection code that is not 'U', 'u', 'D', or 'd' next to a displayed user record, the system rejects the selection and displays an error message indicating the only valid selection codes are U and D. The system then continues to refresh the user list screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
11: Invalid Selection Validation
Display message:
'Invalid selection.
Valid values are U and D'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is displayed with user records, and the user has entered a selection code next to one of the displayed user records
acceptance_criteria.When: The selection code entered is any value other than 'U', 'u', 'D', or 'd'
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the error message 'Invalid selection. Valid values are U and D' on the screen, sets the cursor focus to the User ID input field, and continues to the search and page processing to refresh the user list display

rules.rule_name: Proceed to Search and Page Processing Without Selection
rules.rule_description: When the user presses Enter without entering any selection code next to any of the displayed user records, the system clears any prior selection context and proceeds directly to search and page processing to refresh or filter the user list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Continue to Search/Page Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is displayed with up to 10 user records
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses Enter and all 10 selection fields (SEL0001 through SEL0010) are blank or empty
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system clears the selection flag and the selected user ID, and proceeds to search and page processing using the User ID entered in the search field (or from the beginning of the user directory if the search field is blank)

key_functionalities.title: User ID Search Criteria Handling
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: User ID Search Criteria Handling])
    B[Capture User ID entered\nin the search field]
    C{Is the search field\nblank or empty?}
    D[Set search starting point\nto beginning of User file]
    E[Use entered User ID\nas search starting point]
    F[Reset page number to zero]
    G[Load first page of users\nfrom the determined starting point]
    H([End: Users displayed\nfrom starting point])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C -->|Yes - Blank| D
    C -->|No - User ID entered| E
    D --> F
    E --> F
    F --> G
    G --> H

rules.rule_name: Capture User ID from Search Field
rules.rule_description: When the user submits the User List screen, the system captures whatever value has been entered in the User ID search field to determine where to begin browsing the user directory.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Capture User ID entered in the search field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen has been submitted by the user pressing the ENTER key
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the search request
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system reads the value from the User ID search input field (USRIDINI) to use as the basis for determining the starting point of the user directory browse

rules.rule_name: Blank Search Field Defaults to Start of User Directory
rules.rule_description: If the user leaves the User ID search field blank or empty, the system automatically starts browsing the user directory from the very beginning, ensuring all users are accessible.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is the search field blank or empty? → Yes - Blank → Set search starting point to beginning of User file

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the User List screen with the User ID search field left blank or containing only spaces or empty (low-value) characters
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the content of the User ID search field
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the browse starting key to the lowest possible value (beginning of the user directory), so that the user list is retrieved from the very first user record on file

rules.rule_name: Entered User ID Used as Search Starting Point
rules.rule_description: If the user enters a specific User ID in the search field, the system uses that User ID as the starting point for browsing the user directory, allowing the user to navigate directly to a specific position in the list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is the search field blank or empty? → No - User ID entered → Use entered User ID as search starting point

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has submitted the User List screen with a specific User ID value entered in the User ID search field (not blank and not empty)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the content of the User ID search field
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the browse starting key to the exact User ID value entered by the user, so that the user list is retrieved beginning from that specific user record

rules.rule_name: Page Number Reset to Zero Before New Search
rules.rule_description: Before loading a fresh set of results based on a new search starting point, the system resets the page counter to zero so that page numbering begins correctly from page 1 when the first page of results is displayed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reset page number to zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has determined the browse starting point based on the User ID search field (either beginning of file or a specific User ID)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to load the user list
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system resets the current page number to zero, so that the subsequent page load will correctly assign and display page number 1 as the first page of results

rules.rule_name: Load and Display First Page of Users from Determined Starting Point
rules.rule_description: After the search starting point is established and the page counter is reset, the system retrieves and displays the first page of up to 10 users beginning from the determined starting position in the user directory. If the page loads successfully without errors, the User ID search field is cleared on the display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Load first page of users from the determined starting point

acceptance_criteria.Given: The browse starting key has been set (either to the beginning of the user directory or to a specific User ID) and the page number has been reset to zero
acceptance_criteria.When: The system executes the forward page load process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves up to 10 user records starting from the determined position and displays them on the User List screen; if the page loads successfully with no errors, the User ID search input field is cleared on the screen so it does not retain the previously entered search value

key_functionalities.title: Page Forward Navigation (Enter Key)
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Enter Key Pressed\nNo User Selection Made])
    B{User ID entered\nin search field?}
    C[Start browsing from\nbeginning of user list]
    D[Start browsing from\nentered User ID]
    E[Reset page number to zero]
    F[Clear all 10 user rows\non screen]
    G[Read up to 10 user records\nsequentially from user file]
    H{Were any records\nsuccessfully read?}

    P[Store first and last\nUser IDs displayed\nfor pagination]
    Q[Update page number\non screen]
    R[Populate screen header\nwith date, time, program info]
    S[Display updated\nUser List Screen]

    B -->|User ID Provided| D

    D --> E

    H -->|No Records Found| N
    H -->|Records Found| I
    I -->|Less than 10 records| J
    I -->|10 records loaded| J
    J --> K
    K --> L
    L -->|Yes| M
    L -->|No - End of File| N
    N --> O
    O --> P
    M --> P
    P --> Q
    Q --> R
    R --> S

rules.rule_name: Determine Browse Start Position Based on User ID Search Field
rules.rule_description: When the Enter key is pressed with no user selection made, the system determines the starting position for browsing the user list based on whether a User ID has been entered in the search field.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: User ID entered in search field?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed the Enter key on the User List screen without selecting any user action
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the User ID search field (USRIDINI): if it contains spaces or low-values it is considered blank; otherwise it contains a valid User ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the search field is blank or empty, the browse starting key is set to LOW-VALUES (beginning of the user list); if a User ID is provided, the browse starting key is set to that entered User ID (SEC-USR-ID)

rules.rule_name: Reset Page Number to Zero Before Loading New Page
rules.rule_description: When the Enter key is pressed to initiate a new user list search or refresh, the current page number counter must be reset to zero before any page loading begins, ensuring accurate page numbering from the start.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reset page number to zero

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed the Enter key on the User List screen and the browse start position has been determined
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to load the user list page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The page number counter (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is set to zero before the page forward process begins

rules.rule_name: Clear All Ten User Rows Before Populating New Page Data
rules.rule_description: Before populating the user list screen with new data, all ten user display rows must be cleared to spaces to prevent stale data from a previous page from remaining visible.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear all 10 user rows on screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The page forward process has started and the user file browse has been successfully opened
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to populate the user list screen with new records
acceptance_criteria.Then: All ten user display rows (rows 1 through 10) are cleared to spaces, including User ID (USRID01I–USRID10I), First Name (FNAME01I–FNAME10I), Last Name (LNAME01I–LNAME10I), and User Type (UTYPE01I–UTYPE10I) fields for each row

rules.rule_name: Read Up to Ten User Records Sequentially from User File
rules.rule_description: The system reads user records sequentially from the User Security file, starting from the determined browse position, populating up to ten rows on the screen. Reading stops when ten records have been loaded or the end of the file is reached.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read up to 10 user records sequentially from user file

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user file browse has been opened at the correct starting position and all ten display rows have been cleared
acceptance_criteria.When: The system reads records sequentially forward through the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.Then: Up to 10 user records are read one at a time; for each successfully read record, the User ID (SEC-USR-ID), First Name (SEC-USR-FNAME), Last Name (SEC-USR-LNAME), and User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE) are populated into the corresponding screen row (1 through 10); reading stops when 10 records are loaded or end of file is reached

rules.rule_name: Handle No Records Found During Page Forward Load
rules.rule_description: If no user records are found during a forward page load (e.g., the search key is beyond all existing records), the system marks that no next page is available and does not increment the page number.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Were any records successfully read?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to read user records sequentially from the User Security file during a page forward operation
acceptance_criteria.When: No records are successfully read (WS-IDX remains at 1, meaning zero records were populated)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next-page indicator is set to NEXT-PAGE-NO (no further pages available) and the page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is not incremented

rules.rule_name: Attempt to Read One Additional Record to Determine If More Pages Exist
rules.rule_description: After successfully loading up to 10 user records onto the screen, the system attempts to read one additional record from the User Security file to determine whether more pages of users exist beyond the current page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Attempt to read one additional record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has successfully read at least one user record and populated the screen rows during a page forward operation
acceptance_criteria.When: The loop to read up to 10 records has completed (WS-IDX has reached 11 or end of file was hit)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system attempts one additional sequential read (READNEXT) from the User Security file to check if any more records exist beyond the current page

rules.rule_name: Mark Next Page Available When Additional Records Exist
rules.rule_description: If an additional record is found beyond the 10 records currently displayed, the system marks that a next page is available, enabling the PF8 (page forward) navigation for the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Additional record exists?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has loaded up to 10 user records and attempted to read one additional record from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The additional read is successful and a record is found (USER-SEC-NOT-EOF is TRUE and no error flag is set)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next-page indicator is set to NEXT-PAGE-YES, signaling that PF8 navigation to the next page is available

rules.rule_name: Mark No Next Page and Display Bottom-of-List Message When End of File Reached
rules.rule_description: If no additional record exists beyond the currently displayed 10 records, the system marks that no further pages are available and informs the user they have reached the bottom of the user list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No - End of File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has loaded up to 10 user records and attempted to read one additional record from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The additional read returns end-of-file (USER-SEC-EOF is TRUE), meaning no more records exist beyond the current page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next-page indicator is set to NEXT-PAGE-NO and the message 'You have reached the bottom of the page...' is set in the message field (WS-MESSAGE) to be displayed to the user

rules.rule_name: Store First and Last User IDs on Current Page for Pagination
rules.rule_description: The User ID of the first record displayed (row 1) and the User ID of the last record displayed (row 10) are saved to support accurate forward and backward page navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Store first and last User IDs displayed for pagination

acceptance_criteria.Given: User records are being populated into the screen display rows during a page forward operation
acceptance_criteria.When: The first user record is populated into row 1 and the tenth user record is populated into row 10
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID of the row-1 record is saved as the first-on-page anchor (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST) and the User ID of the row-10 record is saved as the last-on-page anchor (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-LAST)

rules.rule_name: Increment Page Number After Successfully Loading a Page
rules.rule_description: After records have been successfully read and the page has been populated, the page number counter is incremented by 1 to reflect the newly displayed page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Increment page number by 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed reading user records for the current page forward operation
acceptance_criteria.When: At least one record was successfully read and populated (WS-IDX is greater than 1)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The page number counter (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is incremented by 1 (COMPUTE CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM = CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM + 1)

rules.rule_name: Update Page Number Display on User List Screen
rules.rule_description: The current page number is moved to the screen's page number display field so the user can see which page of the user list they are currently viewing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Update page number on screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The page number counter (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) has been updated after loading the current page
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to send the User List screen to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page number value from CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM is moved to the screen page number display field (PAGENUMI OF COUSR0AI) so it is visible on the screen

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Header with Current Date, Time, and Program Information
rules.rule_description: Before displaying the User List screen, the screen header is populated with the current date, current time, transaction ID, and program name to provide the user with contextual information.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Populate screen header with date, time, program info

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the User List screen after completing a page load operation
acceptance_criteria.When: The SEND-USRLST-SCREEN routine is invoked
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen header is populated with: application title lines (CCDA-TITLE01, CCDA-TITLE02), current transaction ID (WS-TRANID → TRNNAMEO), program name (WS-PGMNAME → PGMNAMEO), current date formatted as MM/DD/YY (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY → CURDATEO), and current time formatted as HH:MM:SS (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS → CURTIMEO)

rules.rule_name: Display Updated User List Screen to User
rules.rule_description: After all data has been populated, the User List screen is sent to the user's terminal. The screen is sent with a full erase when the erase flag is set, or as an overlay update when the erase flag is not set.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display updated User List Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen header, user data rows, page number, and any messages have all been populated and the system is ready to present the User List screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The SEND-USRLST-SCREEN routine executes the screen send
acceptance_criteria.Then: If SEND-ERASE-YES is set, the screen is sent with a full terminal erase (ERASE option) and cursor positioned; if SEND-ERASE-NO is set, the screen is sent without erasing (overlay) with cursor positioned; in both cases the screen map COUSR0A from mapset COUSR00 is used with the output data from COUSR0AO

rules.rule_name: Clear User ID Search Field Display After Successful Page Load
rules.rule_description: After a successful page forward load with no errors, the User ID search/filter display field on the screen is cleared to spaces, providing a clean input area for the next search.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display updated User List Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The page forward process has completed successfully with no error flag set (ERR-FLG-ON is FALSE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system returns from the PROCESS-PAGE-FORWARD routine back to PROCESS-ENTER-KEY
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID output display field (USRIDINO OF COUSR0AO) is set to a single space, clearing the search field on the screen

sub_functionalities.title: Read up to 10 user records sequentially from user file → For each record: populate screen row with User ID, First Name, Last Name, User Type → Track first User ID on row 1 and last User ID on row 10 → Check if all 10 rows filled or end of file reached
sub_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Load Page Forward])
    B[Set Row Counter to 1]
    C{All 10 rows filled\nor End of File reached?}
    D[Read Next User Record\nfrom User Security File]
    E{Record\nRetrieved?}
    F{Row Number = 1?}
    G[Populate Row 1:\nUser ID, First Name,\nLast Name, User Type\nSave as FIRST User ID\nfor pagination]
    H{Row Number = 10?}
    I[Populate Row 10:\nUser ID, First Name,\nLast Name, User Type\nSave as LAST User ID\nfor pagination]
    J[Populate Current Row:\nUser ID, First Name,\nLast Name, User Type]
    K[Advance to Next Row]
    L{End of File\nreached?}
    M([End: Page Rows Populated])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C -->|No - Continue Loading| D
    C -->|Yes - Stop Loading| L
    D --> E
    E -->|Record Found| F
    E -->|End of File| L
    F -->|Yes - Row 1| G
    G --> H
    F -->|No| H
    H -->|Yes - Row 10| I
    I --> K
    H -->|No| J
    J --> K
    K --> C
    L -->|EOF Reached| M
    C -->|10 Rows Filled| M

rules.rule_name: Initialize Row Counter Before Loading User List Page
rules.rule_description: Before loading users onto the screen, the row counter must be initialized to position 1 so that user records are populated starting from the first row of the display.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Row Counter to 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is about to load a forward page of users onto the User List screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The page-forward loading process begins
acceptance_criteria.Then: The row counter is set to 1, ensuring user records will be populated starting from the first display row

rules.rule_name: Continue Loading Users Until 10 Rows Filled or End of File Reached
rules.rule_description: The user list page loading loop must continue reading and displaying user records until either all 10 display rows are filled or there are no more user records available in the user security file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: All 10 rows filled or End of File reached?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is in the process of loading user records onto the User List screen
acceptance_criteria.When: Each iteration of the loading loop is evaluated
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the row counter has exceeded 10 (all rows filled) OR the end of the user security file has been reached, the loading loop stops; otherwise the loop continues reading the next user record

rules.rule_name: Read Next User Record Sequentially from User Security File
rules.rule_description: During forward page loading, the system reads user records one at a time in sequential order from the User Security file to populate the display rows.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read Next User Record from User Security File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The loading loop is active and fewer than 10 rows have been filled and the end of file has not been reached
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to read the next user record from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The next sequential user record (containing User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type) is retrieved from the User Security file; if no more records exist, the end-of-file condition is set and the loading loop terminates

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Row with Retrieved User Record Data
rules.rule_description: When a user record is successfully retrieved from the User Security file, the system populates the corresponding screen display row with the user's details including User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Populate Current Row: User ID, First Name, Last Name, User Type

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file and the current row number is between 2 and 9 (inclusive)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the current display row
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type from the retrieved record are written to the corresponding fields of the current screen row (rows 2 through 9)

rules.rule_name: Populate Row 1 and Save as First User ID for Backward Pagination
rules.rule_description: When the first user record is loaded onto the screen (row 1), the system must save that user's ID as the pagination anchor so that the system knows where to start when the user navigates backward to the previous page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Populate Row 1: User ID, First Name, Last Name, User Type Save as FIRST User ID for pagination

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file and the current row counter is at position 1
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates display row 1
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type are written to screen row 1, AND the User ID is additionally saved as the FIRST User ID on the current page (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST) to serve as the backward navigation anchor

rules.rule_name: Populate Row 10 and Save as Last User ID for Forward Pagination
rules.rule_description: When the tenth user record is loaded onto the screen (row 10), the system must save that user's ID as the pagination anchor so that the system knows where to start when the user navigates forward to the next page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Populate Row 10: User ID, First Name, Last Name, User Type Save as LAST User ID for pagination

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file and the current row counter is at position 10
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates display row 10
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type are written to screen row 10, AND the User ID is additionally saved as the LAST User ID on the current page (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-LAST) to serve as the forward navigation anchor

rules.rule_name: Advance Row Counter After Each Successfully Populated Row
rules.rule_description: After each user record is successfully retrieved and its data is populated onto the current screen row, the row counter must be incremented by 1 to move to the next available display row.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Advance to Next Row

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully retrieved and its data has been populated onto the current screen row
acceptance_criteria.When: The row population for the current record is complete
acceptance_criteria.Then: The row counter is incremented by 1 (e.g., from row N to row N+1), positioning the system to populate the next display row on the subsequent loop iteration

rules.rule_name: Stop Page Loading When End of User File is Reached
rules.rule_description: When there are no more user records available in the User Security file during forward page loading, the loading process must stop regardless of how many rows have been filled, and the page is displayed with however many users were retrieved.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: End of File reached?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is loading user records onto the User List screen and a read attempt on the User Security file returns no record because the end of the file has been reached
acceptance_criteria.When: The end-of-file condition is detected during the loading loop
acceptance_criteria.Then: The end-of-file flag (USER-SEC-EOF) is set to TRUE, the loading loop terminates immediately, and the screen is displayed with only the rows that were successfully populated (remaining rows stay blank)

key_functionalities.title: Page Backward Navigation (PF7)
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([PF7 Key Pressed]) 
    B[Set starting position to\nFirst User ID of current page]

    R[Close browse on\nUser Security File]
    S[23: Populate screen header\nwith title, date, time, program info]
    T[24: Display updated user list\nwith new page number]

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D -->|No - Already on first page| E
    E --> F
    F --> U
    D -->|Yes - Previous page exists| G
    G --> H
    H --> I
    I --> J
    J --> K
    K --> L
    L --> M
    M -->|No records found| N
    N --> R

    O -->|No - Top of list reached| Q
    P --> R
    Q --> R

rules.rule_name: Set Starting Browse Position for Backward Navigation
rules.rule_description: When PF7 is pressed to navigate backward, the system sets the browse starting position to the first User ID currently displayed on the screen. If no first User ID is recorded, browsing starts from the very beginning of the user directory.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set starting position to First User ID of current page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing the User List screen and the current page has a recorded first User ID (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF7 to navigate to the previous page
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the first User ID of the current page is not blank or empty, the browse starting key (SEC-USR-ID) is set to that first User ID; otherwise, the browse starting key is set to LOW-VALUES (beginning of the user directory)

rules.rule_name: Enable Forward Page Availability Flag on PF7
rules.rule_description: When PF7 is pressed, the system marks that a next page (forward direction) is available, ensuring that PF8 navigation remains enabled after moving backward.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Next-Page flag to YES

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen and presses PF7
acceptance_criteria.When: PF7 key is processed before any page navigation occurs
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Next-Page availability flag is set to YES, indicating that forward navigation (PF8) will be available from the previous page

rules.rule_name: Validate Backward Navigation is Permitted
rules.rule_description: Before navigating backward, the system checks whether the user is beyond the first page. Backward navigation is only allowed when the current page number is greater than 1.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is current page number greater than 1?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user presses PF7 on the User List screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the current page number is greater than 1, the system proceeds with backward page navigation; if the current page number is 1 or less, the system displays the message 'You are already at the top of the page...' and refreshes the current screen without changing the displayed data

rules.rule_name: Display Top-of-List Message When Already on First Page
rules.rule_description: When the user attempts to navigate backward but is already on the first page, the system informs them that no previous pages exist and keeps the current screen content unchanged.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display message: 'You are already at the top of the page...'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing page 1 of the User List screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF7 to navigate to a previous page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the message 'You are already at the top of the page...' in the message area, the screen is refreshed without erasing existing content (Send-Erase flag set to NO), and the user remains on the current page with no data changes

rules.rule_name: Open User Directory Browse for Backward Navigation
rules.rule_description: To retrieve the previous page of users, the system opens a browse session on the User Security file starting at the first User ID of the currently displayed page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Open browse on User Security File starting at first User ID of current page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current page number is greater than 1 and the browse starting key has been set to the first User ID of the current page
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initiates backward page navigation
acceptance_criteria.Then: A browse session is opened on the User Security file (WS-USRSEC-FILE) positioned at the first User ID of the current page; if the browse cannot be opened, an error message 'Unable to lookup User...' is displayed and navigation is aborted

rules.rule_name: Skip Current Page's First Record Before Reading Previous Records
rules.rule_description: When navigating backward and the action was not triggered by ENTER or PF8, the system reads past the current page's first record so that the previous page begins with the record immediately before it.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Skip past the current page's first record

acceptance_criteria.Given: The browse session is open and positioned at the first User ID of the current page
acceptance_criteria.When: The triggering action is not ENTER key, PF8, or PF3
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system reads one record backward (READPREV) to move the browse position past the current page's first record, so that subsequent reads retrieve the records belonging to the previous page

rules.rule_name: Clear All User Display Rows Before Populating Previous Page
rules.rule_description: Before populating the screen with the previous page's user data, all 10 display rows are cleared to spaces to prevent stale data from a prior page from remaining visible.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 18: Clear all 10 user rows on screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The browse session is open and positioned correctly for backward reading
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is about to populate the screen with the previous page's user records
acceptance_criteria.Then: All 10 user display rows on the screen are cleared — each row's User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type fields are set to spaces — before any new data is written

rules.rule_name: Read Up to 10 User Records in Reverse Order
rules.rule_description: The system reads up to 10 user records backward from the User Security file to fill the previous page, stopping when 10 records are read, the beginning of the file is reached, or an error occurs.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read up to 10 user records in reverse order

acceptance_criteria.Given: The browse session is open, all 10 display rows have been cleared, and the index (WS-IDX) is set to 10
acceptance_criteria.When: The system reads user records in reverse order from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system reads records backward one at a time, decrementing the row index (WS-IDX) from 10 down to 1 after each successful read; reading stops when the index reaches 0, the beginning of the file is reached (EOF), or an error occurs; up to 10 records are retrieved

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Rows with User Data in Reverse Fill Order
rules.rule_description: As each user record is read backward, it is placed into the screen display row corresponding to the current index position, filling from row 10 down to row 1, so that the final display shows users in correct ascending order.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 19: Populate screen rows with user data rows filled from position 10 down to 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully read backward from the User Security file and the current row index (WS-IDX) is between 1 and 10
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the screen row for the current index position
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type from the retrieved user record are placed into the screen display fields for the row number matching the current index (e.g., index 10 fills row 10 fields: USRID10I, FNAME10I, LNAME10I, UTYPE10I; index 1 fills row 1 fields: USRID01I, FNAME01I, LNAME01I, UTYPE01I)

rules.rule_name: Record First and Last User IDs Displayed on Screen
rules.rule_description: When populating row 1 and row 10, the system saves those User IDs as the first and last User IDs on the current page respectively, enabling accurate forward and backward navigation in subsequent requests.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 22: Update First and Last User IDs displayed on screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: User records are being populated into the screen display rows during backward navigation
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates row 1 (index = 1) or row 10 (index = 10)
acceptance_criteria.Then: When row 1 is populated, the User ID of that record is saved as the First User ID on the page (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST); when row 10 is populated, the User ID of that record is saved as the Last User ID on the page (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-LAST)

rules.rule_name: Check Whether Any Previous Records Were Found
rules.rule_description: After attempting to read records backward, the system checks whether any user records were successfully retrieved to determine whether to update the page number or display a top-of-list message.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Were any previous records found?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed reading up to 10 records backward from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The backward read loop ends
acceptance_criteria.Then: If at least one record was found (USER-SEC-NOT-EOF is true and no error flag is set), the system proceeds to check for additional previous records; if no records were found (end-of-file reached immediately), the system displays the message 'You have reached the top of the page...' and proceeds to close the browse

rules.rule_name: Display Top-of-File Message When No Previous Records Exist
rules.rule_description: When backward reading yields no user records, the system informs the user that the beginning of the user directory has been reached.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display message: 'You have reached the top of the page...'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system attempted to read user records backward but reached the beginning of the User Security file without retrieving any records
acceptance_criteria.When: The end-of-file condition is encountered during backward reading
acceptance_criteria.Then: The message 'You have reached the top of the page...' is displayed in the message area of the User List screen

rules.rule_name: Check for Additional Previous Records Beyond Current Page
rules.rule_description: After filling the previous page with up to 10 records, the system attempts to read one more record backward to determine whether additional pages exist before the current page, which governs whether the page number should be decremented or reset to 1.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Does another previous record exist beyond current page?

acceptance_criteria.Given: Records were successfully found during backward reading and the Next-Page flag is set to YES
acceptance_criteria.When: The system reads one additional record backward after filling the 10 display rows
acceptance_criteria.Then: If another record exists (USER-SEC-NOT-EOF is true, no error, and current page number is greater than 1), the system decrements the page number by 1; if no additional record exists or the page number is already 1, the system resets the page number to 1

rules.rule_name: Decrement Page Number When Previous Records Exist
rules.rule_description: When backward navigation successfully finds a previous page and additional records exist before it, the current page number is decremented by 1 to reflect the user's new position in the user directory.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 20: Subtract 1 from current page number

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has successfully read 10 user records backward, the Next-Page flag is YES, an additional previous record exists beyond the current page, and the current page number is greater than 1
acceptance_criteria.When: The system updates the page number after backward navigation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is reduced by exactly 1 (SUBTRACT 1 FROM CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM)

rules.rule_name: Reset Page Number to 1 When Top of List is Reached
rules.rule_description: When backward navigation reaches the beginning of the user directory or the page number cannot be decremented further, the page number is reset to 1 to accurately reflect that the user is viewing the first page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 20: Reset page number to 1 Top of list reached

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed backward reading and either no additional previous record exists beyond the current page, or the current page number is already 1
acceptance_criteria.When: The system updates the page number after backward navigation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is set to 1, indicating the user is now on the first page of the user directory

rules.rule_name: Close User Directory Browse After Backward Navigation
rules.rule_description: After all backward reading operations are complete and the page number has been updated, the browse session on the User Security file is closed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Close browse on User Security File

acceptance_criteria.Given: All backward record reading and page number calculations have been completed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system finalizes the backward navigation process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The browse session on the User Security file (WS-USRSEC-FILE) is closed, releasing the browse cursor

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Header with Current Session Information
rules.rule_description: Before displaying the updated user list, the screen header is populated with the application titles, current date, current time, transaction ID, and program name to provide the user with current context information.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 23: Populate screen header with title, date, time, program info

acceptance_criteria.Given: The backward navigation is complete and the screen is ready to be sent to the user
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the User List screen for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen header fields are populated with: application title line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01), application title line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02), current transaction ID (WS-TRANID), current program name (WS-PGMNAME), current date formatted as MM/DD/YY, and current time formatted as HH:MM:SS

rules.rule_name: Display Updated User List with New Page Number
rules.rule_description: After backward navigation is complete, the system displays the updated User List screen showing the previous page's users along with the updated page number.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 24: Display updated user list with new page number

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen has been populated with the previous page's user records, the page number has been updated, and the screen header has been populated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the User List screen to the user's terminal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The updated page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is displayed in the page number field (PAGENUMI of COUSR0AI), the screen is sent with full erase (ERASE option) when Send-Erase flag is YES, or without erase when Send-Erase flag is NO, and the cursor is positioned at the User ID input field

rules.rule_name: Preserve Session State and Return After Backward Navigation
rules.rule_description: After displaying the updated user list, the system returns control to CICS while preserving the full session state in the communication area so that subsequent user actions can continue from the correct position.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 27: Preserve session state and return

acceptance_criteria.Given: The updated User List screen has been sent to the user's terminal after backward navigation
acceptance_criteria.When: The system completes the current transaction cycle
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control is returned to CICS with the transaction ID (WS-TRANID) and the full communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) — including current page number, first and last User IDs on page, selected user, and navigation flags — preserved for the next user interaction

key_functionalities.title: Page Forward Navigation (PF8)
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([PF8 Key Pressed])
    B{Last User ID on\nCurrent Page Available?}
    C[Set Starting Position to\nLast Displayed User ID]
    D[Set Starting Position to\nEnd of User List]
    E{Next Page\nExists?}
    F[Load Next Page of Users\nStarting from Last Displayed User ID]
    G[Display Message:\n'You are already at the\nbottom of the page...']
    H[Display Updated\nUser List Screen]
    I[Display User List Screen\nWith Message - No Refresh]
    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - Last User ID Known| C
    B -->|No - Last User ID Blank| D
    C --> E
    D --> E
    E -->|Yes - More Records Exist| F
    E -->|No - Already on Last Page| G
    F --> H
    G --> I

rules.rule_name: Set Starting Position Using Last Displayed User ID
rules.rule_description: When PF8 is pressed and the last user ID on the current page is known, the system uses that user ID as the starting position for browsing the next page of users.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Starting Position to Last Displayed User ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing the User List screen and the last displayed User ID on the current page is available (not blank or empty)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF8 to navigate to the next page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the browse starting position to the last displayed User ID on the current page, so the next page begins immediately after the current last record

rules.rule_name: Set Starting Position to End of User List When Last User ID Is Unknown
rules.rule_description: When PF8 is pressed but no last user ID is recorded for the current page (blank or empty), the system sets the browse starting position to the highest possible value, effectively pointing to the end of the user list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Starting Position to End of User List

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing the User List screen and the last displayed User ID on the current page is blank or empty
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF8 to navigate to the next page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the browse starting position to the highest possible value (end of user list), ensuring no records are skipped and the browse starts from the furthest available position

rules.rule_name: Block Navigation When Already on Last Page
rules.rule_description: When PF8 is pressed but the system has determined there are no more user records beyond the current page, navigation is blocked and an informational message is displayed to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Message: 'You are already at the bottom of the page...'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing the User List screen and the system has flagged that no further pages exist (next-page indicator is set to NO)
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF8 to navigate to the next page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the message 'You are already at the bottom of the page...' on the current screen without refreshing or reloading the user list, and the screen is redisplayed without erasing existing content

rules.rule_name: Clear All User Display Rows Before Loading Next Page
rules.rule_description: Before populating the screen with the next page of users, all 10 user display rows are cleared to spaces to prevent stale data from a previous page from remaining visible.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Load Next Page of Users Starting from Last Displayed User ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing to load the next page of users after a successful PF8 navigation request
acceptance_criteria.When: The next page load process begins
acceptance_criteria.Then: All 10 user display rows on the screen (User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type for rows 1 through 10) are cleared to blank spaces before any new user data is populated

rules.rule_name: Populate Up to 10 User Records on Next Page
rules.rule_description: The system reads up to 10 user records sequentially from the User Security file starting after the last displayed user, and populates each screen row with the user's ID, first name, last name, and user type.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Load Next Page of Users Starting from Last Displayed User ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The browse of the User Security file has been successfully started at the position of the last displayed User ID, and the display rows have been cleared
acceptance_criteria.When: The system reads user records forward from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.Then: Up to 10 user records are read and displayed on the screen, with each row showing the User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type; the first populated row's User ID is saved as the 'first user on page' and the tenth row's User ID is saved as the 'last user on page' for future navigation

rules.rule_name: Determine If Additional Pages Exist After Loading Next Page
rules.rule_description: After loading 10 user records, the system attempts to read one additional record to determine whether more users exist beyond the current page, setting the next-page availability indicator accordingly.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Load Next Page of Users Starting from Last Displayed User ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has successfully loaded up to 10 user records onto the current page
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to read one more record beyond the 10th displayed user
acceptance_criteria.Then: If an additional record exists, the next-page indicator is set to YES (PF8 will be available for further navigation); if no additional record exists, the next-page indicator is set to NO (PF8 will be blocked with the bottom-of-page message on the next press)

rules.rule_name: Increment Page Number After Successful Forward Navigation
rules.rule_description: After successfully loading a new page of users in the forward direction, the current page number is incremented by 1 to reflect the user's new position in the user list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Load Next Page of Users Starting from Last Displayed User ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed reading user records for the next page and at least one user record was found
acceptance_criteria.When: The forward page load process completes
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page number is increased by 1 and the updated page number is displayed on the User List screen

rules.rule_name: Display Updated User List Screen After Page Forward
rules.rule_description: After successfully loading the next page of users, the system refreshes the User List screen with the new user data, updated page number, current date, time, and any applicable messages.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Updated User List Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The next page of users has been successfully loaded into the screen display rows and the page number has been updated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the updated User List screen to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen is fully refreshed (erased and redrawn) displaying: the updated page number, up to 10 user records (User ID, First Name, Last Name, User Type), the application titles, current transaction ID, program name, current date in MM/DD/YY format, and current time in HH:MM:SS format

rules.rule_name: Redisplay Current Screen Without Refresh When at Bottom of List
rules.rule_description: When the user attempts to navigate past the last page, the screen is redisplayed with the informational message but without a full screen erase, preserving the currently displayed user list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display User List Screen With Message - No Refresh

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user pressed PF8 and the next-page indicator is set to NO (no further pages exist)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the User List screen back to the user
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen is redisplayed without erasing existing content (overlay mode), showing the message 'You are already at the bottom of the page...' while retaining the currently displayed user list data unchanged

key_functionalities.title: Forward Page Data Loading
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Start: Forward Page Data Loading])
    B[Open Browse on User Security File\nStarting at specified User ID]
    C{Navigation source:\nEnter, PF7, or PF3?}
    D[Skip one record forward\nto advance past current position]
    E[Clear all 10 user rows on screen]
    F[Read next user record\nfrom User Security File]
    G{Record found\nand no errors?}
    H[Populate screen row with\nUser ID, First Name,\nLast Name, User Type]
    I[Store User ID as\nFirst User on Page\nif this is row 1]
    J[Store User ID as\nLast User on Page\nif this is row 10]
    K{All 10 rows filled\nor end of file?}
    L{Were any records\nsuccessfully loaded?}
    M[Increment Page Number by 1]
    N[Attempt to read\none additional record]
    O{Additional record\nexists?}
    P[Set Next Page Flag = YES\nMore users available]
    Q[Set Next Page Flag = NO\nNo more users available]
    R[Close Browse on\nUser Security File]
    S[Update Page Number\non Screen]
    T[Display User List Screen]
    U([End: Forward Page Data Loading])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C -->|Enter, PF7, or PF3| E
    C -->|PF8 or First Load| D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G
    G -->|Record Found| H
    H --> I
    I --> J
    J --> K
    K -->|More rows to fill| F
    K -->|All 10 filled or EOF| L
    G -->|End of File| L
    L -->|Yes, records loaded| M
    L -->|No records loaded| Q
    M --> N
    N --> O
    O -->|Yes| P
    O -->|No / End of File| Q
    P --> R
    Q --> R
    R --> S
    S --> T
    T --> U

rules.rule_name: Open Browse on User Security File at Specified Starting Position
rules.rule_description: When loading a forward page of users, the system opens a sequential browse on the User Security file beginning at the specified User ID, which serves as the starting position for reading user records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Open Browse on User Security File
Starting at specified User ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is about to load a forward page of user records and a starting User ID position has been determined (either a specific User ID entered by the administrator, LOW-VALUES to start from the beginning of the file, or HIGH-VALUES to start from the end)
acceptance_criteria.When: The forward page data loading process is initiated
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system opens a browse on the User Security file using the specified User ID as the starting key, enabling sequential forward reading of user records from that position

rules.rule_name: Skip One Record Forward Based on Navigation Source
rules.rule_description: When navigating forward via PF8 or on the initial screen load, the system skips one record forward past the current position to avoid re-displaying the last record of the previous page. When navigating via Enter, PF7, or PF3, no skip is performed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Navigation source:
Enter, PF7, or PF3?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The browse on the User Security file has been successfully opened at the specified starting User ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The navigation source is determined — if the user pressed PF8 or this is the initial page load (i.e., the action was NOT Enter key, NOT PF7, and NOT PF3)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system reads and discards one record forward to advance past the current anchor position before beginning to populate the screen rows; if the navigation source was Enter, PF7, or PF3, this skip step is bypassed and screen population begins immediately from the current position

rules.rule_name: Clear All User Display Rows Before Loading New Page Data
rules.rule_description: Before populating the screen with new user records, all 10 display rows must be cleared to spaces to prevent stale data from a previous page from remaining visible on the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear all 10 user rows on screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The browse is open and the system is ready to populate the user list screen with new page data, and no end-of-file condition or error has been encountered
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to load user records into the display rows
acceptance_criteria.Then: All 10 user display rows on the screen are cleared — each row's User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type fields are set to spaces — ensuring no residual data from a prior page is displayed

rules.rule_name: Read Up to 10 User Records Sequentially for Page Display
rules.rule_description: The system reads user records sequentially from the User Security file, one at a time, and populates the screen rows until either 10 rows are filled, the end of the file is reached, or an error occurs.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Read next user record
from User Security File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen rows have been cleared and the system is ready to populate the user list with records from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The system iterates through the User Security file reading records forward
acceptance_criteria.Then: For each successfully retrieved record (record found and no errors), the system populates the corresponding screen row and advances the row counter by 1; the reading loop continues until all 10 rows are filled (row counter reaches 11) or the end of the file is reached or an error is encountered — whichever occurs first

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Row with User Record Data
rules.rule_description: Each successfully read user record is mapped to the corresponding screen display row, filling in the User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type fields for that row position.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Populate screen row with
User ID, First Name,
Last Name, User Type

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully read from the User Security file with no errors
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the screen row corresponding to the current row index (1 through 10)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type from the retrieved user record are placed into the matching fields of the screen row at the current row position (rows 1 through 10)

rules.rule_name: Store First User ID on Page for Backward Navigation Anchor
rules.rule_description: When the first row (row 1) of the page is populated, the User ID of that record is saved as the 'First User on Page' anchor. This value is used as the starting position when the user navigates backward to the previous page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Store User ID as
First User on Page
if this is row 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user record is being populated into the screen display rows
acceptance_criteria.When: The current row being populated is row 1 (the first row on the page)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID of the record being placed in row 1 is saved as the First User on Page anchor value (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST), in addition to being displayed in the User ID field of row 1 on the screen

rules.rule_name: Store Last User ID on Page for Forward Navigation Anchor
rules.rule_description: When the last row (row 10) of the page is populated, the User ID of that record is saved as the 'Last User on Page' anchor. This value is used as the starting position when the user navigates forward to the next page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Store User ID as
Last User on Page
if this is row 10

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user record is being populated into the screen display rows
acceptance_criteria.When: The current row being populated is row 10 (the last row on the page)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID of the record being placed in row 10 is saved as the Last User on Page anchor value (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-LAST), in addition to being displayed in the User ID field of row 10 on the screen

rules.rule_name: Increment Page Number When Records Are Successfully Loaded
rules.rule_description: After the reading loop completes, if at least one user record was successfully loaded (no end-of-file and no error condition), the current page number is incremented by 1 to reflect the newly displayed page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Were any records
successfully loaded?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The reading loop for populating the user list screen has completed
acceptance_criteria.When: The end-of-file condition has NOT been reached AND no error condition is active, meaning at least one user record was successfully loaded into the screen rows
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page number is incremented by 1 (Page Number = Page Number + 1) to reflect the page now being displayed

rules.rule_name: Increment Page Number When Partial Records Loaded at End of File
rules.rule_description: When the reading loop ends due to end-of-file or an error, but at least one record was loaded (row index advanced beyond 1), the page number is still incremented by 1 to correctly reflect the partial page being displayed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Were any records
successfully loaded?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The reading loop for populating the user list screen has completed due to end-of-file or an error condition
acceptance_criteria.When: The row index counter is greater than 1, indicating that at least one user record was successfully loaded before the end-of-file or error was encountered
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page number is incremented by 1 (Page Number = Page Number + 1) to reflect the partial page now being displayed; if the row index is exactly 1 (no records were loaded at all), the page number is not incremented

rules.rule_name: Determine Whether a Next Page of Users Exists
rules.rule_description: After successfully loading up to 10 records and incrementing the page number, the system attempts to read one additional record beyond the current page to determine whether more users exist. This controls whether the PF8 (next page) navigation option is available.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Attempt to read
one additional record

acceptance_criteria.Given: At least one user record was successfully loaded into the screen rows and the page number has been incremented
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to read one additional record beyond the 10 displayed records
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the additional record is found successfully (no end-of-file and no error), the Next Page flag is set to YES indicating more users are available and PF8 navigation is enabled; if no additional record exists (end-of-file is reached), the Next Page flag is set to NO indicating the current page is the last page and PF8 navigation is disabled

rules.rule_name: Set Next Page Flag to NO When No Records Are Loaded
rules.rule_description: When no user records are loaded at all during the forward page read (end-of-file was reached immediately or an error occurred before any record was populated), the Next Page flag is set to NO, disabling further forward navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Next Page Flag = NO
No more users available

acceptance_criteria.Given: The reading loop for populating the user list screen has completed
acceptance_criteria.When: No user records were successfully loaded — either the end-of-file condition was reached before any record was read, or an error occurred — AND the row index counter did not advance beyond 1
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Next Page flag is set to NO, indicating there are no more users available beyond the current position and PF8 forward navigation is disabled

rules.rule_name: Close Browse, Update Page Number, and Display User List Screen
rules.rule_description: After all page data has been loaded and navigation flags have been set, the system closes the browse on the User Security file, updates the page number displayed on the screen, clears the User ID search input field, and sends the refreshed user list screen to the administrator.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Close Browse on
User Security File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The forward page data loading process has completed — records have been read, screen rows populated, page number computed, and the Next Page flag has been set
acceptance_criteria.When: The system finalizes the forward page load operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The browse on the User Security file is closed; the computed page number is moved to the page number display field on the screen; the User ID search input field on the screen is cleared to a space; and the updated user list screen is sent to the administrator displaying the current page of users with the correct page number

sub_functionalities.title: Navigation source check: Enter, PF7, or PF3 key pressed? → If PF8 or First Load: skip one record forward by reading next record to advance past current boundary position → If Enter/PF7/PF3: proceed directly to clear rows and load
