rules.rule_name: Open User List Browse from Specified Starting Position
rules.rule_description: When a forward page load is triggered, the system opens a browse session on the User Security File starting at the User ID that was specified as the boundary position, enabling sequential forward reading of user records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Open Browse on User Security File
Starting at specified User ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: A forward page load has been triggered (by Enter, PF7, PF8, or First Load), and a starting User ID boundary position has been set (either a specific User ID entered by the user, LOW-VALUES for start of file, or the last User ID from the current page)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system initiates the forward page data loading process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system opens a browse session on the User Security File positioned at the specified starting User ID, making records available for sequential forward reading from that position onward

rules.rule_name: Determine Record Skip Requirement Based on Navigation Key
rules.rule_description: The system evaluates which navigation key triggered the forward page load to determine whether the browse position needs to advance past the current boundary record before loading the page, or whether it is already at the correct starting position.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Which key triggered
forward page load?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A browse session has been successfully opened on the User Security File at the specified starting User ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the navigation key that triggered the forward page load
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the triggering key was PF8 (Next Page) or First Load (any key other than Enter, PF7, or PF3), the system proceeds to skip one record forward to advance past the boundary position; if the triggering key was Enter, PF7, or PF3, the system proceeds directly to check record availability without skipping any record

rules.rule_name: Skip One Record Forward to Advance Past Boundary Position
rules.rule_description: When the forward page load is triggered by PF8 (Next Page) or First Load, the system reads and discards one record to advance the browse cursor past the current boundary User ID, ensuring the new page begins with the record immediately following the boundary position.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Skip one record forward
Advance past current boundary position

acceptance_criteria.Given: A browse session is open on the User Security File, and the forward page load was triggered by PF8 (Next Page) or by First Load (i.e., the triggering key was not Enter, PF7, or PF3)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines it must advance past the current boundary position
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system reads the next record from the User Security File (READNEXT), advancing the browse cursor one position forward past the boundary User ID; this record is not displayed but serves only to reposition the browse cursor so the subsequent page load begins at the correct next record

rules.rule_name: Verify Record Availability Before Loading Page Data
rules.rule_description: After positioning the browse cursor (with or without skipping), the system checks whether any user records are available to be loaded onto the screen before proceeding to clear and populate the display rows.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
More records
available?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The browse cursor has been positioned either directly at the starting User ID (Enter/PF7/PF3 path) or advanced one record past the boundary (PF8/First Load path)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether more user records are available at the current browse position
acceptance_criteria.Then: If records are available (end-of-file has not been reached and no error condition exists), the system proceeds to clear all 10 user display rows and load the next page of users; if no records are available (end-of-file reached), the system ends the forward page load with no records to display and the screen rows remain as previously shown

rules.rule_name: Clear All Ten User Display Rows Before Loading New Page
rules.rule_description: Before populating the screen with the new page of user records, the system clears all 10 display rows (User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type) to spaces, ensuring no stale data from the previous page remains visible when fewer than 10 records are available for the new page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
18: Clear all 10 user rows
on screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: Records are confirmed to be available for the new page (end-of-file not reached and no error condition), and the system is about to load a new set of user records onto the screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the display rows for the new page of user data
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system clears all 10 user display rows by setting the following fields to spaces for each row 1 through 10: User ID (USRID01I–USRID10I), First Name (FNAME01I–FNAME10I), Last Name (LNAME01I–LNAME10I), and User Type (UTYPE01I–UTYPE10I), after which the system proceeds to load the available user records into the now-empty rows

rules.rule_name: Open User Security File Browse for Backward Navigation
rules.rule_description: When navigating backward through the user list, the system opens a browse session on the User Security File starting at the first User ID displayed on the current page, so that records can be read in reverse order from that position.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Open browse on User Security File starting at first User ID of current page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF7 to navigate to the previous page, and the first User ID of the current page is available in the session state (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST)
acceptance_criteria.When: The backward page loading process begins and the system attempts to open a browse on the User Security File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The browse is opened starting at the first User ID of the current page as the starting key; if the first User ID is blank or empty, the browse starts at LOW-VALUES (beginning of file)

rules.rule_name: Handle Browse Open Failure on User Security File
rules.rule_description: If the User Security File cannot be opened for browsing during backward navigation, the system sets an error flag and displays an error message to the user, halting the page loading process.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Browse opened successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has attempted to open a browse on the User Security File for backward navigation
acceptance_criteria.When: The browse open operation fails due to an unexpected condition (not a normal response and not a record-not-found response)
acceptance_criteria.Then: An error flag is set to ON, the message 'Unable to lookup User...' is displayed on the screen, the cursor is positioned on the User ID input field, and no further backward page loading is performed

rules.rule_name: Skip Boundary Record to Reposition Browse for Backward Read
rules.rule_description: When navigating backward and the action was not triggered by ENTER or PF8, the system reads one record backward to move past the current boundary record and correctly position the browse cursor before filling the page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Skip current boundary record by reading one record backward to reposition correctly

acceptance_criteria.Given: The browse on the User Security File has been successfully opened at the first User ID of the current page
acceptance_criteria.When: The key pressed was not ENTER and not PF8 (i.e., it was PF7)
acceptance_criteria.Then: One record is read backward (READPREV) to skip the boundary record and reposition the browse cursor so that the next backward reads will return the correct previous page records

rules.rule_name: Clear All User Display Rows Before Populating Backward Page
rules.rule_description: Before populating the screen with the previous page of users, all 10 display rows are cleared to spaces to ensure no stale data from the previous screen state is shown.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Clear all 10 user rows on screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The browse has been successfully opened and the boundary record has been skipped if required, and no end-of-file condition has been reached and no error flag is set
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to load the previous page of user records
acceptance_criteria.Then: All 10 user display rows on the screen are cleared — each row's User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type fields are set to spaces

rules.rule_name: Initialize Row Index for Bottom-Up Screen Population
rules.rule_description: Because records are read in reverse order, the screen is filled from the bottom row (row 10) upward to row 1, so the displayed list appears in correct ascending order after backward navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set row index to 10 - Start filling from bottom row

acceptance_criteria.Given: All 10 user display rows have been cleared and the system is ready to populate the screen with backward-read records
acceptance_criteria.When: The backward page population loop is initialized
acceptance_criteria.Then: The row index is set to 10, meaning the first record read will be placed in row 10, and subsequent records will fill rows 9, 8, 7... down to row 1

rules.rule_name: Backward Record Read Loop Continuation Condition
rules.rule_description: The system continues reading user records backward and populating screen rows as long as there are more rows to fill (row index greater than 0) and no end-of-file or error condition has been encountered.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Row index greater than 0 AND more records exist?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The backward page population loop is active
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether to continue reading the next backward record
acceptance_criteria.Then: The loop continues only if the row index is greater than 0 AND the end-of-file flag is not set AND the error flag is not set; if any of these conditions fails, the loop exits

rules.rule_name: Read Previous User Record from User Security File
rules.rule_description: Within the backward navigation loop, the system reads the previous user record from the User Security File to retrieve the user's details for display on the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read previous user record from User Security File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The backward page population loop is active and the row index is greater than 0 with no error or end-of-file condition
acceptance_criteria.When: The system reads the previous record from the User Security File
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the read is successful, the record containing User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type is available for display; if the end of file (top of file) is reached, the end-of-file flag is set and the message 'You have reached the top of the page...' is displayed; if an unexpected error occurs, the error flag is set and 'Unable to lookup User...' is displayed

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Row with User Record Data
rules.rule_description: Each successfully read user record is mapped to the corresponding screen display row, showing the user's ID, first name, last name, and user type.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Populate screen row with User ID, First Name, Last Name, User Type

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully read from the User Security File during backward navigation
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the screen row corresponding to the current row index
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type from the record are placed into the screen fields for that row number (1 through 10); when row index is 1, the User ID is also saved as the 'First User on Page'; when row index is 10, the User ID is also saved as the 'Last User on Page'

rules.rule_name: Decrement Row Index After Each Backward Record Population
rules.rule_description: After populating a screen row with a user record, the row index is decremented by 1 to move upward to the next row, ensuring records are displayed in correct ascending order.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Move to next row upward - Decrement row index by 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully populated into the current screen row during backward navigation
acceptance_criteria.When: The system moves to the next iteration of the backward population loop
acceptance_criteria.Then: The row index is decremented by 1 (e.g., from 10 to 9, then 9 to 8, continuing until row index reaches 0 or no more records exist)

rules.rule_name: Check for Additional Previous Records Beyond Current Page
rules.rule_description: After filling the 10 display rows, the system attempts one additional backward read to determine whether there are more user records before the current page, which determines whether further backward navigation (PF7) will be available.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Attempt one additional backward read to check if previous page exists

acceptance_criteria.Given: The backward page population loop has completed (either 10 rows filled or end-of-file reached) and no error flag is set and no end-of-file flag is set
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs one additional backward read on the User Security File
acceptance_criteria.Then: If a record is found, it confirms that previous records exist beyond the current page; if end-of-file is reached, it confirms the user is at the top of the list

rules.rule_name: Decrement Page Number When Previous Records Exist
rules.rule_description: When the system confirms that previous records exist and the current page number is greater than 1, the page number is decremented by 1 to reflect the user moving to the previous page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Previous records exist beyond current page? / Current page number greater than 1? / Decrement page number by 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The additional backward read confirmed that previous records exist beyond the current page, and the NEXT-PAGE-YES flag is set
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the current page number is greater than 1
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the current page number is greater than 1, the page number is decremented by 1; if the current page number is not greater than 1, the page number is set to 1

rules.rule_name: Set Page Number to 1 When Top of List is Reached
rules.rule_description: When no previous records exist beyond the current page (top of the user list has been reached), the page number is set to 1 to indicate the user is on the first page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set page number to 1 - Top of list reached

acceptance_criteria.Given: The additional backward read found no more previous records (end-of-file at top of list), OR the current page number is already 1 or less
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines the page number for the displayed page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The page number is set to 1, indicating the user is viewing the first page of the user list

rules.rule_name: Close Browse on User Security File After Backward Page Load
rules.rule_description: After all backward page data loading and page number adjustments are complete, the browse session on the User Security File is closed to release the file resource.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Close browse on User Security File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The backward page population and page number adjustment have been completed
acceptance_criteria.When: The system finalizes the backward page loading process
acceptance_criteria.Then: The browse session on the User Security File is closed

rules.rule_name: Update Page Number Display on Screen
rules.rule_description: After completing the backward page load and closing the browse, the current page number is moved to the screen's page number display field so the user can see which page they are viewing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Update page number on screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The browse has been closed and the page number has been adjusted
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to display the updated user list screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is placed into the page number display field (PAGENUMI) on the screen

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Header with Current Date, Time and Program Information
rules.rule_description: Before displaying the user list screen, the header section is populated with the application titles, current date, current time, transaction ID, and program name to provide context to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 23: Populate Screen Header - Title, Date, Time, Program Info

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is preparing to send the user list screen to the user after backward page loading
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen header population routine is executed
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen header is populated with: Application Title 1, Application Title 2, the current Transaction ID, the current Program Name, the current date formatted as MM/DD/YY, and the current time formatted as HH:MM:SS

rules.rule_name: Display Updated User List with Previous Page Records
rules.rule_description: After populating all screen data including user rows, page number, and header, the updated user list screen is sent to the user displaying the previous page of user records.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 24: Display updated user list with previous page records

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen has been populated with the previous page user records, the page number has been updated, and the header information has been populated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the user list screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the SEND-ERASE flag is YES, the screen is sent with a full erase (clearing the entire screen before display); if the SEND-ERASE flag is NO, the screen is sent as an overlay without erasing; any error or informational message is displayed in the message field on the screen

rules.rule_name: Preserve Session State for Next User Interaction
rules.rule_description: After displaying the updated user list, the session state including page number, first and last user IDs on the page, navigation flags, and selected user information is preserved in the communication area so the next user interaction can continue from the correct state.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 27: Preserve session state for next interaction

acceptance_criteria.Given: The updated user list screen has been sent to the user after backward navigation
acceptance_criteria.When: The program returns control to the CICS transaction manager
acceptance_criteria.Then: The communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) containing the current page number, first User ID on page, last User ID on page, next-page availability flag, selected user ID, selection flag, and program context is passed back to CICS with the current transaction ID, so the session state is available for the next user interaction

sub_functionalities.title: Navigation source check: Enter or PF8 key pressed? → If PF7: skip current boundary record by reading one record backward to reposition correctly → If Enter/PF8: proceed directly to clear rows and load in reverse

rules.rule_name: Backward Page Navigation Repositioning Based on Key Pressed
rules.rule_description: When navigating backward through the user list, the system determines whether to skip the current boundary record before loading the previous page. If the user pressed PF7, the system reads one record backward to reposition past the current boundary user, ensuring the correct set of previous users is loaded. If the user pressed Enter or PF8, no repositioning is needed and the system proceeds directly to load the previous page data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 17.1: Navigation Source Check: Enter or PF8 key pressed? → If PF7: skip current boundary record by reading one record backward to reposition correctly → If Enter/PF8: proceed directly to clear rows and load in reverse

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has successfully opened a browse session on the User Security file starting at the current boundary User ID, and the backward page loading process has begun
acceptance_criteria.When: The navigation source is evaluated: (1) The user pressed PF7 to navigate backward, OR (2) The user pressed Enter or PF8 which triggered a backward page load
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the user pressed PF7: the system reads one record backward from the current boundary position to skip past the boundary record and correctly reposition the file cursor before loading the previous page of users; If the user pressed Enter or PF8: the system skips the repositioning step entirely and proceeds directly to clear all 10 user display rows and load the previous page data in reverse order

rules.rule_name: Clear All User List Display Rows Before Loading New Page Data
rules.rule_description: Before displaying a new page of users on the User List screen, all 10 display rows must be completely blanked out — clearing User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type for every row. This ensures no stale data from a previous page remains visible when the new page is rendered, whether navigating forward or backward through the user directory.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Screen Row Initialization - Clear all 10 user rows on the screen (user ID, first name, last name, user type) before populating with new data.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is about to be refreshed with a new page of user data, either as a result of an initial load, a forward page navigation (PF8 / Enter), or a backward page navigation (PF7), AND the file browse has been successfully opened without errors (no error flag is set), AND all 10 display rows (rows 1 through 10) currently contain data from the previous page or from a prior session
acceptance_criteria.When: The system begins the process of populating the User List screen with new user records retrieved from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.Then: For each of the 10 display rows (row 1 through row 10), the system must clear the following four fields to blank spaces before any new data is written: (1) User ID field for that row, (2) First Name field for that row, (3) Last Name field for that row, (4) User Type field for that row — such that after initialization all 10 rows are completely empty and ready to receive fresh user data from the current page read

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Row 1 with User Record and Track First User ID
rules.rule_description: When the first user record is being placed on the user list screen, all user details are displayed in row 1 and the User ID is saved as the anchor point for backward pagination.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Row 1:
Populate User ID, First Name,
Last Name, User Type
⭐ Save User ID as
FIRST User ID for pagination

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user record has been retrieved from the User Security file and the current screen row index (WS-IDX) is 1
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates screen row 1 with the retrieved user record details
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID is displayed in row 1 of the screen, the First Name is displayed in row 1, the Last Name is displayed in row 1, the User Type is displayed in row 1, AND the User ID is additionally saved as the FIRST User ID on the page (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST) to serve as the backward navigation anchor point for PF7 pagination

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Rows 2 through 9 with User Record Details
rules.rule_description: When user records are being placed in the middle rows of the user list screen (rows 2 through 9), all user details are displayed without any additional pagination tracking.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Rows 2 to 9:
Populate User ID, First Name,
Last Name, User Type

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user record has been retrieved from the User Security file and the current screen row index (WS-IDX) is any value from 2 to 9 inclusive
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates the corresponding screen row with the retrieved user record details
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID is displayed in the corresponding row of the screen, the First Name is displayed in the corresponding row, the Last Name is displayed in the corresponding row, and the User Type is displayed in the corresponding row. No pagination anchor values are updated.

rules.rule_name: Populate Screen Row 10 with User Record and Track Last User ID
rules.rule_description: When the tenth user record is being placed on the user list screen, all user details are displayed in row 10 and the User ID is saved as the anchor point for forward pagination.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Row 10:
Populate User ID, First Name,
Last Name, User Type
⭐ Save User ID as
LAST User ID for pagination

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user record has been retrieved from the User Security file and the current screen row index (WS-IDX) is 10
acceptance_criteria.When: The system populates screen row 10 with the retrieved user record details
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID is displayed in row 10 of the screen, the First Name is displayed in row 10, the Last Name is displayed in row 10, the User Type is displayed in row 10, AND the User ID is additionally saved as the LAST User ID on the page (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-LAST) to serve as the forward navigation anchor point for PF8 pagination

rules.rule_name: No Action for Out-of-Range Screen Row Index
rules.rule_description: When the row index falls outside the valid range of 1 to 10, no user data is populated and no screen fields are updated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Any other row index:
No action taken

acceptance_criteria.Given: A user record has been retrieved from the User Security file and the current screen row index (WS-IDX) is any value other than 1 through 10
acceptance_criteria.When: The system attempts to populate a screen row with the retrieved user record details
acceptance_criteria.Then: No screen fields are updated, no user data is displayed, and no pagination anchor values are modified. The record is effectively skipped.

rules.rule_name: Reset Page Number to Zero Before New Search or Enter Key Navigation
rules.rule_description: When the user presses the Enter key or initiates a new user list search, the page number counter must be reset to zero before loading begins, so that the first page of results is correctly numbered as page 1 after the forward page load increments it.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Reset Page Number to 0 Before Loading

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen and has pressed the Enter key, optionally entering a User ID in the search field to filter the list
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the Enter key action and prepares to load the user list
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is reset to 0 before any records are read, ensuring the subsequent page increment results in page number 1 for the first page of results

rules.rule_name: Increment Page Number When a Full Page of Users Is Successfully Loaded
rules.rule_description: When navigating forward through the user list and a full page of 10 users is loaded with more records still available beyond the current page, the page number is incremented by 1 to reflect the newly displayed page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Increment Page Number by 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has opened a browse on the User Security file and is loading records in the forward direction
acceptance_criteria.When: All 10 user rows on the screen have been populated and at least one additional user record exists beyond the current page (end-of-file has NOT been reached and no errors occurred)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is incremented by 1, the next-page indicator is set to YES (PF8 enabled), and the updated page number is displayed on the screen

rules.rule_name: Increment Page Number When a Partial Page of Users Is Loaded
rules.rule_description: When navigating forward through the user list and fewer than 10 users are loaded because the end of the user directory has been reached, but at least one user record was read, the page number is still incremented by 1 to reflect the partial page being displayed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Increment Page Number by 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has opened a browse on the User Security file and is loading records in the forward direction
acceptance_criteria.When: The end of the user file is reached before filling all 10 rows, but at least one user record was successfully read and populated on the screen (the internal row index WS-IDX is greater than 1)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is incremented by 1, the next-page indicator is set to NO (PF8 disabled), and the updated page number is displayed on the screen

rules.rule_name: Keep Page Number Unchanged When No User Records Are Loaded
rules.rule_description: When navigating forward through the user list and no user records are found at all (e.g., the search key is beyond all existing records), the page number remains unchanged and is not incremented.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Keep Page Number Unchanged

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has opened a browse on the User Security file and is loading records in the forward direction
acceptance_criteria.When: The end of the user file is reached immediately without reading any user records (the internal row index WS-IDX remains at 1, meaning no records were populated)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is NOT incremented and remains at its current value, the next-page indicator is set to NO (PF8 disabled), and the unchanged page number is displayed on the screen

rules.rule_name: Decrement Page Number When Navigating Backward to a Previous Page
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF7 to navigate backward and a previous page of users exists, the page number is decremented by 1 to reflect the page being navigated back to.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Decrement Page Number by 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF7 to navigate backward, the system has successfully loaded 10 user records in the backward direction, and an attempt to read one more record backward was made
acceptance_criteria.When: The backward read confirms that more records exist before the current page (end-of-file not reached, no errors), AND the current page number is greater than 1
acceptance_criteria.Then: The page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is decremented by 1, and the updated page number is displayed on the screen

rules.rule_name: Set Page Number to 1 When Backward Navigation Reaches the First Page
rules.rule_description: When navigating backward and the system determines that no further previous records exist or the page number is already at 1, the page number is explicitly set to 1 to ensure the display correctly reflects the first page of the user list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Page Number to 1 Already at First Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF7 to navigate backward and the system has loaded user records in the backward direction
acceptance_criteria.When: Either the backward read reaches the beginning of the user file (end-of-file condition), an error occurs during the backward read, OR the current page number is already 1 or less
acceptance_criteria.Then: The page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is set to 1 (not decremented), and the page number value of 1 is displayed on the screen, indicating the user is on the first page

rules.rule_name: Display Updated Page Number on Screen After Forward Navigation
rules.rule_description: After completing any forward page load operation (triggered by Enter key or PF8), the current page number must be displayed on the User List screen so the user knows which page they are viewing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Updated Page Number on Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed loading user records in the forward direction (either full page, partial page, or no records) and the page number has been computed accordingly
acceptance_criteria.When: The User List screen is being prepared for display after a forward navigation action (Enter key or PF8)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The computed page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is moved to the page number display field (PAGENUMI) on the User List screen, and the screen is sent to the user showing the correct page number

rules.rule_name: Display Updated Page Number on Screen After Backward Navigation
rules.rule_description: After completing any backward page load operation (triggered by PF7), the current page number must be displayed on the User List screen so the user knows which page they are viewing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display Updated Page Number on Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed loading user records in the backward direction and the page number has been decremented or set to 1 accordingly
acceptance_criteria.When: The User List screen is being prepared for display after a backward navigation action (PF7)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The computed page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is moved to the page number display field (PAGENUMI) on the User List screen, and the screen is sent to the user showing the correct page number

    I[Increment Page Number by 1]

    E -->|No - End of user list| G

rules.rule_name: Determine If Current Page Was Fully Populated
rules.rule_description: After attempting to load up to 10 user records onto the current page, the system evaluates whether all 10 rows were successfully filled and no errors occurred, to decide the appropriate page-number and next-page-availability logic.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Were all 10 rows successfully populated?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed reading user records from the User Security file to populate the current page, and the loop to fill up to 10 rows has ended
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether the end-of-file condition has NOT been reached AND no error condition is active (i.e., all 10 rows were successfully populated)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If both conditions are true (not end-of-file AND no error), the page is considered fully loaded and the system proceeds to increment the page number and probe for additional records; otherwise the system evaluates whether any partial records were loaded

rules.rule_name: Increment Page Number When Full Page Is Loaded
rules.rule_description: When a full page of 10 user records has been successfully loaded without reaching end-of-file or encountering an error, the current page number is incremented by 1 to reflect the newly displayed page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Increment Page Number by 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current page has been fully populated with 10 user records (end-of-file not reached and no error active)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system confirms the full-page condition is met
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is incremented by exactly 1, resulting in CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM = CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM + 1

rules.rule_name: Probe Read to Detect Additional Records Beyond Current Page
rules.rule_description: After a full page of 10 users is loaded and the page number is incremented, the system attempts to read one additional record from the User Security file solely to determine whether more users exist beyond the current page, without displaying that record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Attempt to Read One Additional Record from User File

acceptance_criteria.Given: A full page of 10 user records has been loaded and the page number has been incremented
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs one additional sequential forward read (READNEXT) on the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The result of this read (whether a record was found or end-of-file was reached) is used exclusively to set the next-page availability flag; the record itself is not displayed to the user

rules.rule_name: Set Next Page Available Flag When Additional Record Exists
rules.rule_description: If the probe read after loading a full page successfully retrieves an additional record (end-of-file not reached and no error), the system marks that a next page is available, enabling the user to navigate forward.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Next Page Flag = YES
More users exist beyond current page

acceptance_criteria.Given: A full page of 10 user records has been loaded and a probe read was performed on the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The probe read returns a valid record (end-of-file condition is NOT set AND no error is active)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Next Page flag is set to YES (NEXT-PAGE-YES), indicating that more user records exist beyond the current page and forward navigation (PF8) is available

rules.rule_name: Set Next Page Unavailable Flag When No Additional Record Exists After Full Page
rules.rule_description: If the probe read after loading a full page reaches end-of-file or encounters an error, the system marks that no further pages are available, disabling forward navigation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Next Page Flag = NO
Current page is the last page

acceptance_criteria.Given: A full page of 10 user records has been loaded and a probe read was performed on the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The probe read does NOT return a valid record (end-of-file condition IS set OR an error is active)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Next Page flag is set to NO (NEXT-PAGE-NO), indicating the current page is the last page and forward navigation (PF8) will be disabled with the message 'You are already at the bottom of the page...'

rules.rule_name: Determine If Any Records Were Loaded on a Partial Page
rules.rule_description: When the page was not fully populated (end-of-file was reached or an error occurred before filling all 10 rows), the system checks whether at least one record was loaded by evaluating if the row index advanced beyond its starting value of 1.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Were any records loaded on this page?
Row Index greater than 1?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The page loading loop ended before filling all 10 rows (end-of-file was reached or an error occurred), meaning the full-page condition was not met
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the current row index (WS-IDX) is greater than 1
acceptance_criteria.Then: If WS-IDX is greater than 1, at least one user record was loaded and the system proceeds to increment the page number before setting Next Page flag to NO; if WS-IDX is not greater than 1, no records were loaded and the system sets Next Page flag to NO without incrementing the page number

rules.rule_name: Increment Page Number When Partial Page Has At Least One Record
rules.rule_description: When the page was only partially populated (fewer than 10 records loaded) but at least one record was successfully loaded, the page number is still incremented by 1 to reflect the partial page being displayed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Increment Page Number by 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The page loading loop ended before filling all 10 rows (partial or end-of-file condition), and the row index (WS-IDX) is greater than 1, confirming at least one user record was loaded
acceptance_criteria.When: The system confirms that WS-IDX > 1 on a partial page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is incremented by exactly 1, resulting in CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM = CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM + 1

rules.rule_name: Set Next Page Unavailable Flag for Partial or Empty Page
rules.rule_description: Whenever the current page is not fully populated — whether it contains some records or no records at all — the system unconditionally marks that no further pages are available beyond the current page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Next Page Flag = NO
No further pages available

acceptance_criteria.Given: The page loading loop ended before filling all 10 rows, meaning end-of-file was reached or an error occurred during page loading (the full-page condition was not met)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes the partial or empty page outcome, regardless of whether WS-IDX is greater than 1 or not
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Next Page flag is set to NO (NEXT-PAGE-NO) unconditionally, indicating no further pages exist and forward navigation (PF8) will be disabled

sub_functionalities.title: Were all 10 rows successfully populated? → Yes: Increment page number by 1, attempt to read one additional record, if found set Next Page Flag YES else set Next Page Flag NO → No (partial page): check if row index greater than 1, if yes increment page number by 1 then set Next Page Flag NO, if no records at all set Next Page Flag NO without incrementing
sub_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([21.1: Determine Next Page Availability])
    B{Were all 10 rows\nsuccessfully populated?\nEnd of File NOT reached}
    C[Increment Page Number by 1]
    D[Attempt to read\none additional record]
    E{Additional record\nfound?}
    F[Set Next Page Flag\nto YES\nMore pages available]
    G[Set Next Page Flag\nto NO\nNo more pages]
    H{Was row index\ngreater than 1?\nAt least 1 record loaded}
    I[Increment Page Number by 1\nthen Set Next Page Flag to NO\nPartial page reached end]
    J[Set Next Page Flag to NO\nNo records loaded\nPage number unchanged]
    K([End: Next Page Status Determined])

    A --> B
    B -->|Yes - Full Page Loaded| C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E -->|Yes - Record Found| F
    E -->|No - End of File| G
    F --> K
    G --> K
    B -->|No - Partial or Empty Page| H
    H -->|Yes - At Least 1 Record| I
    H -->|No - Zero Records Loaded| J
    I --> K
    J --> K

rules.rule_name: Full Page Loaded – Increment Page Number
rules.rule_description: When all 10 user rows on the current page have been successfully populated from the User Security file without reaching the end of file, the current page number is incremented by 1 to reflect the newly loaded page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Were all 10 rows successfully populated? End of File NOT reached → Increment Page Number by 1

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is being populated in a forward page navigation, the row index has reached 11 (all 10 rows filled), and the end of the User Security file has NOT been reached
acceptance_criteria.When: The system determines that a full page of 10 user records was successfully loaded
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is incremented by 1

rules.rule_name: Full Page Loaded – Attempt to Read Additional Record to Determine Next Page Availability
rules.rule_description: After a full page of 10 users is loaded and the page number is incremented, the system attempts to read one additional record from the User Security file solely to determine whether a next page of users exists, without displaying that record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Attempt to read one additional record

acceptance_criteria.Given: All 10 user rows have been successfully populated and the page number has been incremented by 1
acceptance_criteria.When: The system performs a forward read of one additional record from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The result of this read (record found or end of file) is used exclusively to set the Next Page availability flag, and the record itself is not displayed on screen

rules.rule_name: Additional Record Found – Enable Next Page Navigation
rules.rule_description: If an additional record is successfully read from the User Security file after a full page of 10 users is loaded, the Next Page flag is set to YES, indicating that more users are available and the PF8 (page forward) navigation should be enabled.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Additional record found? → Yes - Record Found → Set Next Page Flag to YES, More pages available

acceptance_criteria.Given: All 10 user rows have been populated, the page number has been incremented, and an attempt to read one additional record from the User Security file is made
acceptance_criteria.When: The additional record read is successful (a record is found beyond the current page)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Next Page Flag (NEXT-PAGE-YES) is set to TRUE, indicating more pages of users are available for forward navigation

rules.rule_name: No Additional Record Found – Disable Next Page Navigation
rules.rule_description: If no additional record is found after a full page of 10 users is loaded (end of file is reached), the Next Page flag is set to NO, indicating that the current page is the last page and PF8 (page forward) navigation should be disabled.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Additional record found? → No - End of File → Set Next Page Flag to NO, No more pages

acceptance_criteria.Given: All 10 user rows have been populated, the page number has been incremented, and an attempt to read one additional record from the User Security file is made
acceptance_criteria.When: The additional record read reaches the end of the User Security file (no further records exist)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Next Page Flag (NEXT-PAGE-NO) is set to TRUE, indicating no more pages of users are available and forward navigation is disabled

rules.rule_name: Partial Page Loaded – Increment Page Number and Disable Next Page Navigation
rules.rule_description: When the end of the User Security file is reached before all 10 rows are filled, but at least 1 user record was loaded (row index advanced beyond its starting value of 1), the page number is incremented by 1 and the Next Page flag is set to NO, indicating this is the last partial page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No - Partial or Empty Page → Was row index greater than 1? At least 1 record loaded → Yes - At Least 1 Record → Increment Page Number by 1 then Set Next Page Flag to NO, Partial page reached end

acceptance_criteria.Given: A forward page navigation is in progress, the end of the User Security file was reached before 10 rows were filled, and the row index (WS-IDX) is greater than 1 indicating at least one user record was successfully loaded
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the partial page condition after the read loop exits due to end of file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is incremented by 1, AND the Next Page Flag (NEXT-PAGE-NO) is set to TRUE, indicating this partial page is the last page and no further forward navigation is possible

rules.rule_name: Zero Records Loaded – Disable Next Page Navigation Without Incrementing Page Number
rules.rule_description: When the end of the User Security file is reached immediately with no user records loaded at all (row index remains at its initial value of 1, meaning it never advanced), the Next Page flag is set to NO and the page number is left unchanged.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Was row index greater than 1? → No - Zero Records Loaded → Set Next Page Flag to NO, No records loaded, Page number unchanged

acceptance_criteria.Given: A forward page navigation is in progress, the end of the User Security file was reached before any rows were filled, and the row index (WS-IDX) is NOT greater than 1 (equals 1, meaning zero records were loaded)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the empty page condition after the read loop exits due to end of file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Next Page Flag (NEXT-PAGE-NO) is set to TRUE indicating no forward navigation is possible, AND the current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) remains unchanged (is NOT incremented)

rules.rule_name: Populate Full User Details on Screen Rows 2 Through 9

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is populating user records onto the User List screen and the current record is assigned to any screen row between 2 and 9 (inclusive)

acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID (SEC-USR-ID), First Name (SEC-USR-FNAME), Last Name (SEC-USR-LNAME), and User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE) must be stored in the corresponding screen row display fields (USRIDnnI, FNAMEnnI, LNAMEnnI, UTYPEnnI where nn is the row number 02 through 09), and no pagination anchor value is updated

rules.rule_name: Save Last User ID as Forward Pagination Anchor When Populating Row 10

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is populating user records onto the User List screen and the current record being placed is assigned to screen row 10

rules.rule_name: Populate Full User Details on Screen Row 10

rules.rule_description: When populating the screen header, the system retrieves the current system date and time to be formatted and displayed on the User List screen.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is about to populate the User List screen header
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen header population process is triggered
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date and time and stores it in the working date/time data area (WS-CURDATE-DATA) for subsequent formatting and display

rules.rule_name: Set Application Title Lines on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The screen header must display two application title lines sourced from the application's common data area, identifying the application to the user.

Title Line 1 and Title Line 2

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen header population process is executing

acceptance_criteria.Then: Title Line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) is placed into the first title display field (TITLE01O) and Title Line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) is placed into the second title display field (TITLE02O) on the screen output area

rules.rule_name: Set Current Transaction ID on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The screen header must display the current transaction identifier so the user can identify which transaction is active during their session.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Transaction ID
on Screen Header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen header population process is executing and the current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is available
acceptance_criteria.When: The transaction ID is being set on the User List screen header
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is placed into the transaction name display field (TRNNAMEO) on the screen output area

rules.rule_name: Set Current Program Name on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: The screen header must display the current program name so the user can identify which program module is currently active.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Program Name
on Screen Header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The screen header population process is executing and the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is available
acceptance_criteria.When: The program name is being set on the User List screen header
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is placed into the program name display field (PGMNAMEO) on the screen output area

rules.rule_name: Format Current Date as MM/DD/YY for Screen Display
rules.rule_description: The current date retrieved from the system must be formatted into MM/DD/YY format before being displayed on the screen header. The year is represented as a 2-digit value extracted from the 4-digit year.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Format Current Date
as MM/DD/YY

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current system date has been retrieved and stored in the working date area (WS-CURDATE-DATA), containing separate month (WS-CURDATE-MONTH), day (WS-CURDATE-DAY), and 4-digit year (WS-CURDATE-YEAR) components
acceptance_criteria.When: The date is being formatted for screen header display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The month component (WS-CURDATE-MONTH) is moved to the MM position (WS-CURDATE-MM), the day component (WS-CURDATE-DAY) is moved to the DD position (WS-CURDATE-DD), and only the last 2 digits of the year (positions 3 and 4 of WS-CURDATE-YEAR) are moved to the YY position (WS-CURDATE-YY), producing a date in MM/DD/YY format (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY)

rules.rule_name: Set Formatted Date on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: After the current date has been formatted into MM/DD/YY format, it must be placed into the appropriate screen header display field for the user to see.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Formatted Date
on Screen Header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current date has been formatted into MM/DD/YY format and stored in WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY
acceptance_criteria.When: The formatted date is being set on the User List screen header
acceptance_criteria.Then: The formatted date (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) is placed into the current date display field (CURDATEO) on the screen output area

rules.rule_name: Format Current Time as HH:MM:SS for Screen Display
rules.rule_description: The current time retrieved from the system must be formatted into HH:MM:SS format before being displayed on the screen header, using separate hours, minutes, and seconds components.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Format Current Time
as HH:MM:SS

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current system time has been retrieved and stored in the working time area, containing separate hours (WS-CURTIME-HOURS), minutes (WS-CURTIME-MINUTE), and seconds (WS-CURTIME-SECOND) components
acceptance_criteria.When: The time is being formatted for screen header display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The hours component (WS-CURTIME-HOURS) is moved to the HH position (WS-CURTIME-HH), the minutes component (WS-CURTIME-MINUTE) is moved to the MM position (WS-CURTIME-MM), and the seconds component (WS-CURTIME-SECOND) is moved to the SS position (WS-CURTIME-SS), producing a time in HH:MM:SS format (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS)

rules.rule_name: Set Formatted Time on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: After the current time has been formatted into HH:MM:SS format, it must be placed into the appropriate screen header display field for the user to see.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Formatted Time
on Screen Header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current time has been formatted into HH:MM:SS format and stored in WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS
acceptance_criteria.When: The formatted time is being set on the User List screen header
acceptance_criteria.Then: The formatted time (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS) is placed into the current time display field (CURTIMEO) on the screen output area, completing the screen header population

key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:

rules.rule_name: Populate Application Titles on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: When preparing the User List screen for display, the system populates the screen header with the standard application titles defined in the common demo area.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
23: Populate Screen Header
Get current date and time / Set application title on screen header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is about to be sent to the terminal and the screen header needs to be populated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the screen header information
acceptance_criteria.Then: The first application title (CCDA-TITLE01) is placed in the TITLE01O field of the screen output area, and the second application title (CCDA-TITLE02) is placed in the TITLE02O field of the screen output area

rules.rule_name: Populate Transaction ID and Program Name on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: When preparing the User List screen for display, the system populates the screen header with the current transaction identifier and program name to provide context to the user.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Transaction ID and Program Name on header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is about to be sent to the terminal and the screen header needs to be populated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the transaction and program identification fields in the header
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is placed in the TRNNAMEO field of the screen output area, and the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is placed in the PGMNAMEO field of the screen output area

rules.rule_name: Format and Display Current Date on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: When preparing the User List screen for display, the system retrieves the current system date and formats it as MM/DD/YY before placing it in the screen header.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Format and set current date
MM/DD/YY on header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is about to be sent to the terminal and the screen header needs to be populated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system retrieves the current date using the system date function and formats it
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current date is extracted from the system, the month portion is placed in WS-CURDATE-MM, the day portion is placed in WS-CURDATE-DD, the last two digits of the year are placed in WS-CURDATE-YY, and the fully formatted date in MM/DD/YY format (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) is placed in the CURDATEO field of the screen output area

rules.rule_name: Format and Display Current Time on Screen Header
rules.rule_description: When preparing the User List screen for display, the system retrieves the current system time and formats it as HH:MM:SS before placing it in the screen header.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Format and set current time
HH:MM:SS on header

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is about to be sent to the terminal and the screen header needs to be populated
acceptance_criteria.When: The system retrieves the current time using the system date function and formats it
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current time is extracted from the system, the hours portion is placed in WS-CURTIME-HH, the minutes portion is placed in WS-CURTIME-MM, the seconds portion is placed in WS-CURTIME-SS, and the fully formatted time in HH:MM:SS format (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS) is placed in the CURTIMEO field of the screen output area

rules.rule_name: Display Message or Error Text on Screen
rules.rule_description: Before sending the User List screen to the terminal, any informational or error message that has been set during processing is placed in the screen's message display field so the user can see feedback about their last action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Move any message or error
text to screen message field

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is about to be sent to the terminal and a message may have been set during processing (e.g., invalid key, already at top/bottom of page, invalid selection, or unable to look up user)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the screen for display
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current value of WS-MESSAGE (which may contain an informational or error message, or spaces if no message) is moved to the ERRMSGO field of the screen output area (COUSR0AO), making it visible to the user on the screen

rules.rule_name: Send User List Screen with Full Screen Erase on First Display
rules.rule_description: When the User List screen is being displayed for the first time in a transaction cycle or after a fresh data load, the screen is sent to the terminal with a full erase to clear any previously displayed content before showing the new user list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is this a first-time display? / Send screen to terminal with full screen erase Showing up to 10 users with User ID, First Name, Last Name, User Type, Page Number and Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen header has been populated with titles, transaction ID, program name, current date, current time, and any message text, AND the Send-Erase flag (SEND-ERASE-YES) is set to TRUE indicating a first-time or fresh display
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the User List screen (map COUSR0A from mapset COUSR00) to the terminal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen is sent with the ERASE option, which clears the entire terminal screen before displaying the new content; the screen shows up to 10 users each with their User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type, along with the current page number and any message or error text, and the cursor is positioned at the User ID input field

rules.rule_name: Send User List Screen Without Erase for Subsequent Displays
rules.rule_description: When the User List screen is being refreshed or updated (not a first-time display), the screen is sent to the terminal without erasing the existing content, providing a smoother update experience.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Is this a first-time display? / Send screen to terminal without screen erase Showing up to 10 users with User ID, First Name, Last Name, User Type, Page Number and Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen header has been populated with titles, transaction ID, program name, current date, current time, and any message text, AND the Send-Erase flag (SEND-ERASE-YES) is set to FALSE (SEND-ERASE-NO) indicating a subsequent or overlay display
acceptance_criteria.When: The system sends the User List screen (map COUSR0A from mapset COUSR00) to the terminal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen is sent without the ERASE option, overlaying the existing terminal screen content with the updated user list; the screen shows up to 10 users each with their User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type, along with the current page number and any message or error text, and the cursor is positioned at the User ID input field

rules.rule_name: User List Screen Content Definition
rules.rule_description: The User List screen presents a paginated list of up to 10 users at a time, displaying key identifying and classification information for each user, along with navigation context and feedback messages.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Send screen to terminal with full screen erase
Showing up to 10 users with
User ID, First Name, Last Name,
User Type, Page Number and Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is being prepared for display after user records have been retrieved from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The screen content is assembled and sent to the terminal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The screen displays up to 10 user rows, where each row contains: User ID (USRID01I–USRID10I), First Name (FNAME01I–FNAME10I), Last Name (LNAME01I–LNAME10I), and User Type (UTYPE01I–UTYPE10I); the current page number (PAGENUMI) is shown; any rows without data are displayed as blank spaces; and a selection field (SEL0001I–SEL0010I) is available next to each user row for the user to enter an action code

key_functionalities.title: End of File Notification
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Page Forward Loading in Progress])
    B[Read Next User Record\nfrom User Security File]
    C{End of File\nReached?}
    D[Set EOF Flag ON]
    E[Set Message:\n'You have reached the\nbottom of the page...']
    F[Set Next Page\nIndicator to NO]
    G[Stop Reading\nMore Records]
    H[Display User List Screen\nwith Bottom-of-Page Message]
    I([End of File Notification Complete])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C -->|Yes - No More Records| D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G
    G --> H
    H --> I
    C -->|No - Record Found| I

rules.rule_name: Detect End of User List During Forward Page Navigation
rules.rule_description: When the system attempts to read the next user record during forward page loading and no more records exist in the User Security file, the system must detect this end-of-file condition and mark the list as fully traversed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: End of File Reached?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is loading users forward through the User Security file and has been reading user records sequentially
acceptance_criteria.When: A read-next operation on the User Security file returns an end-of-file condition, indicating no more user records exist beyond the current position
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the End-of-File (EOF) flag to TRUE, marking that the bottom of the user list has been reached and no further forward reads should be attempted

rules.rule_name: Display Bottom-of-Page Message When End of User List is Reached
rules.rule_description: When the end of the User Security file is encountered during forward page loading, the system must inform the user that they have reached the last available user record by displaying an appropriate notification message on the User List screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Message: 'You have reached the bottom of the page...'

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is performing a forward page load of the User List screen and the EOF flag has been set to TRUE because no more user records exist in the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The end-of-file condition is confirmed during the read-next operation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the screen message to 'You have reached the bottom of the page...' to notify the user that the end of the user list has been reached

rules.rule_name: Disable Forward Paging When End of User List is Reached
rules.rule_description: When the system detects that no more user records exist beyond the current page during forward navigation, the Next Page indicator must be set to NO to prevent the user from attempting to navigate further forward.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Next Page Indicator to NO

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has completed loading users for the current page during a forward page navigation and the EOF flag is TRUE (no more records exist) or an error condition is present
acceptance_criteria.When: The check for additional records beyond the current page confirms that the User Security file has no more records (EOF condition is active)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the Next Page indicator to NO, which will prevent PF8 (page forward) from loading another page and will display the bottom-of-page message if PF8 is pressed again

rules.rule_name: Display User List Screen with Bottom-of-Page Notification
rules.rule_description: When the end of the User Security file is reached during forward page loading, the system must immediately display the User List screen along with the bottom-of-page notification message so the user is aware they are viewing the last available users.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Display User List Screen with Bottom-of-Page Message

acceptance_criteria.Given: The EOF flag is set to TRUE during a forward read of the User Security file, and the message 'You have reached the bottom of the page...' has been set
acceptance_criteria.When: The end-of-file condition is detected during the read-next operation on the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system displays the User List screen (COUSR0A) with the bottom-of-page message 'You have reached the bottom of the page...' visible to the user, showing all user records that were successfully loaded before the end of file was reached

key_functionalities.title: Top of File Notification
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([Paging Backward - PF7 Pressed])
    B[Open Browse on User File\nStarting at First User ID of Current Page]
    C{User File Position\nFound?}
    D[Read Previous Record\nfrom User File]
    E{Record\nRetrieved?}
    F[Continue Reading Previous Records\nPopulate Screen Rows in Reverse]
    G{Top of User\nFile Reached?}
    H[Set End-of-File Indicator]
    I[Display Message:\n'You have reached the top of the page...']
    J[Display Updated\nUser List Screen]
    K[Set End-of-File Indicator]
    L[Display Message:\n'You are at the top of the page...']
    M[Display Updated\nUser List Screen]

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C -->|Not Found - Already at Top| K
    K --> L
    L --> M
    C -->|Found| D
    D --> E
    E -->|More Records Exist| F
    F --> G
    G -->|No - More Records Available| F
    G -->|Yes - Top of File Reached| H
    H --> I
    I --> J

rules.rule_name: Initiate Backward Paging from Current Page Position
rules.rule_description: When the user presses PF7 to page backward, the system determines the correct starting position in the user list. If the first user ID of the current page is available, browsing starts from that user ID; otherwise, browsing starts from the very beginning of the user list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Open Browse on User File
Starting at First User ID of Current Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing the User List screen and the current page number is greater than 1
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF7 to navigate to the previous page
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the first User ID of the current page is blank or empty, the system sets the browse start position to the beginning of the user list (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the system sets the browse start position to the first User ID displayed on the current page, and then opens a browse session on the User Security file starting at that position

rules.rule_name: Already at Top of List - PF7 Blocked
rules.rule_description: When the user attempts to page backward but is already on page 1, the system prevents further backward navigation and informs the user they are at the top of the list.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Open Browse on User File
Starting at First User ID of Current Page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is viewing the User List screen and the current page number is 1
acceptance_criteria.When: The user presses PF7 to navigate to the previous page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system does not attempt backward navigation, displays the message 'You are already at the top of the page...' on the screen, and refreshes the current screen without erasing it

rules.rule_name: User File Browse Start Position Not Found - Top of List Notification
rules.rule_description: When the system attempts to open a browse session on the User Security file starting at the specified User ID but the position is not found, it means the system is already at or beyond the top of the user list. The user is notified accordingly.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Not Found - Already at Top

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has initiated a backward page navigation and attempts to open a browse session on the User Security file at the specified starting User ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The User Security file browse position is not found (the specified User ID does not exist in the file)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the end-of-file indicator to TRUE, displays the message 'You are at the top of the page...' on the screen, and sends the updated User List screen to the user

rules.rule_name: Skip One Record Backward Before Populating Previous Page
rules.rule_description: When navigating backward and the action was not triggered by ENTER or PF8, the system skips one record backward before beginning to populate the screen. This ensures the correct set of 10 records is displayed for the previous page.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Read Previous Record
from User File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has successfully opened a browse session on the User Security file for backward navigation
acceptance_criteria.When: The key pressed was not ENTER and not PF8
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system reads one record backward (skipping it) before starting to populate the screen rows, ensuring the page boundary is correctly positioned

rules.rule_name: Populate Previous Page Screen Rows in Reverse Order
rules.rule_description: The system reads up to 10 user records backward from the User Security file and populates the screen rows in reverse order (from row 10 down to row 1), so that the final display shows users in correct ascending order.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Continue Reading Previous Records
Populate Screen Rows in Reverse

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has successfully positioned the browse cursor on the User Security file for backward navigation and all 10 screen rows have been cleared
acceptance_criteria.When: The system reads previous records from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.Then: For each record successfully retrieved (up to 10), the system populates the corresponding screen row (starting from row 10 down to row 1) with the user's User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type; the User ID of the record placed in row 1 is saved as the 'First User ID on Page' and the User ID placed in row 10 is saved as the 'Last User ID on Page'; reading continues until 10 rows are filled or the top of the file is reached

rules.rule_name: Top of User File Reached During Backward Read - Notification
rules.rule_description: When the system is reading records backward to populate the previous page and reaches the beginning of the User Security file, it sets the end-of-file indicator and notifies the user that the top of the list has been reached.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Yes - Top of File Reached

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is reading user records backward from the User Security file to populate the previous page
acceptance_criteria.When: The system reaches the beginning of the User Security file (no more previous records exist)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system sets the end-of-file indicator to TRUE and displays the message 'You have reached the top of the page...' on the User List screen

rules.rule_name: Page Number Decrement on Successful Backward Navigation
rules.rule_description: After successfully reading records for the previous page, the system adjusts the page number. If more records exist before the current page and the page number is greater than 1, the page number is decremented by 1; otherwise it is reset to 1.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Display Updated
User List Screen

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has finished reading records backward and populating the screen rows for the previous page
acceptance_criteria.When: The system checks whether additional records exist before the current page position
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the NEXT-PAGE-YES flag is set AND more previous records exist AND the current page number is greater than 1, the system subtracts 1 from the current page number; otherwise the system sets the page number to 1; the updated page number is then displayed on the User List screen and the screen is sent to the user

rules.rule_name: Clear All Screen Rows Before Populating Previous Page
rules.rule_description: Before populating the screen with the previous page of users, all 10 display rows are cleared to spaces to prevent stale data from a prior page from remaining visible.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Continue Reading Previous Records
Populate Screen Rows in Reverse

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has successfully opened a browse session on the User Security file and the end-of-file indicator is not set and no error flag is active
acceptance_criteria.When: The system is about to populate the screen rows for the previous page
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system clears all 10 screen rows by setting User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type fields to spaces for each row (rows 1 through 10) before reading and populating any user data

key_functionalities.title: Session State Preservation
key_functionalities.mermaid_diagram:
flowchart TD
    A([All Screen Processing Completed])
    B[Collect Current State for Preservation]
    C[Save Current Page Number]
    D[Save Selected User ID]
    E[Save User Selection Flag\nU for Update / D for Delete]
    F[Save First User ID on Current Page\nUsed for backward navigation]
    G[Save Last User ID on Current Page\nUsed for forward navigation]
    H[Save Next Page Availability Flag\nIndicates if more records exist beyond current page]
    I[Save Program Re-Entry Marker\nEnsures correct flow on next interaction]
    J[Package All Saved State into\nCommunication Area]
    K[Return Control to Transaction\nwith Updated Communication Area]
    L([Awaiting Next User Interaction])

    A --> B
    B --> C
    C --> D
    D --> E
    E --> F
    F --> G
    G --> H
    H --> I
    I --> J
    J --> K
    K --> L

rules.rule_name: Preserve Current Page Number in Session State
rules.rule_description: The system tracks and saves the current page number in the session communication area so that when the user returns to the User List screen, the correct page context is maintained.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Save Current Page Number

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user is navigating the User List screen and a page operation (forward or backward) has been performed
acceptance_criteria.When: A forward page navigation completes successfully with at least one user record read, the page number is incremented by 1 and stored; when a backward page navigation completes and a previous record exists and the current page is greater than 1, the page number is decremented by 1; when navigating backward and no previous record exists or the page is already 1, the page number is set to 1
acceptance_criteria.Then: The updated page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is saved into the communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) and carried forward to the next user interaction, ensuring the screen displays the correct page number on re-entry

rules.rule_name: Preserve Selected User ID in Session State
rules.rule_description: When a user selects one of the displayed users by entering an action code, the selected user's ID is captured and saved in the session communication area so it is available to the target program (Update or Delete).
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Save Selected User ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered an action code ('U', 'u', 'D', or 'd') next to one of the 10 displayed users on the User List screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system scans selection fields SEL0001I through SEL0010I in order from row 1 to row 10, and the first non-blank, non-low-value selection field is found at row N (where N is 1 through 10)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The corresponding User ID from field USRID0NI (e.g., USRID01I for row 1, USRID02I for row 2, up to USRID10I for row 10) is moved into CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED and packaged into the communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) for use by the invoked program; if no selection is made, CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED is set to spaces

rules.rule_name: Preserve User Action Selection Flag in Session State
rules.rule_description: The action code entered by the user ('U' for Update or 'D' for Delete) is saved in the session communication area alongside the selected user ID, so the target program knows which operation to perform.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Save User Selection Flag
U for Update / D for Delete

acceptance_criteria.Given: The user has entered an action code in one of the selection fields (SEL0001I through SEL0010I) on the User List screen
acceptance_criteria.When: The system identifies the first non-blank, non-low-value selection field among SEL0001I through SEL0010I
acceptance_criteria.Then: The value of that selection field (expected to be 'U', 'u', 'D', or 'd') is moved into CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG and saved in the communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA); if no selection field contains a value, CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG is set to spaces

rules.rule_name: Preserve First User ID on Current Page for Backward Navigation
rules.rule_description: The User ID of the first user displayed on the current page is saved in the session state. This anchor point is used when the user presses PF7 to navigate backward, ensuring the previous page is retrieved correctly relative to the current page's starting position.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Save First User ID on Current Page
Used for backward navigation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is populating the User List screen with user records retrieved from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The first user record (row index WS-IDX = 1) is being populated on the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID (SEC-USR-ID) of that first record is saved into CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST within the communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), so that when PF7 is pressed, the backward browse starts from this User ID
