rules.rule_name: Preserve Last User ID on Current Page for Forward Navigation
rules.rule_description: The User ID of the last user displayed on the current page is saved in the session state. This anchor point is used when the user presses PF8 to navigate forward, ensuring the next page is retrieved correctly relative to the current page's ending position.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Save Last User ID on Current Page
Used for forward navigation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is populating the User List screen with user records retrieved from the User Security file
acceptance_criteria.When: The tenth user record (row index WS-IDX = 10) is being populated on the screen
acceptance_criteria.Then: The User ID (SEC-USR-ID) of that tenth record is saved into CDEMO-CU00-USRID-LAST within the communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), so that when PF8 is pressed, the forward browse starts from this User ID

rules.rule_name: Preserve Next Page Availability Flag in Session State
rules.rule_description: After loading a page of users, the system checks whether additional user records exist beyond the current page and saves this availability indicator in the session state. This flag controls whether PF8 (next page) navigation is permitted on the next interaction.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Save Next Page Availability Flag
Indicates if more records exist beyond current page

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system has finished loading up to 10 user records for the current page during a forward or backward page operation
acceptance_criteria.When: During forward navigation: after populating up to 10 rows, the system attempts to read one additional record — if that record exists, the Next Page flag is set to YES (NEXT-PAGE-YES); if no additional record exists or an end-of-file condition is reached, the flag is set to NO (NEXT-PAGE-NO); during backward navigation: the Next Page flag is initialized to YES (NEXT-PAGE-YES) at the start of PF7 processing
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Next Page availability flag is saved in the communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA); on the next interaction, if the flag is NO and the user presses PF8, the message 'You are already at the bottom of the page...' is displayed and no navigation occurs

rules.rule_name: Preserve Program Re-Entry Marker in Session State
rules.rule_description: A re-entry marker is set in the session communication area on the first visit to the User List screen. On all subsequent interactions, this marker signals that the screen has already been initialized, directing the program to receive user input rather than re-initializing the screen.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Save Program Re-Entry Marker
Ensures correct flow on next interaction

acceptance_criteria.Given: The User List screen is being accessed for the first time within the current session (the re-entry marker CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is not yet set)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program detects that CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is FALSE (NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER), indicating this is the initial entry
acceptance_criteria.Then: CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is set to TRUE and saved in the communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA); on all subsequent interactions, the program bypasses screen initialization and proceeds directly to receiving and processing user input

rules.rule_name: Package All Session State into Communication Area
rules.rule_description: All session state elements — including page number, selected user ID, selection flag, first and last user IDs on the page, next page availability flag, and re-entry marker — are collectively stored within the communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), which serves as the session state container passed between interactions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Package All Saved State into
Communication Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: All screen processing for the current user interaction has completed, including any page navigation, user selection, or error handling
acceptance_criteria.When: The program prepares to return control to the CICS transaction manager
acceptance_criteria.Then: The communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) contains the fully updated session state including: current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM), selected user ID (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED), user action flag (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG), first user ID on page (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST), last user ID on page (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-LAST), next page availability flag (NEXT-PAGE-YES/NO), and re-entry marker (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER); this packaged state is passed as the COMMAREA in the CICS RETURN command

rules.rule_name: Return Control to Transaction with Updated Session State
rules.rule_description: After all screen processing is complete, the program returns control to the CICS transaction manager, passing the fully updated communication area. This ensures the session remains active and all state is available when the user performs the next action.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Return Control to Transaction
with Updated Communication Area

acceptance_criteria.Given: All business processing for the current user interaction on the User List screen has been completed — including page navigation, user selection handling, error messaging, and screen display
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reaches the end of the main processing logic (MAIN-PARA)
acceptance_criteria.Then: Control is returned to the CICS transaction identified by WS-TRANID, with the fully updated CARDDEMO-COMMAREA passed as the communication area, preserving all session state (page number, selected user, selection flag, first/last user IDs, next page flag, re-entry marker) so the next user interaction resumes correctly from the current state

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List program has been invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins execution
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error flag is set to OFF, the end-of-file indicator is set to NOT-EOF, the next-page indicator is set to TRUE, the screen erase flag is set to YES, the message field is cleared to spaces, the screen error message field is cleared to spaces, and the cursor is positioned at the User ID input field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Program Initialization
all_rules.Rule_Description: On every program entry, all processing flags are reset to their default states and all message fields are cleared to ensure a clean processing environment.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List program has been invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No communication area is passed to the program (session length equals zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The target program is set to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) and control is transferred to that screen, preventing access to the User List

all_rules.Rule_Name: Session Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program verifies that a valid user session exists before allowing access to the User List screen. If no session context is present, the user is redirected to the Sign-On screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid user session exists and the communication area is available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program re-entry flag in the communication area is NOT set (first-time entry)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program marks itself as re-enterable, clears the screen output area to low-values, automatically processes the Enter key logic to load the first page of users, and displays the User List screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: First-Time Screen Display Detection
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program distinguishes between the first entry and subsequent re-entries to determine whether to auto-load the user list or to process user input from the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid user session exists and the program has been previously displayed to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen by pressing any key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All screen input data including selection codes, User ID search field, and the function key pressed are received from the terminal into the program's input area for processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: User Input Reception
all_rules.Rule_Description: On re-entry to the program, the system reads all input data entered by the user from the User List screen before processing any actions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the User List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the key pressed by the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If ENTER was pressed, user selection and search processing is performed; if PF3 was pressed, the user is navigated to the Admin Menu (COADM01C); if PF7 was pressed, backward page navigation is performed; if PF8 was pressed, forward page navigation is performed; if any other key was pressed, an invalid key error message is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Function Key Routing
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program routes processing to the appropriate function based on which key the user pressed: Enter for selection/search, PF3 for menu return, PF7 for page backward, PF8 for page forward, or any other key triggers an invalid key error.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the User List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A key other than ENTER, PF3, PF7, or PF8 is pressed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error flag is set to 'Y', the cursor is positioned at the User ID input field, the message 'Invalid key pressed' (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) is displayed on the screen, and the screen is refreshed without erasing existing content

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invalid Key Handling
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses an unsupported function key, the system displays an error message and refreshes the screen without making any changes to the displayed data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the User List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF3
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The target program is set to the Administration Menu (COADM01C), the current transaction ID and program name are recorded in the communication area, and control is immediately transferred to the Administration Menu with the full session context

all_rules.Rule_Name: Navigation to Admin Menu
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3, the system transfers control to the Administration Menu program, passing the current session context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the User List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system scans selection fields for rows 1 through 10 sequentially
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The first row (lowest row number) whose selection field is not blank and not low-values is identified; the selection code from that row is captured into the user selection flag, and the User ID from that same row is captured as the selected user; if no row has a selection code entered, both the selection flag and selected user ID are cleared to spaces

all_rules.Rule_Name: User Selection Detection
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses ENTER, the system scans all 10 displayed user rows in order (row 1 through row 10) to find the first row where a selection code has been entered.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a selection code on the User List screen and pressed ENTER
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The selection code is 'U' or 'u' and a valid User ID is associated with the selected row
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The target program is set to the Update User screen (COUSR02C), the current transaction ID is recorded as the originating transaction, the current program name is recorded as the originating program, the program context is set to 0, and control is immediately transferred to COUSR02C with the full session context including the selected User ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Navigate to Update User
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user enters 'U' or 'u' as the selection code next to a user, the system transfers control to the Update User program with the selected user's ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a selection code on the User List screen and pressed ENTER
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The selection code is 'D' or 'd' and a valid User ID is associated with the selected row
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The target program is set to the Delete User screen (COUSR03C), the current transaction ID is recorded as the originating transaction, the current program name is recorded as the originating program, the program context is set to 0, and control is immediately transferred to COUSR03C with the full session context including the selected User ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Navigate to Delete User
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user enters 'D' or 'd' as the selection code next to a user, the system transfers control to the Delete User program with the selected user's ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered a selection code on the User List screen and pressed ENTER
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The selection code entered is not 'U', 'u', 'D', or 'd' (i.e., any other non-blank, non-low-value character)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error message 'Invalid selection. Valid values are U and D' is displayed on the screen, the cursor is positioned at the User ID input field, and no navigation to another program occurs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invalid Selection Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user enters a selection code that is not 'U', 'u', 'D', or 'd', the system displays an error message indicating the valid selection values.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the User List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the User ID search input field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the User ID search field is blank or low-values, the browse start key is set to low-values (beginning of the user directory); if the User ID search field contains a value, that value is used as the browse start key to position the list at that specific user

all_rules.Rule_Name: User ID Search Criteria Handling
all_rules.Rule_Description: After processing any user selection, the system captures the User ID search field value to determine the starting point for loading the user list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed ENTER on the User List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to load the user list
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The page number counter is reset to 0, and forward page loading is performed starting from the User ID search key position, effectively loading the first page of results matching the search criteria

all_rules.Rule_Name: Page Forward Navigation via Enter Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses ENTER, the page counter is reset to zero before loading the first page of results based on the search criteria entered.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF7 on the User List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the current page number
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current page number is greater than 1, backward page loading is performed using the first User ID on the current page as the browse start key; if the current page number is 1 or less, the message 'You are already at the top of the page...' is displayed and the screen is refreshed without changing the displayed data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Page Backward Navigation Guard
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF7 to go to the previous page, the system checks whether the user is already on the first page before attempting backward navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF8 on the User List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the next-page availability indicator
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the next-page indicator is set to YES (more records exist beyond the current page), forward page loading is performed using the last User ID on the current page as the browse start key; if the next-page indicator is set to NO, the message 'You are already at the bottom of the page...' is displayed and the screen is refreshed without changing the displayed data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Page Forward Navigation Guard
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF8 to go to the next page, the system checks whether additional pages of users exist before attempting forward navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A forward page load has been triggered (by ENTER or PF8)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system browses the User Security file starting from the specified User ID key position
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The browse is opened at the specified start key; if the trigger was not ENTER, PF7, or PF3, one record is skipped forward before reading; all 10 display rows are cleared; up to 10 user records are read sequentially forward from the User Security file; each record's User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type are populated into the corresponding screen row; after filling rows, one additional record read is attempted to determine if more pages exist; the browse is then closed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Forward Page Data Loading
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system reads up to 10 user records forward from the User Security file starting at the specified browse key position to populate the current page of the user list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A backward page load has been triggered (by PF7) and the current page number is greater than 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system browses the User Security file backward starting from the first User ID on the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The browse is opened at the first User ID of the current page; if the trigger was not ENTER or PF8, one record is skipped backward before reading; all 10 display rows are cleared; up to 10 user records are read sequentially backward from the User Security file; each record's User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type are populated into screen rows filling from row 10 down to row 1 (reverse order); after filling rows, one additional record read backward is attempted to determine page number adjustment; the browse is then closed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Backward Page Data Loading
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system reads up to 10 user records backward from the User Security file starting at the specified browse key position to populate the previous page of the user list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A page load (forward or backward) is about to populate the screen with user records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initializes the display rows prior to reading records
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each of the 10 display rows (rows 1 through 10), the User ID field, First Name field, Last Name field, and User Type field are all set to spaces, ensuring no residual data from a previous page remains on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Row Initialization
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the user list with new data, all 10 display rows are cleared to spaces to prevent stale data from a previous page from remaining visible.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully read from the User Security file during a page load
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the screen row corresponding to the current row index (1 through 10)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID from the record is placed in the User ID field of the corresponding row; the First Name from the record is placed in the First Name field; the Last Name from the record is placed in the Last Name field; the User Type from the record is placed in the User Type field; if the row index does not match 1 through 10, no action is taken

all_rules.Rule_Name: User Record Population
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each user record read from the User Security file is mapped to the corresponding display row on the screen, showing the user's ID, first name, last name, and user type.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A page load (forward or backward) has completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system updates the page number after loading records
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For forward navigation: the page number is incremented by 1 if at least one record was read (index greater than 1); for backward navigation: if more records exist before the current page and the page number is greater than 1, the page number is decremented by 1, otherwise the page number is set to 1; the updated page number is then displayed in the page number field on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Page Number Tracking
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system maintains an accurate page number counter that is incremented during forward navigation and decremented during backward navigation, and displays it on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A forward page load has completed reading up to 10 user records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to read one additional record beyond the 10 displayed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the additional record read is successful (more users exist in the file), the next-page indicator is set to YES, enabling PF8 forward navigation; if the additional record read reaches end-of-file (no more users exist), the next-page indicator is set to NO, disabling PF8 forward navigation; if fewer than 10 records were read (end-of-file reached during the main read loop), the next-page indicator is also set to NO

all_rules.Rule_Name: Next Page Availability Indicator
all_rules.Rule_Description: After loading a full page of 10 users, the system attempts to read one additional record to determine whether a next page of users is available, controlling whether PF8 navigation is permitted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: User records are being populated into the display rows during a page load
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates row 1 and row 10 of the display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: When row 1 is populated, the User ID of that record is saved as the 'first user on page' anchor value in the communication area; when row 10 is populated, the User ID of that record is saved as the 'last user on page' anchor value in the communication area; these anchor values are used as browse start keys for PF7 (backward) and PF8 (forward) navigation respectively

all_rules.Rule_Name: First and Last User ID Tracking
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system records the User ID of the first and last users displayed on the current page to serve as anchor points for subsequent forward and backward page navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is about to be sent to the terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the screen header fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The first application title (CCDA-TITLE01) is placed in the title 1 field; the second application title (CCDA-TITLE02) is placed in the title 2 field; the current transaction ID is placed in the transaction name field; the current program name is placed in the program name field; the current date is formatted as MM/DD/YY and placed in the date field; the current time is formatted as HH:MM:SS and placed in the time field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Header Population
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before sending the User List screen to the terminal, the system populates the screen header with current application context information including titles, transaction details, and the current date and time.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header has been populated and the user list data is ready for display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the User List screen to the terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current message (error or informational) is placed in the screen message field; if the screen erase flag is set to YES, the screen is sent with a full terminal erase (clearing any previous content) and the cursor is positioned; if the screen erase flag is set to NO, the screen is sent as an overlay without erasing existing terminal content, with the cursor positioned

all_rules.Rule_Name: User List Screen Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system sends the fully populated User List screen to the user's terminal, with the display mode (full erase or overlay) determined by the screen erase flag.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has completed processing the current user interaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program returns control to CICS
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is returned to CICS with the current transaction ID specified for the next invocation, and the full communication area (containing page number, first/last user IDs on page, selected user, re-entry flag, next-page indicator, and all other session state) is passed back to CICS to be available on the next user interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Session State Preservation
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the end of each program execution cycle, the system returns control to CICS while preserving the complete session state in the communication area so that the next user interaction can resume from the correct context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List Management program begins a new execution cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its processing environment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error flag must be set to OFF, indicating no errors are present and all subsequent processing should proceed normally without any pre-existing error condition

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Error Flag to No-Error State
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the start of every program execution cycle, the error flag must be set to OFF to ensure no residual error state from a previous interaction affects the current session processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List Management program begins a new execution cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its processing environment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User Security file status must be set to 'Not End-of-File', signaling that user records are available to be read and displayed on the User List screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize User Security File Status to Records Available
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the start of every program execution cycle, the User Security file read status must be set to 'Not End-of-File' to indicate that user records are available for retrieval and display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List Management program begins a new execution cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its processing environment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next-page flag must be set to NO, indicating that no further pages of user records are assumed to be available until the data retrieval process confirms additional records exist

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Next Page Availability Flag to No Additional Pages
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the start of every program execution cycle, the next-page availability flag must be set to NO, meaning the system assumes by default that no additional pages of user records exist beyond the current view until confirmed otherwise during data retrieval.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List Management program begins a new execution cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its processing environment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen erase flag must be set to YES, ensuring the User List screen will be fully erased and refreshed when displayed, so no residual data from a prior screen interaction remains visible to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Screen Refresh Mode to Full Erase
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the start of every program execution cycle, the screen erase flag must be set to YES so that when the User List screen is sent to the user, the entire screen is fully cleared and redrawn, preventing any stale data from a previous display from remaining visible.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List Management program begins a new execution cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its processing environment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The general message field (WS-MESSAGE) must be set to spaces, ensuring no leftover message from a previous user interaction is carried forward and displayed on the current screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear General Message Field at Program Start
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the start of every program execution cycle, the general message field must be cleared to spaces so that no informational or status message from a prior interaction is inadvertently displayed to the user during the current session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List Management program begins a new execution cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its processing environment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The error message output field (ERRMSGO) on the User List screen must be set to spaces, ensuring no prior error message is visible to the user when the screen is rendered in the current cycle

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Error Message Display Field at Program Start
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the start of every program execution cycle, the error message display field on the User List screen must be cleared to spaces so that no error message from a prior interaction is shown to the user at the beginning of the current processing cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List Management program begins a new execution cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its processing environment
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID input field length indicator (USRIDINL) must be set to -1, positioning the screen cursor at the User ID search field so the user can immediately begin entering a User ID to search or filter the user list

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set User ID Search Field to Default Entry Position
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the start of every program execution cycle, the User ID input field on the User List screen must be set to its default cursor entry position, directing the user's cursor to the User ID search field as the primary input point for filtering or searching users.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user attempts to access the User List screen and no active session communication area is present (communication area length equals zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether a valid session context exists
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) and initiates a redirect to that screen, ending the current program execution

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Missing User Session and Set Sign-On Destination
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User List screen is invoked, the system checks whether an active user session exists by verifying the presence of a communication area. If no session is found, the system designates the Sign-On screen as the redirect destination before transferring control.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user accesses the User List screen and an active session communication area exists (communication area length is greater than zero)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms the presence of a valid session
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system loads the full session context (including program state, navigation flags, selected user details, and page information) from the communication area into the working session data, and proceeds to program processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Load Active Session Data When Valid Session Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a valid user session is detected (communication area is present), the system loads the session context data from the communication area to enable further processing of the User List screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined that no valid user session exists and the destination program has been set to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C); additionally, if the destination program is blank or unset at the time of redirect, it defaults to COSGN00C
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the redirect to the previous or designated screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the current transaction ID as the originating transaction, records the current program name as the originating program, resets the program context to zero, and transfers full control to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) passing the current session communication area, terminating execution of the User List program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redirect User to Sign-On Screen When No Session Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no active session exists, the system transfers control to the Sign-On screen. If no destination program has been explicitly set, the system defaults the destination to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) before redirecting. The current program's transaction ID and program name are recorded as the originating context before the transfer.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is being accessed for the first time within the current session (the program has not yet been marked as re-entered)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes the first-time screen display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program must be flagged as re-entered (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER = TRUE) so that all future interactions within this session are treated as return visits, AND the entire screen output area (COUSR0AO) must be reset to LOW-VALUES to ensure no stale data is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Program as Re-Entered on First Visit
all_rules.Rule_Description: On the very first time a user enters the User List screen, the program must mark itself as re-entered so that any subsequent interaction by the same user is treated as a return visit rather than a fresh launch, and the screen output area is fully cleared to remove any residual data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is being loaded for the first time and the User ID input field (USRIDINI) on the screen is either blank (SPACES) or empty (LOW-VALUES)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines the starting point for browsing the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The search key (SEC-USR-ID) must be set to LOW-VALUES so that the browse begins from the very first record in the User Security file; if the User ID input field contains a value, that value must be moved to SEC-USR-ID to start the browse from that specific user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set User ID Search Starting Point to Beginning of User Directory
all_rules.Rule_Description: When loading the user list for the first time, if no User ID search value has been entered by the user, the browse must start from the very beginning of the User Security file. If a User ID has been entered, that value is used as the starting point for the browse.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is being loaded for the first time and the page forward process is about to begin
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to load the first page of users
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) must be set to 0 so that after the first page load increments it, the displayed page number correctly shows 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Page Number to Zero Before Loading First Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before loading the first page of users, the page counter must be reset to zero so that after the first page is successfully loaded, the page number is correctly incremented to 1.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The search starting key (SEC-USR-ID) has been set to either LOW-VALUES (start of file) or a specific User ID value
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the user list retrieval process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A browse must be opened on the User Security file (WS-USRSEC-FILE) positioned at the record matching or immediately following the SEC-USR-ID key, enabling sequential forward reading of user records from that position

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Browse on User Security File from Starting Position
all_rules.Rule_Description: To retrieve the list of users, the system must open a sequential browse on the User Security file starting from the determined search key position. This establishes the read cursor for subsequent sequential reads of user records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The browse on the User Security file has been successfully opened and the system is about to populate the screen with user records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screen rows for new data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All 10 user display rows (rows 1 through 10) must have their User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type fields set to SPACES, ensuring a clean slate before new user data is loaded

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All 10 User Display Rows Before Populating New Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the screen with newly retrieved user records, all 10 display rows must be cleared to spaces to ensure no stale or residual user data from a previous page is visible on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User Security file browse is open, all 10 screen rows have been cleared, and the row index (WS-IDX) is set to 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sequentially reads user records from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must read the next user record and populate the corresponding screen row, then increment the row index by 1; this process must continue until the row index reaches 11 (10 rows filled), the end of the User Security file is reached, or a retrieval error occurs — whichever happens first

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Up to 10 User Records Sequentially for Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system reads user records one at a time from the User Security file in forward sequence, populating each screen row in order, until either 10 rows are filled, the end of the file is reached, or an error occurs.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully read from the User Security file and the current row index (WS-IDX) is between 1 and 10
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the screen row corresponding to the current row index
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID (SEC-USR-ID) must be moved to the User ID display field of the matching row (USRID01I through USRID10I); the First Name (SEC-USR-FNAME) must be moved to the First Name field (FNAME01I through FNAME10I); the Last Name (SEC-USR-LNAME) must be moved to the Last Name field (LNAME01I through LNAME10I); and the User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE) must be moved to the User Type field (UTYPE01I through UTYPE10I) of the corresponding row

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Each Screen Row with User Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each user record successfully read from the User Security file, the system maps the user's details — User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type — to the corresponding screen display row (1 through 10).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: User records are being populated into the screen rows
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates row 1 or row 10 with a user record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: When populating row 1, the User ID (SEC-USR-ID) must also be saved to CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST to mark the first user on the current page; when populating row 10, the User ID (SEC-USR-ID) must also be saved to CDEMO-CU00-USRID-LAST to mark the last user on the current page — these values are used as anchors for subsequent page forward and backward navigation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Track First and Last User ID on Current Page for Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: To support accurate forward and backward page navigation, the system must record the User ID of the first user displayed (row 1) and the User ID of the last user displayed (row 10) on the current page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has finished reading up to 10 user records and populating the screen rows
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks for the existence of additional user records beyond the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must attempt to read one more record from the User Security file; if the read is successful and the record exists (USER-SEC-NOT-EOF is TRUE and no error), the next-page indicator (NEXT-PAGE) must be set to YES, indicating more pages are available; if the read returns end-of-file or an error, the next-page indicator must be set to NO, indicating the current page is the last page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Whether Additional Pages of Users Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: After filling up to 10 rows, the system attempts to read one additional record beyond the current page to determine whether more users exist. This controls whether the PF8 (next page) navigation option is available to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed reading user records for the current page (at least one record was read, WS-IDX is greater than 1) and the page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) was initialized to 0 before the first load
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system finalizes the page load after reading records
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) must be incremented by 1 (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM = CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM + 1), resulting in a page number of 1 for the first page load, and the updated page number must be moved to the page number display field (PAGENUMI) on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Increment Page Number After Successfully Loading a Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully loading user records onto the screen, the page number counter is incremented by 1. Since the counter starts at 0 before the first page load, this results in the page number being set to 1 after the first page is displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All 10 screen rows have been populated with user data (or cleared if fewer than 10 users exist), the page number has been set, and the screen header has been populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the User List screen to the user for the first-time display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen must be sent using the COUSR0A map from the COUSR00 mapset with the ERASE option active (SEND-ERASE-YES = TRUE), ensuring the entire screen is refreshed; any informational or error message stored in WS-MESSAGE must be displayed in the error message field (ERRMSGO) on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display User List Screen with Full Screen Refresh
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all user data and header information have been prepared, the User List screen is sent to the user with a full erase to ensure a clean display of the first page of users.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is about to send the User List screen to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header information is being prepared
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen header must be populated with: the application title line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) in TITLE01O, the application title line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) in TITLE02O, the current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) in TRNNAMEO, the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) in PGMNAMEO, the current date formatted as MM/DD/YY (derived from the system date) in CURDATEO, and the current time formatted as HH:MM:SS (derived from the system time) in CURTIMEO

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Header with Application and Session Information
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the User List screen, the screen header must be populated with the application titles, the current transaction ID, the current program name, the current date formatted as MM/DD/YY, and the current time formatted as HH:MM:SS.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen and has previously visited it at least once (the screen is in re-entry mode)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user submits the screen by pressing any key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system captures all screen input into the internal input map (COUSR0AI), including: selection flag fields for all 10 user rows (SEL0001I through SEL0010I), the User ID displayed on each of the 10 rows (USRID01I through USRID10I), the User ID entered in the search/filter field (USRIDINI), and the identity of the function key pressed (EIBAID)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture All User List Screen Input
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user submits the User List screen, the system must capture all input fields including selection codes entered next to any of the 10 listed users, the User ID associated with each listed row, any User ID entered in the search field, and the function key pressed by the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is displaying up to 10 users and the user has entered a selection code in one or more selection fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the Enter key action and evaluates the selection fields
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system scans selection fields SEL0001I through SEL0010I in sequential order (row 1 first, row 10 last); the first selection field that is not blank and not empty is identified; the selection action code from that field is stored as the User Selection Flag (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG); the User ID from the corresponding row (USRID01I through USRID10I) is stored as the Selected User (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED); all subsequent selection fields are ignored; if no selection field contains a value, both the User Selection Flag and Selected User are set to spaces

all_rules.Rule_Name: User Enters Selection Code Next to a Listed User
all_rules.Rule_Description: The user may enter a selection action code in the selection field next to any of the 10 displayed users. The system scans rows 1 through 10 in order and processes only the first row where a non-blank, non-empty selection code is found. The selected action code and the corresponding User ID are captured for subsequent processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is displayed with up to 10 user rows and the user has entered selection codes next to more than one user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the selection fields upon pressing Enter
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system processes only the first row (lowest row number from 1 to 10) where the selection field is not blank and not empty; the selection code and User ID from that row are captured; selection codes entered on any other rows are ignored entirely

all_rules.Rule_Name: First Non-Blank Selection Takes Priority
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the user enters selection codes next to multiple users on the same screen, only the selection code on the lowest-numbered row (closest to row 1) is acted upon. All other selection entries are disregarded.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen and the search field (USRIDINI) is available for input
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses Enter and the system processes the search criteria
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the User ID search field (USRIDINI) contains a value that is not blank and not empty, that value is used as the starting point (SEC-USR-ID) for browsing the user directory; if the User ID search field is blank or empty, the browse starting point (SEC-USR-ID) is set to LOW-VALUES, causing the list to start from the very first user in the directory

all_rules.Rule_Name: User Enters User ID in Search Field to Filter List
all_rules.Rule_Description: The user may type a User ID in the search field to start the displayed list from that specific user. If the search field is left blank or empty, the system starts the list from the very beginning of the user directory.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the User List screen and all input has been captured
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the function key pressed (EIBAID)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the user pressed Enter, the system performs user selection and list search processing (PROCESS-ENTER-KEY); if the user pressed PF3, the system navigates back to the Administration Menu (COADM01C); if the user pressed PF7, the system performs backward page navigation (PROCESS-PF7-KEY); if the user pressed PF8, the system performs forward page navigation (PROCESS-PF8-KEY); if the user pressed any other key, the system sets the error flag to 'Y', sets cursor focus to the User ID input field, displays the invalid key error message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY), and refreshes the User List screen without changing any data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route Processing Based on Function Key Pressed
all_rules.Rule_Description: After capturing screen input, the system determines which processing path to follow based on the function key the user pressed. Each supported key triggers a distinct business operation, and any unsupported key results in an error message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses a function key that is not Enter, PF3, PF7, or PF8
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error indicator to 'Y' (WS-ERR-FLG), positions the cursor on the User ID input field (USRIDINL set to -1), displays the standard invalid key error message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) in the message area of the screen, and re-displays the User List screen with the existing data unchanged

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invalid Function Key Pressed on User List Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: Only the function keys Enter, PF3, PF7, and PF8 are valid on the User List screen. If the user presses any other key, the system displays an error message and refreshes the screen without performing any data changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has navigated to the User List screen with a valid session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether this is the first visit or a return visit to the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If this is the first visit (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is not set), the system marks the screen as re-enterable, clears the screen output area, and directly loads and displays the user list without receiving any screen input; if this is a return visit (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is already set), the system receives the screen input from the user before proceeding to evaluate the function key and process the request

all_rules.Rule_Name: Screen Input Reception Only on Re-Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system only receives and processes screen input from the user on subsequent visits to the User List screen. On the very first visit, the screen is initialized and displayed without reading any user input.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen and has an active session with a valid communication area loaded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the Enter key to submit their input
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system routes control to the Enter Key processing logic (PROCESS-ENTER-KEY) which evaluates any user row selections made and performs page navigation accordingly

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route Enter Key Press to User Selection and Page Navigation Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses the Enter key on the User List screen, the system routes processing to the Enter Key logic which handles user row selections and page navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen and has an active session with a valid communication area loaded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the target program to 'COADM01C', records the current transaction ID and program name as the originating context, resets the program context to zero, and transfers control to the Administration Menu program (COADM01C) passing the full session communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route PF3 Key Press to Return to Administration Menu
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3 on the User List screen, the system navigates back to the Administration Menu program (COADM01C), passing the current session context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen and has an active session with a valid communication area loaded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF7 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system routes control to the PF7 key processing logic (PROCESS-PF7-KEY) which handles backward page navigation through the user list

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route PF7 Key Press to Previous Page Navigation Logic
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF7 on the User List screen, the system routes processing to the previous page navigation logic to display the prior set of users.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen and has an active session with a valid communication area loaded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF8 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system routes control to the PF8 key processing logic (PROCESS-PF8-KEY) which handles forward page navigation through the user list

all_rules.Rule_Name: Route PF8 Key Press to Next Page Navigation Logic
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF8 on the User List screen, the system routes processing to the next page navigation logic to display the following set of users.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen and has an active session with a valid communication area loaded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any key that is not Enter, PF3, PF7, or PF8
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y', positions the cursor on the User ID input field, displays the standard invalid key error message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) in the screen error message area, and refreshes the User List screen showing the error message without altering any user data currently displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Invalid Key Error for Unsupported Function Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses any function key other than Enter, PF3, PF7, or PF8 on the User List screen, the system displays an invalid key error message and refreshes the screen without making any changes to the displayed data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen and has already interacted with it at least once (screen is in re-entry mode)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses any keyboard key to submit an action
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system evaluates the key pressed and routes to the appropriate action only if it is one of the four supported keys: Enter (submit/search), PF3 (return to Admin Menu), PF7 (page backward), or PF8 (page forward). Any other key is considered unsupported and triggers the invalid key handling process.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Supported Function Key Identification for User List Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: Defines which keyboard function keys are valid and accepted on the User List screen. Only Enter, PF3, PF7, and PF8 are recognized as supported actions. Any other key press is treated as invalid.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen in re-entry mode
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses a key that is not Enter, PF3, PF7, or PF8
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the error flag to 'Y' (ON), marking the current interaction as erroneous so that subsequent screen display logic is aware an error condition exists

all_rules.Rule_Name: Error Flag Activation on Invalid Key Press
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user presses an unsupported key on the User List screen, the system activates the error flag to indicate that an invalid action was attempted. This flag signals that the current interaction contains an error that must be communicated back to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen in re-entry mode and the error flag has been set to ON
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user has pressed a key that is not one of the supported keys (Enter, PF3, PF7, PF8)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system assigns the standard application-defined invalid key message (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) to the screen message field (WS-MESSAGE), which will be displayed to the user as feedback

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invalid Key Error Message Assignment
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an unsupported key is pressed on the User List screen, the system assigns the standard invalid key message to the screen message field. This message is sourced from the application's centrally defined message constants (CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY) to ensure consistent messaging across the application.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen, the error flag is set to ON, and the invalid key error message has been assigned to the message field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to redisplay the User List screen after an invalid key press
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the User List screen with: (1) the invalid key error message shown in the error message area, (2) the cursor positioned at the User ID input field, (3) the screen header populated with current application titles, transaction ID, program name, current date in MM/DD/YY format, and current time in HH:MM:SS format, and (4) the existing user list data preserved so the user can see the current page and make a valid selection or key press

all_rules.Rule_Name: User List Screen Redisplay with Invalid Key Error
all_rules.Rule_Description: After detecting an invalid key press and setting the error message, the system redisplays the User List screen to the user with the error message visible. The screen is sent with the cursor positioned at the User ID input field, and the existing user list data remains intact so the user can correct their action without losing context.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen with an active session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the PF3 key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program to the Administration Menu screen identified as COADM01C and initiates the return-to-previous-screen navigation process

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Destination to Administration Menu on PF3
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF3 on the User List screen, the system designates the Administration Menu (COADM01C) as the target destination for navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The navigation process has been initiated and the destination program field is being evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The destination program value is blank (spaces) or uninitialized (low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system overrides the destination and sets it to the Sign-On screen identified as COSGN00C, ensuring no navigation occurs to an undefined screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Default Navigation Target to Sign-On Screen When Destination is Blank
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control, the system validates that a destination program has been set. If the destination is blank or uninitialized, the system defaults the navigation target to the Sign-On screen (COSGN00C) to ensure the user is always directed to a valid screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The destination program has been validated and is ready for navigation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is preparing to transfer control to the destination screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the current transaction ID into the 'from transaction' field, records the current program name into the 'from program' field, and sets the program context to zero — all stored in the shared communication area for use by the destination screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Current Program and Transaction Context Before Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to another screen, the system captures and stores the current transaction identifier, current program name, and resets the program context to zero. This information is passed via the communication area so the destination screen knows where the user navigated from.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The destination program has been set (either COADM01C or defaulted to COSGN00C) and the current program and transaction details have been recorded in the communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the control transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system transfers full control to the destination program and passes the entire session communication area (containing user session data, navigation context, and program details) to the destination screen, terminating execution of the current User List program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Control to Administration Menu
all_rules.Rule_Description: After recording the navigation context, the system transfers full control to the designated destination program (Administration Menu COADM01C or defaulted Sign-On screen COSGN00C), passing the complete session communication area so the destination screen has access to all current session data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is displayed with up to 10 user rows, and the user has pressed the Enter key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system scans selection fields for rows 1 through 10 sequentially and finds the first row where the selection code is not blank and not empty
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The selection code and the User ID from that first non-blank row are captured into the active selection variables; scanning stops at the first match and no further rows are evaluated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Sequential Row Scan to Detect First User Selection
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Enter key is pressed on the User List screen, the system scans all 10 displayed user rows in order from Row 1 to Row 10. The first row that contains a non-blank, non-empty selection code is captured along with its associated User ID. Only the first such entry is acted upon; all subsequent rows are ignored.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is displayed with up to 10 user rows and the user has pressed the Enter key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: None of the 10 selection fields (Row 1 through Row 10) contain a non-blank, non-empty value
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The selection code field and the selected User ID field are both cleared to spaces, and the system proceeds to the search and page-forward operation without navigating to any user action screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: No Selection Made - Clear Selection Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the user presses Enter without entering a selection code on any of the 10 displayed rows, the system clears the selection code and selected User ID fields, indicating no user action was requested.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed scanning all 10 rows after the Enter key was pressed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the captured selection code is non-blank and non-empty AND the captured User ID is non-blank and non-empty
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If both the selection code and User ID are present and non-blank, the system proceeds to evaluate the action code; if either is blank or empty, the system skips action routing and proceeds directly to the search and page-forward operation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate That Both Selection Code and User ID Are Present Before Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before processing a user's selection action, the system verifies that both a selection code and a User ID have been successfully captured. If either is missing or blank, the system bypasses the action routing and proceeds directly to the search and page-forward operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid selection code and User ID have been captured from the User List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The captured selection code is 'U' (uppercase) or 'u' (lowercase)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the target program to the Update User program (COUSR02C), records the current transaction ID and program name as the originating context, resets the program context to zero, and transfers control to the Update User program with the full session communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Navigate to Update User Screen When 'U' is Selected
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters 'U' or 'u' as the selection code next to a listed user, the system navigates to the Update User screen, passing the selected User ID and current session context so the administrator can modify that user's details.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid selection code and User ID have been captured from the User List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The captured selection code is 'D' (uppercase) or 'd' (lowercase)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the target program to the Delete User program (COUSR03C), records the current transaction ID and program name as the originating context, resets the program context to zero, and transfers control to the Delete User program with the full session communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Navigate to Delete User Screen When 'D' is Selected
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters 'D' or 'd' as the selection code next to a listed user, the system navigates to the Delete User screen, passing the selected User ID and current session context so the administrator can remove that user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A valid selection code and User ID have been captured from the User List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The captured selection code is any value other than 'U', 'u', 'D', or 'd'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the error message 'Invalid selection. Valid values are U and D' on the screen, does not navigate to any user action screen, and proceeds to the search and page-forward operation to refresh the user list

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reject Invalid Selection Code with Error Message
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the user enters a selection code that is neither 'U', 'u', 'D', nor 'd', the system rejects the action and displays an error message informing the user that only 'U' (Update) and 'D' (Delete) are valid selection codes. The system then proceeds to refresh the user list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Enter key was pressed on the User List screen and selection code processing has completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Either no selection was made across all 10 rows, or an invalid selection code was entered, or the selection processing did not result in navigation to another screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the User ID search key based on the value entered in the User ID search field (using the start of the file if the field is blank), resets the page number to zero, and performs the page-forward operation to load and display the user list

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to User List Search and Page Forward After Selection Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: After completing selection code processing — whether no selection was made, an invalid selection code was entered, or a valid selection was processed but did not result in navigation — the system proceeds to execute the user list search and page-forward operation to display or refresh the user list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user has entered a selection code next to one of the displayed user records on the User List screen, and the selection code has been captured into the selection flag field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the captured selection flag and finds it equals 'U' (uppercase) or 'u' (lowercase)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system identifies this as an Update User request and proceeds to set up the navigation to the Update User screen; if the selection flag is neither 'U' nor 'u', the Update User navigation path is not taken

all_rules.Rule_Name: Identify Update User Selection
all_rules.Rule_Description: Determine whether the action code entered by the user next to a user record is an Update request, accepting both uppercase 'U' and lowercase 'u' as valid update indicators.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected 'U' or 'u' next to a user record on the User List screen, and the system has confirmed this is an Update User request
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to navigate to the Update User program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the current transaction ID into the 'From Transaction' field of the communication area, and records the current program name into the 'From Program' field of the communication area, so the Update User program can identify its caller

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Origin Program and Transaction for Update Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to the Update User program, the system records the current program name and transaction ID as the originating source so that the Update User program knows where to return after completing its operation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected 'U' or 'u' next to a user record, and the origin program and transaction have been recorded in the communication area
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sets up the navigation destination
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program identifier in the communication area to 'COUSR02C' (Update User Program)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Update User as Destination Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: When an Update action is confirmed, the system designates the Update User program (COUSR02C) as the target destination for the navigation transfer.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has selected 'U' or 'u' next to a specific user record on the User List screen, and the destination program has been set to COUSR02C
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the communication area for the transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system places the selected User ID into the 'User Selected' field of the communication area, and places the selection flag ('U' or 'u') into the 'User Selection Flag' field, and sets the program context to zero indicating a fresh invocation, so the Update User program receives the correct user to process

all_rules.Rule_Name: Pass Selected User ID to Update User Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: The User ID of the record selected for update is passed through the shared communication area to the Update User program, so it knows which user record to load and present for editing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The communication area has been populated with the selected User ID, selection flag, origin transaction ID, origin program name, destination program name (COUSR02C), and program context set to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the program transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is fully transferred to the Update User program (COUSR02C) along with the entire communication area; the User List program (COUSR00C) is no longer active and the Update User program takes over the user's session

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Control to Update User Program
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all navigation parameters are set, the system transfers full control to the Update User program (COUSR02C), passing the complete communication area containing the selected user's details, origin program, and transaction information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is displaying up to 10 user records, each with a selection input field (SEL0001 through SEL0010) and a corresponding User ID field (USRID01 through USRID10)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses the Enter key after entering a selection code next to one or more user records
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system scans selection fields SEL0001 through SEL0010 sequentially and captures the selection code and User ID from the FIRST row where the selection field is not blank and not empty. If no selection field contains a value, both the selection flag and the selected User ID are cleared to spaces.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Scan All Screen Rows to Identify User Selection
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Enter key is pressed on the User List screen, the system scans all 10 displayed user rows in order (row 1 through row 10) to find the first row where the user has entered a selection code. Only the first non-blank selection found is processed; all subsequent selections are ignored.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has identified a screen row (1 through 10) where the user has entered a non-blank, non-empty selection code next to a displayed user record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The selection code and User ID are read from that specific row
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system stores the entered selection code into the User Selection Flag (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG) and stores the corresponding User ID from that row (USRID01 through USRID10) into the Selected User ID field (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture Selected User ID from the Chosen Row
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the first non-blank selection row is identified, the system captures both the action code entered by the user and the User ID associated with that row, storing them for subsequent processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A selection code has been captured from the User List screen and stored in the User Selection Flag (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG), and a non-blank User ID has been stored in the Selected User ID field (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the captured selection code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the selection code is 'D' or 'd' AND the Selected User ID is not blank or empty, the system proceeds with the Delete User action. If the selection code is neither 'D' nor 'd', the delete action is not triggered and processing continues with other logic.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Delete Action Selection Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a selection has been captured, the system validates whether the entered action code represents a Delete request. The delete action is recognized only when the selection code is the letter 'D' (uppercase or lowercase), and a valid User ID has been captured alongside it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered 'D' or 'd' as the selection code next to a user record on the User List screen, and a valid User ID has been captured
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms the selection code is 'D' or 'd'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the destination program identifier to 'COUSR03C' (Delete User Program) in the navigation target field (CDEMO-TO-PROGRAM)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Destination Program to Delete User
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a valid Delete action code ('D' or 'd') is confirmed for a selected user, the system designates the Delete User program (COUSR03C) as the target destination for the navigation transfer.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has confirmed a Delete action and has set the destination program to COUSR03C
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to transfer control to the Delete User program
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system records the current Transaction ID (WS-TRANID) into the originating transaction field (CDEMO-FROM-TRANID), records the current Program Name (WS-PGMNAME) into the originating program field (CDEMO-FROM-PROGRAM), and sets the Program Context indicator (CDEMO-PGM-CONTEXT) to zero to indicate a fresh entry into the target program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record Current Program and Transaction for Return Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before transferring control to the Delete User program, the system records the identity of the current program and transaction so that the Delete User program can navigate back to the User List screen upon completion.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The destination program has been set to COUSR03C, the current program and transaction details have been recorded in the session context (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), and the selected User ID is stored in CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED within the session context
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the program transfer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is fully transferred to the Delete User program (COUSR03C) and the complete session communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) — containing the selected User ID, originating program, originating transaction, and program context — is passed to the Delete User program. The current User List program ceases execution.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Control to Delete User Program with Selected User ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: After recording navigation details, the system transfers full control to the Delete User program (COUSR03C), passing the complete session context including the selected User ID, so the Delete User program can operate on the correct user record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is displayed with up to 10 user records, and the user has pressed the Enter key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system scans selection fields SEL0001 through SEL0010 in order from row 1 to row 10 and finds the first field that is not blank and not empty
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system captures that selection code and the corresponding User ID from the same row as the active selection, and proceeds to evaluate the selection code; if no selection field contains a value, the selection flag and selected user ID are cleared and the system proceeds directly to search and page processing without any navigation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect User Selection from List
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system scans all 10 user rows on the User List screen to determine whether the user has entered a selection code next to any displayed user record. The first non-blank, non-low-value selection field found (rows 1 through 10, in order) is treated as the active selection.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is displayed with user records, and the user has entered a selection code next to one of the displayed user records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The selection code entered is 'U' (uppercase) or 'u' (lowercase) and the corresponding User ID is not blank
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the target program to COUSR02C (Update User), records the current transaction ID and program name as the originating context, resets the program context to 0, and transfers control to the Update User program passing the full session communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Navigate to Update User Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters the selection code 'U' or 'u' next to a displayed user record and presses Enter, the system navigates to the Update User screen, passing the selected user's information for update processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is displayed with user records, and the user has entered a selection code next to one of the displayed user records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The selection code entered is 'D' (uppercase) or 'd' (lowercase) and the corresponding User ID is not blank
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the target program to COUSR03C (Delete User), records the current transaction ID and program name as the originating context, resets the program context to 0, and transfers control to the Delete User program passing the full session communication area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Navigate to Delete User Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters the selection code 'D' or 'd' next to a displayed user record and presses Enter, the system navigates to the Delete User screen, passing the selected user's information for deletion processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is displayed with user records, and the user has entered a selection code next to one of the displayed user records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The selection code entered is any value other than 'U', 'u', 'D', or 'd'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the error message 'Invalid selection. Valid values are U and D' on the screen, sets the cursor focus to the User ID input field, and continues to the search and page processing to refresh the user list display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invalid Selection Code Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters a selection code that is not 'U', 'u', 'D', or 'd' next to a displayed user record, the system rejects the selection and displays an error message indicating the only valid selection codes are U and D. The system then continues to refresh the user list screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is displayed with up to 10 user records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses Enter and all 10 selection fields (SEL0001 through SEL0010) are blank or empty
