Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears the selection flag and the selected user ID, and proceeds to search and page processing using the User ID entered in the search field (or from the beginning of the user directory if the search field is blank)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Search and Page Processing Without Selection
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses Enter without entering any selection code next to any of the displayed user records, the system clears any prior selection context and proceeds directly to search and page processing to refresh or filter the user list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen has been submitted by the user pressing the ENTER key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the search request
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system reads the value from the User ID search input field (USRIDINI) to use as the basis for determining the starting point of the user directory browse

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture User ID from Search Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user submits the User List screen, the system captures whatever value has been entered in the User ID search field to determine where to begin browsing the user directory.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the User List screen with the User ID search field left blank or containing only spaces or empty (low-value) characters
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the content of the User ID search field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the browse starting key to the lowest possible value (beginning of the user directory), so that the user list is retrieved from the very first user record on file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Blank Search Field Defaults to Start of User Directory
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the user leaves the User ID search field blank or empty, the system automatically starts browsing the user directory from the very beginning, ensuring all users are accessible.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has submitted the User List screen with a specific User ID value entered in the User ID search field (not blank and not empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the content of the User ID search field
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the browse starting key to the exact User ID value entered by the user, so that the user list is retrieved beginning from that specific user record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Entered User ID Used as Search Starting Point
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the user enters a specific User ID in the search field, the system uses that User ID as the starting point for browsing the user directory, allowing the user to navigate directly to a specific position in the list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has determined the browse starting point based on the User ID search field (either beginning of file or a specific User ID)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to load the user list
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system resets the current page number to zero, so that the subsequent page load will correctly assign and display page number 1 as the first page of results

all_rules.Rule_Name: Page Number Reset to Zero Before New Search
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before loading a fresh set of results based on a new search starting point, the system resets the page counter to zero so that page numbering begins correctly from page 1 when the first page of results is displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The browse starting key has been set (either to the beginning of the user directory or to a specific User ID) and the page number has been reset to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system executes the forward page load process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves up to 10 user records starting from the determined position and displays them on the User List screen; if the page loads successfully with no errors, the User ID search input field is cleared on the screen so it does not retain the previously entered search value

all_rules.Rule_Name: Load and Display First Page of Users from Determined Starting Point
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the search starting point is established and the page counter is reset, the system retrieves and displays the first page of up to 10 users beginning from the determined starting position in the user directory. If the page loads successfully without errors, the User ID search field is cleared on the display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed the Enter key on the User List screen without selecting any user action
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the User ID search field (USRIDINI): if it contains spaces or low-values it is considered blank; otherwise it contains a valid User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the search field is blank or empty, the browse starting key is set to LOW-VALUES (beginning of the user list); if a User ID is provided, the browse starting key is set to that entered User ID (SEC-USR-ID)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Browse Start Position Based on User ID Search Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Enter key is pressed with no user selection made, the system determines the starting position for browsing the user list based on whether a User ID has been entered in the search field.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed the Enter key on the User List screen and the browse start position has been determined
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to load the user list page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The page number counter (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is set to zero before the page forward process begins

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Page Number to Zero Before Loading New Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Enter key is pressed to initiate a new user list search or refresh, the current page number counter must be reset to zero before any page loading begins, ensuring accurate page numbering from the start.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The page forward process has started and the user file browse has been successfully opened
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to populate the user list screen with new records
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All ten user display rows (rows 1 through 10) are cleared to spaces, including User ID (USRID01I–USRID10I), First Name (FNAME01I–FNAME10I), Last Name (LNAME01I–LNAME10I), and User Type (UTYPE01I–UTYPE10I) fields for each row

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All Ten User Rows Before Populating New Page Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the user list screen with new data, all ten user display rows must be cleared to spaces to prevent stale data from a previous page from remaining visible.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user file browse has been opened at the correct starting position and all ten display rows have been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads records sequentially forward through the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Up to 10 user records are read one at a time; for each successfully read record, the User ID (SEC-USR-ID), First Name (SEC-USR-FNAME), Last Name (SEC-USR-LNAME), and User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE) are populated into the corresponding screen row (1 through 10); reading stops when 10 records are loaded or end of file is reached

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Up to Ten User Records Sequentially from User File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system reads user records sequentially from the User Security file, starting from the determined browse position, populating up to ten rows on the screen. Reading stops when ten records have been loaded or the end of the file is reached.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to read user records sequentially from the User Security file during a page forward operation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No records are successfully read (WS-IDX remains at 1, meaning zero records were populated)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next-page indicator is set to NEXT-PAGE-NO (no further pages available) and the page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is not incremented

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle No Records Found During Page Forward Load
all_rules.Rule_Description: If no user records are found during a forward page load (e.g., the search key is beyond all existing records), the system marks that no next page is available and does not increment the page number.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has successfully read at least one user record and populated the screen rows during a page forward operation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The loop to read up to 10 records has completed (WS-IDX has reached 11 or end of file was hit)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system attempts one additional sequential read (READNEXT) from the User Security file to check if any more records exist beyond the current page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Attempt to Read One Additional Record to Determine If More Pages Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully loading up to 10 user records onto the screen, the system attempts to read one additional record from the User Security file to determine whether more pages of users exist beyond the current page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has loaded up to 10 user records and attempted to read one additional record from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The additional read is successful and a record is found (USER-SEC-NOT-EOF is TRUE and no error flag is set)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next-page indicator is set to NEXT-PAGE-YES, signaling that PF8 navigation to the next page is available

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark Next Page Available When Additional Records Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: If an additional record is found beyond the 10 records currently displayed, the system marks that a next page is available, enabling the PF8 (page forward) navigation for the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has loaded up to 10 user records and attempted to read one additional record from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The additional read returns end-of-file (USER-SEC-EOF is TRUE), meaning no more records exist beyond the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next-page indicator is set to NEXT-PAGE-NO and the message 'You have reached the bottom of the page...' is set in the message field (WS-MESSAGE) to be displayed to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Mark No Next Page and Display Bottom-of-List Message When End of File Reached
all_rules.Rule_Description: If no additional record exists beyond the currently displayed 10 records, the system marks that no further pages are available and informs the user they have reached the bottom of the user list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: User records are being populated into the screen display rows during a page forward operation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The first user record is populated into row 1 and the tenth user record is populated into row 10
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID of the row-1 record is saved as the first-on-page anchor (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST) and the User ID of the row-10 record is saved as the last-on-page anchor (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-LAST)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store First and Last User IDs on Current Page for Pagination
all_rules.Rule_Description: The User ID of the first record displayed (row 1) and the User ID of the last record displayed (row 10) are saved to support accurate forward and backward page navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed reading user records for the current page forward operation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: At least one record was successfully read and populated (WS-IDX is greater than 1)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The page number counter (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is incremented by 1 (COMPUTE CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM = CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM + 1)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Increment Page Number After Successfully Loading a Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: After records have been successfully read and the page has been populated, the page number counter is incremented by 1 to reflect the newly displayed page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The page number counter (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) has been updated after loading the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to send the User List screen to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page number value from CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM is moved to the screen page number display field (PAGENUMI OF COUSR0AI) so it is visible on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Update Page Number Display on User List Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current page number is moved to the screen's page number display field so the user can see which page of the user list they are currently viewing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to display the User List screen after completing a page load operation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The SEND-USRLST-SCREEN routine is invoked
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen header is populated with: application title lines (CCDA-TITLE01, CCDA-TITLE02), current transaction ID (WS-TRANID → TRNNAMEO), program name (WS-PGMNAME → PGMNAMEO), current date formatted as MM/DD/YY (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY → CURDATEO), and current time formatted as HH:MM:SS (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS → CURTIMEO)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Header with Current Date, Time, and Program Information
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the User List screen, the screen header is populated with the current date, current time, transaction ID, and program name to provide the user with contextual information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header, user data rows, page number, and any messages have all been populated and the system is ready to present the User List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The SEND-USRLST-SCREEN routine executes the screen send
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If SEND-ERASE-YES is set, the screen is sent with a full terminal erase (ERASE option) and cursor positioned; if SEND-ERASE-NO is set, the screen is sent without erasing (overlay) with cursor positioned; in both cases the screen map COUSR0A from mapset COUSR00 is used with the output data from COUSR0AO

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Updated User List Screen to User
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all data has been populated, the User List screen is sent to the user's terminal. The screen is sent with a full erase when the erase flag is set, or as an overlay update when the erase flag is not set.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The page forward process has completed successfully with no error flag set (ERR-FLG-ON is FALSE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system returns from the PROCESS-PAGE-FORWARD routine back to PROCESS-ENTER-KEY
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID output display field (USRIDINO OF COUSR0AO) is set to a single space, clearing the search field on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear User ID Search Field Display After Successful Page Load
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a successful page forward load with no errors, the User ID search/filter display field on the screen is cleared to spaces, providing a clean input area for the next search.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the User List screen and the current page has a recorded first User ID (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF7 to navigate to the previous page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the first User ID of the current page is not blank or empty, the browse starting key (SEC-USR-ID) is set to that first User ID; otherwise, the browse starting key is set to LOW-VALUES (beginning of the user directory)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Starting Browse Position for Backward Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When PF7 is pressed to navigate backward, the system sets the browse starting position to the first User ID currently displayed on the screen. If no first User ID is recorded, browsing starts from the very beginning of the user directory.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen and presses PF7
Acceptance_Criteria.When: PF7 key is processed before any page navigation occurs
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Next-Page availability flag is set to YES, indicating that forward navigation (PF8) will be available from the previous page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enable Forward Page Availability Flag on PF7
all_rules.Rule_Description: When PF7 is pressed, the system marks that a next page (forward direction) is available, ensuring that PF8 navigation remains enabled after moving backward.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user presses PF7 on the User List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current page number is greater than 1, the system proceeds with backward page navigation; if the current page number is 1 or less, the system displays the message 'You are already at the top of the page...' and refreshes the current screen without changing the displayed data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Backward Navigation is Permitted
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before navigating backward, the system checks whether the user is beyond the first page. Backward navigation is only allowed when the current page number is greater than 1.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing page 1 of the User List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF7 to navigate to a previous page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the message 'You are already at the top of the page...' in the message area, the screen is refreshed without erasing existing content (Send-Erase flag set to NO), and the user remains on the current page with no data changes

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Top-of-List Message When Already on First Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user attempts to navigate backward but is already on the first page, the system informs them that no previous pages exist and keeps the current screen content unchanged.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current page number is greater than 1 and the browse starting key has been set to the first User ID of the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates backward page navigation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A browse session is opened on the User Security file (WS-USRSEC-FILE) positioned at the first User ID of the current page; if the browse cannot be opened, an error message 'Unable to lookup User...' is displayed and navigation is aborted

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open User Directory Browse for Backward Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: To retrieve the previous page of users, the system opens a browse session on the User Security file starting at the first User ID of the currently displayed page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The browse session is open and positioned at the first User ID of the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The triggering action is not ENTER key, PF8, or PF3
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system reads one record backward (READPREV) to move the browse position past the current page's first record, so that subsequent reads retrieve the records belonging to the previous page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Current Page's First Record Before Reading Previous Records
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating backward and the action was not triggered by ENTER or PF8, the system reads past the current page's first record so that the previous page begins with the record immediately before it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The browse session is open and positioned correctly for backward reading
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is about to populate the screen with the previous page's user records
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All 10 user display rows on the screen are cleared — each row's User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type fields are set to spaces — before any new data is written

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All User Display Rows Before Populating Previous Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the screen with the previous page's user data, all 10 display rows are cleared to spaces to prevent stale data from a prior page from remaining visible.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The browse session is open, all 10 display rows have been cleared, and the index (WS-IDX) is set to 10
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads user records in reverse order from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system reads records backward one at a time, decrementing the row index (WS-IDX) from 10 down to 1 after each successful read; reading stops when the index reaches 0, the beginning of the file is reached (EOF), or an error occurs; up to 10 records are retrieved

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Up to 10 User Records in Reverse Order
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system reads up to 10 user records backward from the User Security file to fill the previous page, stopping when 10 records are read, the beginning of the file is reached, or an error occurs.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully read backward from the User Security file and the current row index (WS-IDX) is between 1 and 10
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the screen row for the current index position
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type from the retrieved user record are placed into the screen display fields for the row number matching the current index (e.g., index 10 fills row 10 fields: USRID10I, FNAME10I, LNAME10I, UTYPE10I; index 1 fills row 1 fields: USRID01I, FNAME01I, LNAME01I, UTYPE01I)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Rows with User Data in Reverse Fill Order
all_rules.Rule_Description: As each user record is read backward, it is placed into the screen display row corresponding to the current index position, filling from row 10 down to row 1, so that the final display shows users in correct ascending order.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: User records are being populated into the screen display rows during backward navigation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates row 1 (index = 1) or row 10 (index = 10)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: When row 1 is populated, the User ID of that record is saved as the First User ID on the page (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST); when row 10 is populated, the User ID of that record is saved as the Last User ID on the page (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-LAST)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Record First and Last User IDs Displayed on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: When populating row 1 and row 10, the system saves those User IDs as the first and last User IDs on the current page respectively, enabling accurate forward and backward navigation in subsequent requests.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed reading up to 10 records backward from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The backward read loop ends
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If at least one record was found (USER-SEC-NOT-EOF is true and no error flag is set), the system proceeds to check for additional previous records; if no records were found (end-of-file reached immediately), the system displays the message 'You have reached the top of the page...' and proceeds to close the browse

all_rules.Rule_Name: Check Whether Any Previous Records Were Found
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to read records backward, the system checks whether any user records were successfully retrieved to determine whether to update the page number or display a top-of-list message.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system attempted to read user records backward but reached the beginning of the User Security file without retrieving any records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end-of-file condition is encountered during backward reading
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The message 'You have reached the top of the page...' is displayed in the message area of the User List screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Top-of-File Message When No Previous Records Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: When backward reading yields no user records, the system informs the user that the beginning of the user directory has been reached.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Records were successfully found during backward reading and the Next-Page flag is set to YES
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads one additional record backward after filling the 10 display rows
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If another record exists (USER-SEC-NOT-EOF is true, no error, and current page number is greater than 1), the system decrements the page number by 1; if no additional record exists or the page number is already 1, the system resets the page number to 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Check for Additional Previous Records Beyond Current Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: After filling the previous page with up to 10 records, the system attempts to read one more record backward to determine whether additional pages exist before the current page, which governs whether the page number should be decremented or reset to 1.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has successfully read 10 user records backward, the Next-Page flag is YES, an additional previous record exists beyond the current page, and the current page number is greater than 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system updates the page number after backward navigation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is reduced by exactly 1 (SUBTRACT 1 FROM CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decrement Page Number When Previous Records Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: When backward navigation successfully finds a previous page and additional records exist before it, the current page number is decremented by 1 to reflect the user's new position in the user directory.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed backward reading and either no additional previous record exists beyond the current page, or the current page number is already 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system updates the page number after backward navigation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is set to 1, indicating the user is now on the first page of the user directory

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Page Number to 1 When Top of List is Reached
all_rules.Rule_Description: When backward navigation reaches the beginning of the user directory or the page number cannot be decremented further, the page number is reset to 1 to accurately reflect that the user is viewing the first page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All backward record reading and page number calculations have been completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system finalizes the backward navigation process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The browse session on the User Security file (WS-USRSEC-FILE) is closed, releasing the browse cursor

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close User Directory Browse After Backward Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all backward reading operations are complete and the page number has been updated, the browse session on the User Security file is closed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The backward navigation is complete and the screen is ready to be sent to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the User List screen for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen header fields are populated with: application title line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01), application title line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02), current transaction ID (WS-TRANID), current program name (WS-PGMNAME), current date formatted as MM/DD/YY, and current time formatted as HH:MM:SS

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Header with Current Session Information
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the updated user list, the screen header is populated with the application titles, current date, current time, transaction ID, and program name to provide the user with current context information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen has been populated with the previous page's user records, the page number has been updated, and the screen header has been populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the User List screen to the user's terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The updated page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is displayed in the page number field (PAGENUMI of COUSR0AI), the screen is sent with full erase (ERASE option) when Send-Erase flag is YES, or without erase when Send-Erase flag is NO, and the cursor is positioned at the User ID input field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Updated User List with New Page Number
all_rules.Rule_Description: After backward navigation is complete, the system displays the updated User List screen showing the previous page's users along with the updated page number.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The updated User List screen has been sent to the user's terminal after backward navigation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system completes the current transaction cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is returned to CICS with the transaction ID (WS-TRANID) and the full communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) — including current page number, first and last User IDs on page, selected user, and navigation flags — preserved for the next user interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Preserve Session State and Return After Backward Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After displaying the updated user list, the system returns control to CICS while preserving the full session state in the communication area so that subsequent user actions can continue from the correct position.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the User List screen and the last displayed User ID on the current page is available (not blank or empty)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF8 to navigate to the next page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the browse starting position to the last displayed User ID on the current page, so the next page begins immediately after the current last record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Starting Position Using Last Displayed User ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: When PF8 is pressed and the last user ID on the current page is known, the system uses that user ID as the starting position for browsing the next page of users.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the User List screen and the last displayed User ID on the current page is blank or empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF8 to navigate to the next page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the browse starting position to the highest possible value (end of user list), ensuring no records are skipped and the browse starts from the furthest available position

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Starting Position to End of User List When Last User ID Is Unknown
all_rules.Rule_Description: When PF8 is pressed but no last user ID is recorded for the current page (blank or empty), the system sets the browse starting position to the highest possible value, effectively pointing to the end of the user list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the User List screen and the system has flagged that no further pages exist (next-page indicator is set to NO)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF8 to navigate to the next page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the message 'You are already at the bottom of the page...' on the current screen without refreshing or reloading the user list, and the screen is redisplayed without erasing existing content

all_rules.Rule_Name: Block Navigation When Already on Last Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When PF8 is pressed but the system has determined there are no more user records beyond the current page, navigation is blocked and an informational message is displayed to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to load the next page of users after a successful PF8 navigation request
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The next page load process begins
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All 10 user display rows on the screen (User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type for rows 1 through 10) are cleared to blank spaces before any new user data is populated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All User Display Rows Before Loading Next Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the screen with the next page of users, all 10 user display rows are cleared to spaces to prevent stale data from a previous page from remaining visible.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The browse of the User Security file has been successfully started at the position of the last displayed User ID, and the display rows have been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads user records forward from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Up to 10 user records are read and displayed on the screen, with each row showing the User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type; the first populated row's User ID is saved as the 'first user on page' and the tenth row's User ID is saved as the 'last user on page' for future navigation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Up to 10 User Records on Next Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system reads up to 10 user records sequentially from the User Security file starting after the last displayed user, and populates each screen row with the user's ID, first name, last name, and user type.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has successfully loaded up to 10 user records onto the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to read one more record beyond the 10th displayed user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If an additional record exists, the next-page indicator is set to YES (PF8 will be available for further navigation); if no additional record exists, the next-page indicator is set to NO (PF8 will be blocked with the bottom-of-page message on the next press)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine If Additional Pages Exist After Loading Next Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: After loading 10 user records, the system attempts to read one additional record to determine whether more users exist beyond the current page, setting the next-page availability indicator accordingly.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed reading user records for the next page and at least one user record was found
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The forward page load process completes
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page number is increased by 1 and the updated page number is displayed on the User List screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Increment Page Number After Successful Forward Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully loading a new page of users in the forward direction, the current page number is incremented by 1 to reflect the user's new position in the user list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The next page of users has been successfully loaded into the screen display rows and the page number has been updated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the updated User List screen to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen is fully refreshed (erased and redrawn) displaying: the updated page number, up to 10 user records (User ID, First Name, Last Name, User Type), the application titles, current transaction ID, program name, current date in MM/DD/YY format, and current time in HH:MM:SS format

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Updated User List Screen After Page Forward
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully loading the next page of users, the system refreshes the User List screen with the new user data, updated page number, current date, time, and any applicable messages.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user pressed PF8 and the next-page indicator is set to NO (no further pages exist)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the User List screen back to the user
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen is redisplayed without erasing existing content (overlay mode), showing the message 'You are already at the bottom of the page...' while retaining the currently displayed user list data unchanged

all_rules.Rule_Name: Redisplay Current Screen Without Refresh When at Bottom of List
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user attempts to navigate past the last page, the screen is redisplayed with the informational message but without a full screen erase, preserving the currently displayed user list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is about to load a forward page of user records and a starting User ID position has been determined (either a specific User ID entered by the administrator, LOW-VALUES to start from the beginning of the file, or HIGH-VALUES to start from the end)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The forward page data loading process is initiated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system opens a browse on the User Security file using the specified User ID as the starting key, enabling sequential forward reading of user records from that position

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Browse on User Security File at Specified Starting Position
all_rules.Rule_Description: When loading a forward page of users, the system opens a sequential browse on the User Security file beginning at the specified User ID, which serves as the starting position for reading user records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The browse on the User Security file has been successfully opened at the specified starting User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The navigation source is determined — if the user pressed PF8 or this is the initial page load (i.e., the action was NOT Enter key, NOT PF7, and NOT PF3)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system reads and discards one record forward to advance past the current anchor position before beginning to populate the screen rows; if the navigation source was Enter, PF7, or PF3, this skip step is bypassed and screen population begins immediately from the current position

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip One Record Forward Based on Navigation Source
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating forward via PF8 or on the initial screen load, the system skips one record forward past the current position to avoid re-displaying the last record of the previous page. When navigating via Enter, PF7, or PF3, no skip is performed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The browse is open and the system is ready to populate the user list screen with new page data, and no end-of-file condition or error has been encountered
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to load user records into the display rows
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All 10 user display rows on the screen are cleared — each row's User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type fields are set to spaces — ensuring no residual data from a prior page is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All User Display Rows Before Loading New Page Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the screen with new user records, all 10 display rows must be cleared to spaces to prevent stale data from a previous page from remaining visible on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen rows have been cleared and the system is ready to populate the user list with records from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system iterates through the User Security file reading records forward
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each successfully retrieved record (record found and no errors), the system populates the corresponding screen row and advances the row counter by 1; the reading loop continues until all 10 rows are filled (row counter reaches 11) or the end of the file is reached or an error is encountered — whichever occurs first

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Up to 10 User Records Sequentially for Page Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system reads user records sequentially from the User Security file, one at a time, and populates the screen rows until either 10 rows are filled, the end of the file is reached, or an error occurs.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully read from the User Security file with no errors
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the screen row corresponding to the current row index (1 through 10)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type from the retrieved user record are placed into the matching fields of the screen row at the current row position (rows 1 through 10)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Row with User Record Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each successfully read user record is mapped to the corresponding screen display row, filling in the User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type fields for that row position.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record is being populated into the screen display rows
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current row being populated is row 1 (the first row on the page)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID of the record being placed in row 1 is saved as the First User on Page anchor value (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST), in addition to being displayed in the User ID field of row 1 on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store First User ID on Page for Backward Navigation Anchor
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the first row (row 1) of the page is populated, the User ID of that record is saved as the 'First User on Page' anchor. This value is used as the starting position when the user navigates backward to the previous page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record is being populated into the screen display rows
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current row being populated is row 10 (the last row on the page)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID of the record being placed in row 10 is saved as the Last User on Page anchor value (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-LAST), in addition to being displayed in the User ID field of row 10 on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Last User ID on Page for Forward Navigation Anchor
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the last row (row 10) of the page is populated, the User ID of that record is saved as the 'Last User on Page' anchor. This value is used as the starting position when the user navigates forward to the next page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reading loop for populating the user list screen has completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end-of-file condition has NOT been reached AND no error condition is active, meaning at least one user record was successfully loaded into the screen rows
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page number is incremented by 1 (Page Number = Page Number + 1) to reflect the page now being displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Increment Page Number When Records Are Successfully Loaded
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the reading loop completes, if at least one user record was successfully loaded (no end-of-file and no error condition), the current page number is incremented by 1 to reflect the newly displayed page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reading loop for populating the user list screen has completed due to end-of-file or an error condition
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The row index counter is greater than 1, indicating that at least one user record was successfully loaded before the end-of-file or error was encountered
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page number is incremented by 1 (Page Number = Page Number + 1) to reflect the partial page now being displayed; if the row index is exactly 1 (no records were loaded at all), the page number is not incremented

all_rules.Rule_Name: Increment Page Number When Partial Records Loaded at End of File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the reading loop ends due to end-of-file or an error, but at least one record was loaded (row index advanced beyond 1), the page number is still incremented by 1 to correctly reflect the partial page being displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: At least one user record was successfully loaded into the screen rows and the page number has been incremented
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to read one additional record beyond the 10 displayed records
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the additional record is found successfully (no end-of-file and no error), the Next Page flag is set to YES indicating more users are available and PF8 navigation is enabled; if no additional record exists (end-of-file is reached), the Next Page flag is set to NO indicating the current page is the last page and PF8 navigation is disabled

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Whether a Next Page of Users Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully loading up to 10 records and incrementing the page number, the system attempts to read one additional record beyond the current page to determine whether more users exist. This controls whether the PF8 (next page) navigation option is available.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The reading loop for populating the user list screen has completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No user records were successfully loaded — either the end-of-file condition was reached before any record was read, or an error occurred — AND the row index counter did not advance beyond 1
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Next Page flag is set to NO, indicating there are no more users available beyond the current position and PF8 forward navigation is disabled

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Next Page Flag to NO When No Records Are Loaded
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no user records are loaded at all during the forward page read (end-of-file was reached immediately or an error occurred before any record was populated), the Next Page flag is set to NO, disabling further forward navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The forward page data loading process has completed — records have been read, screen rows populated, page number computed, and the Next Page flag has been set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system finalizes the forward page load operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The browse on the User Security file is closed; the computed page number is moved to the page number display field on the screen; the User ID search input field on the screen is cleared to a space; and the updated user list screen is sent to the administrator displaying the current page of users with the correct page number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Browse, Update Page Number, and Display User List Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all page data has been loaded and navigation flags have been set, the system closes the browse on the User Security file, updates the page number displayed on the screen, clears the User ID search input field, and sends the refreshed user list screen to the administrator.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF7 to navigate to the previous page, and the first User ID of the current page is available in the session state (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The backward page loading process begins and the system attempts to open a browse on the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The browse is opened starting at the first User ID of the current page as the starting key; if the first User ID is blank or empty, the browse starts at LOW-VALUES (beginning of file)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open User Security File Browse for Backward Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating backward through the user list, the system opens a browse session on the User Security File starting at the first User ID displayed on the current page, so that records can be read in reverse order from that position.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has attempted to open a browse on the User Security File for backward navigation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The browse open operation fails due to an unexpected condition (not a normal response and not a record-not-found response)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An error flag is set to ON, the message 'Unable to lookup User...' is displayed on the screen, the cursor is positioned on the User ID input field, and no further backward page loading is performed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Handle Browse Open Failure on User Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the User Security File cannot be opened for browsing during backward navigation, the system sets an error flag and displays an error message to the user, halting the page loading process.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The browse on the User Security File has been successfully opened at the first User ID of the current page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The key pressed was not ENTER and not PF8 (i.e., it was PF7)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: One record is read backward (READPREV) to skip the boundary record and reposition the browse cursor so that the next backward reads will return the correct previous page records

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Boundary Record to Reposition Browse for Backward Read
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating backward and the action was not triggered by ENTER or PF8, the system reads one record backward to move past the current boundary record and correctly position the browse cursor before filling the page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The browse has been successfully opened and the boundary record has been skipped if required, and no end-of-file condition has been reached and no error flag is set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to load the previous page of user records
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All 10 user display rows on the screen are cleared — each row's User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type fields are set to spaces

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All User Display Rows Before Populating Backward Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the screen with the previous page of users, all 10 display rows are cleared to spaces to ensure no stale data from the previous screen state is shown.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All 10 user display rows have been cleared and the system is ready to populate the screen with backward-read records
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The backward page population loop is initialized
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The row index is set to 10, meaning the first record read will be placed in row 10, and subsequent records will fill rows 9, 8, 7... down to row 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Row Index for Bottom-Up Screen Population
all_rules.Rule_Description: Because records are read in reverse order, the screen is filled from the bottom row (row 10) upward to row 1, so the displayed list appears in correct ascending order after backward navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The backward page population loop is active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether to continue reading the next backward record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The loop continues only if the row index is greater than 0 AND the end-of-file flag is not set AND the error flag is not set; if any of these conditions fails, the loop exits

all_rules.Rule_Name: Backward Record Read Loop Continuation Condition
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system continues reading user records backward and populating screen rows as long as there are more rows to fill (row index greater than 0) and no end-of-file or error condition has been encountered.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The backward page population loop is active and the row index is greater than 0 with no error or end-of-file condition
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the previous record from the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the read is successful, the record containing User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type is available for display; if the end of file (top of file) is reached, the end-of-file flag is set and the message 'You have reached the top of the page...' is displayed; if an unexpected error occurs, the error flag is set and 'Unable to lookup User...' is displayed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Previous User Record from User Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: Within the backward navigation loop, the system reads the previous user record from the User Security File to retrieve the user's details for display on the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully read from the User Security File during backward navigation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the screen row corresponding to the current row index
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type from the record are placed into the screen fields for that row number (1 through 10); when row index is 1, the User ID is also saved as the 'First User on Page'; when row index is 10, the User ID is also saved as the 'Last User on Page'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Row with User Record Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each successfully read user record is mapped to the corresponding screen display row, showing the user's ID, first name, last name, and user type.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully populated into the current screen row during backward navigation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system moves to the next iteration of the backward population loop
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The row index is decremented by 1 (e.g., from 10 to 9, then 9 to 8, continuing until row index reaches 0 or no more records exist)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decrement Row Index After Each Backward Record Population
all_rules.Rule_Description: After populating a screen row with a user record, the row index is decremented by 1 to move upward to the next row, ensuring records are displayed in correct ascending order.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The backward page population loop has completed (either 10 rows filled or end-of-file reached) and no error flag is set and no end-of-file flag is set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs one additional backward read on the User Security File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If a record is found, it confirms that previous records exist beyond the current page; if end-of-file is reached, it confirms the user is at the top of the list

all_rules.Rule_Name: Check for Additional Previous Records Beyond Current Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: After filling the 10 display rows, the system attempts one additional backward read to determine whether there are more user records before the current page, which determines whether further backward navigation (PF7) will be available.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The additional backward read confirmed that previous records exist beyond the current page, and the NEXT-PAGE-YES flag is set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the current page number is greater than 1
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the current page number is greater than 1, the page number is decremented by 1; if the current page number is not greater than 1, the page number is set to 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decrement Page Number When Previous Records Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system confirms that previous records exist and the current page number is greater than 1, the page number is decremented by 1 to reflect the user moving to the previous page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The additional backward read found no more previous records (end-of-file at top of list), OR the current page number is already 1 or less
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines the page number for the displayed page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The page number is set to 1, indicating the user is viewing the first page of the user list

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Page Number to 1 When Top of List is Reached
all_rules.Rule_Description: When no previous records exist beyond the current page (top of the user list has been reached), the page number is set to 1 to indicate the user is on the first page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The backward page population and page number adjustment have been completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system finalizes the backward page loading process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The browse session on the User Security File is closed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Browse on User Security File After Backward Page Load
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all backward page data loading and page number adjustments are complete, the browse session on the User Security File is closed to release the file resource.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The browse has been closed and the page number has been adjusted
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to display the updated user list screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is placed into the page number display field (PAGENUMI) on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Update Page Number Display on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: After completing the backward page load and closing the browse, the current page number is moved to the screen's page number display field so the user can see which page they are viewing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is preparing to send the user list screen to the user after backward page loading
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header population routine is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen header is populated with: Application Title 1, Application Title 2, the current Transaction ID, the current Program Name, the current date formatted as MM/DD/YY, and the current time formatted as HH:MM:SS

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Header with Current Date, Time and Program Information
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying the user list screen, the header section is populated with the application titles, current date, current time, transaction ID, and program name to provide context to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen has been populated with the previous page user records, the page number has been updated, and the header information has been populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the user list screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the SEND-ERASE flag is YES, the screen is sent with a full erase (clearing the entire screen before display); if the SEND-ERASE flag is NO, the screen is sent as an overlay without erasing; any error or informational message is displayed in the message field on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Updated User List with Previous Page Records
all_rules.Rule_Description: After populating all screen data including user rows, page number, and header, the updated user list screen is sent to the user displaying the previous page of user records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The updated user list screen has been sent to the user after backward navigation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program returns control to the CICS transaction manager
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) containing the current page number, first User ID on page, last User ID on page, next-page availability flag, selected user ID, selection flag, and program context is passed back to CICS with the current transaction ID, so the session state is available for the next user interaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Preserve Session State for Next User Interaction
all_rules.Rule_Description: After displaying the updated user list, the session state including page number, first and last user IDs on the page, navigation flags, and selected user information is preserved in the communication area so the next user interaction can continue from the correct state.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is about to be refreshed with a new page of user data, either as a result of an initial load, a forward page navigation (PF8 / Enter), or a backward page navigation (PF7), AND the file browse has been successfully opened without errors (no error flag is set), AND all 10 display rows (rows 1 through 10) currently contain data from the previous page or from a prior session
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins the process of populating the User List screen with new user records retrieved from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each of the 10 display rows (row 1 through row 10), the system must clear the following four fields to blank spaces before any new data is written: (1) User ID field for that row, (2) First Name field for that row, (3) Last Name field for that row, (4) User Type field for that row — such that after initialization all 10 rows are completely empty and ready to receive fresh user data from the current page read

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All User List Display Rows Before Loading New Page Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before displaying a new page of users on the User List screen, all 10 display rows must be completely blanked out — clearing User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type for every row. This ensures no stale data from a previous page remains visible when the new page is rendered, whether navigating forward or backward through the user directory.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been retrieved from the User Security file and the current screen row index (WS-IDX) is 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates screen row 1 with the retrieved user record details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID is displayed in row 1 of the screen, the First Name is displayed in row 1, the Last Name is displayed in row 1, the User Type is displayed in row 1, AND the User ID is additionally saved as the FIRST User ID on the page (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST) to serve as the backward navigation anchor point for PF7 pagination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Row 1 with User Record and Track First User ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the first user record is being placed on the user list screen, all user details are displayed in row 1 and the User ID is saved as the anchor point for backward pagination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been retrieved from the User Security file and the current screen row index (WS-IDX) is any value from 2 to 9 inclusive
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the corresponding screen row with the retrieved user record details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID is displayed in the corresponding row of the screen, the First Name is displayed in the corresponding row, the Last Name is displayed in the corresponding row, and the User Type is displayed in the corresponding row. No pagination anchor values are updated.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Rows 2 through 9 with User Record Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: When user records are being placed in the middle rows of the user list screen (rows 2 through 9), all user details are displayed without any additional pagination tracking.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been retrieved from the User Security file and the current screen row index (WS-IDX) is 10
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates screen row 10 with the retrieved user record details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID is displayed in row 10 of the screen, the First Name is displayed in row 10, the Last Name is displayed in row 10, the User Type is displayed in row 10, AND the User ID is additionally saved as the LAST User ID on the page (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-LAST) to serve as the forward navigation anchor point for PF8 pagination

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Row 10 with User Record and Track Last User ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the tenth user record is being placed on the user list screen, all user details are displayed in row 10 and the User ID is saved as the anchor point for forward pagination.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been retrieved from the User Security file and the current screen row index (WS-IDX) is any value other than 1 through 10
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to populate a screen row with the retrieved user record details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: No screen fields are updated, no user data is displayed, and no pagination anchor values are modified. The record is effectively skipped.

all_rules.Rule_Name: No Action for Out-of-Range Screen Row Index
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the row index falls outside the valid range of 1 to 10, no user data is populated and no screen fields are updated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is on the User List screen and has pressed the Enter key, optionally entering a User ID in the search field to filter the list
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the Enter key action and prepares to load the user list
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is reset to 0 before any records are read, ensuring the subsequent page increment results in page number 1 for the first page of results

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Page Number to Zero Before New Search or Enter Key Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses the Enter key or initiates a new user list search, the page number counter must be reset to zero before loading begins, so that the first page of results is correctly numbered as page 1 after the forward page load increments it.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has opened a browse on the User Security file and is loading records in the forward direction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All 10 user rows on the screen have been populated and at least one additional user record exists beyond the current page (end-of-file has NOT been reached and no errors occurred)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is incremented by 1, the next-page indicator is set to YES (PF8 enabled), and the updated page number is displayed on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Increment Page Number When a Full Page of Users Is Successfully Loaded
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating forward through the user list and a full page of 10 users is loaded with more records still available beyond the current page, the page number is incremented by 1 to reflect the newly displayed page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has opened a browse on the User Security file and is loading records in the forward direction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end of the user file is reached before filling all 10 rows, but at least one user record was successfully read and populated on the screen (the internal row index WS-IDX is greater than 1)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is incremented by 1, the next-page indicator is set to NO (PF8 disabled), and the updated page number is displayed on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Increment Page Number When a Partial Page of Users Is Loaded
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating forward through the user list and fewer than 10 users are loaded because the end of the user directory has been reached, but at least one user record was read, the page number is still incremented by 1 to reflect the partial page being displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has opened a browse on the User Security file and is loading records in the forward direction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end of the user file is reached immediately without reading any user records (the internal row index WS-IDX remains at 1, meaning no records were populated)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is NOT incremented and remains at its current value, the next-page indicator is set to NO (PF8 disabled), and the unchanged page number is displayed on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Keep Page Number Unchanged When No User Records Are Loaded
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating forward through the user list and no user records are found at all (e.g., the search key is beyond all existing records), the page number remains unchanged and is not incremented.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF7 to navigate backward, the system has successfully loaded 10 user records in the backward direction, and an attempt to read one more record backward was made
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The backward read confirms that more records exist before the current page (end-of-file not reached, no errors), AND the current page number is greater than 1
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is decremented by 1, and the updated page number is displayed on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Decrement Page Number When Navigating Backward to a Previous Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF7 to navigate backward and a previous page of users exists, the page number is decremented by 1 to reflect the page being navigated back to.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed PF7 to navigate backward and the system has loaded user records in the backward direction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Either the backward read reaches the beginning of the user file (end-of-file condition), an error occurs during the backward read, OR the current page number is already 1 or less
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is set to 1 (not decremented), and the page number value of 1 is displayed on the screen, indicating the user is on the first page

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Page Number to 1 When Backward Navigation Reaches the First Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating backward and the system determines that no further previous records exist or the page number is already at 1, the page number is explicitly set to 1 to ensure the display correctly reflects the first page of the user list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed loading user records in the forward direction (either full page, partial page, or no records) and the page number has been computed accordingly
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User List screen is being prepared for display after a forward navigation action (Enter key or PF8)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The computed page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is moved to the page number display field (PAGENUMI) on the User List screen, and the screen is sent to the user showing the correct page number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Updated Page Number on Screen After Forward Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After completing any forward page load operation (triggered by Enter key or PF8), the current page number must be displayed on the User List screen so the user knows which page they are viewing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed loading user records in the backward direction and the page number has been decremented or set to 1 accordingly
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User List screen is being prepared for display after a backward navigation action (PF7)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The computed page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is moved to the page number display field (PAGENUMI) on the User List screen, and the screen is sent to the user showing the correct page number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Updated Page Number on Screen After Backward Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After completing any backward page load operation (triggered by PF7), the current page number must be displayed on the User List screen so the user knows which page they are viewing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed reading user records from the User Security file to populate the current page, and the loop to fill up to 10 rows has ended
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the end-of-file condition has NOT been reached AND no error condition is active (i.e., all 10 rows were successfully populated)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If both conditions are true (not end-of-file AND no error), the page is considered fully loaded and the system proceeds to increment the page number and probe for additional records; otherwise the system evaluates whether any partial records were loaded

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine If Current Page Was Fully Populated
all_rules.Rule_Description: After attempting to load up to 10 user records onto the current page, the system evaluates whether all 10 rows were successfully filled and no errors occurred, to decide the appropriate page-number and next-page-availability logic.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current page has been fully populated with 10 user records (end-of-file not reached and no error active)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms the full-page condition is met
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is incremented by exactly 1, resulting in CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM = CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM + 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Increment Page Number When Full Page Is Loaded
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a full page of 10 user records has been successfully loaded without reaching end-of-file or encountering an error, the current page number is incremented by 1 to reflect the newly displayed page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A full page of 10 user records has been loaded and the page number has been incremented
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs one additional sequential forward read (READNEXT) on the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The result of this read (whether a record was found or end-of-file was reached) is used exclusively to set the next-page availability flag; the record itself is not displayed to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Probe Read to Detect Additional Records Beyond Current Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a full page of 10 users is loaded and the page number is incremented, the system attempts to read one additional record from the User Security file solely to determine whether more users exist beyond the current page, without displaying that record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A full page of 10 user records has been loaded and a probe read was performed on the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The probe read returns a valid record (end-of-file condition is NOT set AND no error is active)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Next Page flag is set to YES (NEXT-PAGE-YES), indicating that more user records exist beyond the current page and forward navigation (PF8) is available

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Next Page Available Flag When Additional Record Exists
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the probe read after loading a full page successfully retrieves an additional record (end-of-file not reached and no error), the system marks that a next page is available, enabling the user to navigate forward.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A full page of 10 user records has been loaded and a probe read was performed on the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The probe read does NOT return a valid record (end-of-file condition IS set OR an error is active)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Next Page flag is set to NO (NEXT-PAGE-NO), indicating the current page is the last page and forward navigation (PF8) will be disabled with the message 'You are already at the bottom of the page...'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Next Page Unavailable Flag When No Additional Record Exists After Full Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the probe read after loading a full page reaches end-of-file or encounters an error, the system marks that no further pages are available, disabling forward navigation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The page loading loop ended before filling all 10 rows (end-of-file was reached or an error occurred), meaning the full-page condition was not met
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates whether the current row index (WS-IDX) is greater than 1
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If WS-IDX is greater than 1, at least one user record was loaded and the system proceeds to increment the page number before setting Next Page flag to NO; if WS-IDX is not greater than 1, no records were loaded and the system sets Next Page flag to NO without incrementing the page number

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine If Any Records Were Loaded on a Partial Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the page was not fully populated (end-of-file was reached or an error occurred before filling all 10 rows), the system checks whether at least one record was loaded by evaluating if the row index advanced beyond its starting value of 1.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The page loading loop ended before filling all 10 rows (partial or end-of-file condition), and the row index (WS-IDX) is greater than 1, confirming at least one user record was loaded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms that WS-IDX > 1 on a partial page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is incremented by exactly 1, resulting in CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM = CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM + 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Increment Page Number When Partial Page Has At Least One Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the page was only partially populated (fewer than 10 records loaded) but at least one record was successfully loaded, the page number is still incremented by 1 to reflect the partial page being displayed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The page loading loop ended before filling all 10 rows, meaning end-of-file was reached or an error occurred during page loading (the full-page condition was not met)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes the partial or empty page outcome, regardless of whether WS-IDX is greater than 1 or not
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Next Page flag is set to NO (NEXT-PAGE-NO) unconditionally, indicating no further pages exist and forward navigation (PF8) will be disabled

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Next Page Unavailable Flag for Partial or Empty Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: Whenever the current page is not fully populated — whether it contains some records or no records at all — the system unconditionally marks that no further pages are available beyond the current page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is populating user records onto the User List screen and the current record being placed is assigned to screen row 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID of the current record is written to screen row 1
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The same User ID must also be saved as the 'First User ID on Page' (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST), which serves as the starting reference point for backward page navigation when the user presses PF7

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save First User ID as Backward Pagination Anchor When Populating Row 1
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the first user record is placed on screen row 1, the User ID must be saved as the backward pagination anchor so that pressing PF7 (Page Backward) can correctly navigate to the previous page starting from this user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is populating user records onto the User List screen and the current record is assigned to screen row 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user record data is written to screen row 1
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The First Name (SEC-USR-FNAME), Last Name (SEC-USR-LNAME), and User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE) of the user record must be stored in the corresponding screen row 1 display fields (FNAME01I, LNAME01I, UTYPE01I)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Full User Details on Screen Row 1
all_rules.Rule_Description: When populating screen row 1, all user profile details — First Name, Last Name, and User Type — must be displayed alongside the User ID to provide complete user information on the list screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is populating user records onto the User List screen and the current record is assigned to any screen row between 2 and 9 (inclusive)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user record data is written to the assigned screen row
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID (SEC-USR-ID), First Name (SEC-USR-FNAME), Last Name (SEC-USR-LNAME), and User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE) must be stored in the corresponding screen row display fields (USRIDnnI, FNAMEnnI, LNAMEnnI, UTYPEnnI where nn is the row number 02 through 09), and no pagination anchor value is updated

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Full User Details on Screen Rows 2 Through 9
all_rules.Rule_Description: For user records placed on screen rows 2 through 9, all four user details — User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type — are displayed in their respective screen row fields. No pagination anchor is saved for these rows.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is populating user records onto the User List screen and the current record being placed is assigned to screen row 10
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User ID of the current record is written to screen row 10
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The same User ID must also be saved as the 'Last User ID on Page' (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-LAST), which serves as the starting reference point for forward page navigation when the user presses PF8

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Last User ID as Forward Pagination Anchor When Populating Row 10
