all_rules.Rule_Description: When the tenth user record is placed on screen row 10, the User ID must be saved as the forward pagination anchor so that pressing PF8 (Page Forward) can correctly navigate to the next page starting after this user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is populating user records onto the User List screen and the current record is assigned to screen row 10
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user record data is written to screen row 10
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The First Name (SEC-USR-FNAME), Last Name (SEC-USR-LNAME), and User Type (SEC-USR-TYPE) of the user record must be stored in the corresponding screen row 10 display fields (FNAME10I, LNAME10I, UTYPE10I)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Full User Details on Screen Row 10
all_rules.Rule_Description: When populating screen row 10, all user profile details — First Name, Last Name, and User Type — must be displayed alongside the User ID to provide complete user information on the list screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is about to populate the User List screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen header population process is triggered
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system retrieves the current system date and time and stores it in the working date/time data area (WS-CURDATE-DATA) for subsequent formatting and display

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Current System Date and Time for Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: When populating the screen header, the system retrieves the current system date and time to be formatted and displayed on the User List screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is executing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Application title lines are being set on the User List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Title Line 1 (CCDA-TITLE01) is placed into the first title display field (TITLE01O) and Title Line 2 (CCDA-TITLE02) is placed into the second title display field (TITLE02O) on the screen output area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Application Title Lines on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The screen header must display two application title lines sourced from the application's common data area, identifying the application to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is executing and the current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction ID is being set on the User List screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is placed into the transaction name display field (TRNNAMEO) on the screen output area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Current Transaction ID on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The screen header must display the current transaction identifier so the user can identify which transaction is active during their session.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The screen header population process is executing and the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program name is being set on the User List screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is placed into the program name display field (PGMNAMEO) on the screen output area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Current Program Name on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: The screen header must display the current program name so the user can identify which program module is currently active.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system date has been retrieved and stored in the working date area (WS-CURDATE-DATA), containing separate month (WS-CURDATE-MONTH), day (WS-CURDATE-DAY), and 4-digit year (WS-CURDATE-YEAR) components
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The date is being formatted for screen header display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The month component (WS-CURDATE-MONTH) is moved to the MM position (WS-CURDATE-MM), the day component (WS-CURDATE-DAY) is moved to the DD position (WS-CURDATE-DD), and only the last 2 digits of the year (positions 3 and 4 of WS-CURDATE-YEAR) are moved to the YY position (WS-CURDATE-YY), producing a date in MM/DD/YY format (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Current Date as MM/DD/YY for Screen Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current date retrieved from the system must be formatted into MM/DD/YY format before being displayed on the screen header. The year is represented as a 2-digit value extracted from the 4-digit year.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current date has been formatted into MM/DD/YY format and stored in WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The formatted date is being set on the User List screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted date (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) is placed into the current date display field (CURDATEO) on the screen output area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Formatted Date on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the current date has been formatted into MM/DD/YY format, it must be placed into the appropriate screen header display field for the user to see.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current system time has been retrieved and stored in the working time area, containing separate hours (WS-CURTIME-HOURS), minutes (WS-CURTIME-MINUTE), and seconds (WS-CURTIME-SECOND) components
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The time is being formatted for screen header display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The hours component (WS-CURTIME-HOURS) is moved to the HH position (WS-CURTIME-HH), the minutes component (WS-CURTIME-MINUTE) is moved to the MM position (WS-CURTIME-MM), and the seconds component (WS-CURTIME-SECOND) is moved to the SS position (WS-CURTIME-SS), producing a time in HH:MM:SS format (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Current Time as HH:MM:SS for Screen Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current time retrieved from the system must be formatted into HH:MM:SS format before being displayed on the screen header, using separate hours, minutes, and seconds components.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current time has been formatted into HH:MM:SS format and stored in WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The formatted time is being set on the User List screen header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The formatted time (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS) is placed into the current time display field (CURTIMEO) on the screen output area, completing the screen header population

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Formatted Time on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the current time has been formatted into HH:MM:SS format, it must be placed into the appropriate screen header display field for the user to see.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is about to be sent to the terminal and the screen header needs to be populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screen header information
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The first application title (CCDA-TITLE01) is placed in the TITLE01O field of the screen output area, and the second application title (CCDA-TITLE02) is placed in the TITLE02O field of the screen output area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Application Titles on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: When preparing the User List screen for display, the system populates the screen header with the standard application titles defined in the common demo area.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is about to be sent to the terminal and the screen header needs to be populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the transaction and program identification fields in the header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction ID (WS-TRANID) is placed in the TRNNAMEO field of the screen output area, and the current program name (WS-PGMNAME) is placed in the PGMNAMEO field of the screen output area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Transaction ID and Program Name on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: When preparing the User List screen for display, the system populates the screen header with the current transaction identifier and program name to provide context to the user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is about to be sent to the terminal and the screen header needs to be populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system retrieves the current date using the system date function and formats it
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current date is extracted from the system, the month portion is placed in WS-CURDATE-MM, the day portion is placed in WS-CURDATE-DD, the last two digits of the year are placed in WS-CURDATE-YY, and the fully formatted date in MM/DD/YY format (WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY) is placed in the CURDATEO field of the screen output area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Display Current Date on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: When preparing the User List screen for display, the system retrieves the current system date and formats it as MM/DD/YY before placing it in the screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is about to be sent to the terminal and the screen header needs to be populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system retrieves the current time using the system date function and formats it
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current time is extracted from the system, the hours portion is placed in WS-CURTIME-HH, the minutes portion is placed in WS-CURTIME-MM, the seconds portion is placed in WS-CURTIME-SS, and the fully formatted time in HH:MM:SS format (WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS) is placed in the CURTIMEO field of the screen output area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Display Current Time on Screen Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: When preparing the User List screen for display, the system retrieves the current system time and formats it as HH:MM:SS before placing it in the screen header.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is about to be sent to the terminal and a message may have been set during processing (e.g., invalid key, already at top/bottom of page, invalid selection, or unable to look up user)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the screen for display
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current value of WS-MESSAGE (which may contain an informational or error message, or spaces if no message) is moved to the ERRMSGO field of the screen output area (COUSR0AO), making it visible to the user on the screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Message or Error Text on Screen
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before sending the User List screen to the terminal, any informational or error message that has been set during processing is placed in the screen's message display field so the user can see feedback about their last action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen header has been populated with titles, transaction ID, program name, current date, current time, and any message text, AND the Send-Erase flag (SEND-ERASE-YES) is set to TRUE indicating a first-time or fresh display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the User List screen (map COUSR0A from mapset COUSR00) to the terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen is sent with the ERASE option, which clears the entire terminal screen before displaying the new content; the screen shows up to 10 users each with their User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type, along with the current page number and any message or error text, and the cursor is positioned at the User ID input field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send User List Screen with Full Screen Erase on First Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User List screen is being displayed for the first time in a transaction cycle or after a fresh data load, the screen is sent to the terminal with a full erase to clear any previously displayed content before showing the new user list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen header has been populated with titles, transaction ID, program name, current date, current time, and any message text, AND the Send-Erase flag (SEND-ERASE-YES) is set to FALSE (SEND-ERASE-NO) indicating a subsequent or overlay display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system sends the User List screen (map COUSR0A from mapset COUSR00) to the terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen is sent without the ERASE option, overlaying the existing terminal screen content with the updated user list; the screen shows up to 10 users each with their User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type, along with the current page number and any message or error text, and the cursor is positioned at the User ID input field

all_rules.Rule_Name: Send User List Screen Without Erase for Subsequent Displays
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the User List screen is being refreshed or updated (not a first-time display), the screen is sent to the terminal without erasing the existing content, providing a smoother update experience.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is being prepared for display after user records have been retrieved from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The screen content is assembled and sent to the terminal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The screen displays up to 10 user rows, where each row contains: User ID (USRID01I–USRID10I), First Name (FNAME01I–FNAME10I), Last Name (LNAME01I–LNAME10I), and User Type (UTYPE01I–UTYPE10I); the current page number (PAGENUMI) is shown; any rows without data are displayed as blank spaces; and a selection field (SEL0001I–SEL0010I) is available next to each user row for the user to enter an action code

all_rules.Rule_Name: User List Screen Content Definition
all_rules.Rule_Description: The User List screen presents a paginated list of up to 10 users at a time, displaying key identifying and classification information for each user, along with navigation context and feedback messages.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is loading users forward through the User Security file and has been reading user records sequentially
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A read-next operation on the User Security file returns an end-of-file condition, indicating no more user records exist beyond the current position
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the End-of-File (EOF) flag to TRUE, marking that the bottom of the user list has been reached and no further forward reads should be attempted

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect End of User List During Forward Page Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system attempts to read the next user record during forward page loading and no more records exist in the User Security file, the system must detect this end-of-file condition and mark the list as fully traversed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is performing a forward page load of the User List screen and the EOF flag has been set to TRUE because no more user records exist in the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end-of-file condition is confirmed during the read-next operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the screen message to 'You have reached the bottom of the page...' to notify the user that the end of the user list has been reached

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Bottom-of-Page Message When End of User List is Reached
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the end of the User Security file is encountered during forward page loading, the system must inform the user that they have reached the last available user record by displaying an appropriate notification message on the User List screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed loading users for the current page during a forward page navigation and the EOF flag is TRUE (no more records exist) or an error condition is present
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The check for additional records beyond the current page confirms that the User Security file has no more records (EOF condition is active)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the Next Page indicator to NO, which will prevent PF8 (page forward) from loading another page and will display the bottom-of-page message if PF8 is pressed again

all_rules.Rule_Name: Disable Forward Paging When End of User List is Reached
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system detects that no more user records exist beyond the current page during forward navigation, the Next Page indicator must be set to NO to prevent the user from attempting to navigate further forward.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The EOF flag is set to TRUE during a forward read of the User Security file, and the message 'You have reached the bottom of the page...' has been set
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end-of-file condition is detected during the read-next operation on the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the User List screen (COUSR0A) with the bottom-of-page message 'You have reached the bottom of the page...' visible to the user, showing all user records that were successfully loaded before the end of file was reached

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display User List Screen with Bottom-of-Page Notification
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the end of the User Security file is reached during forward page loading, the system must immediately display the User List screen along with the bottom-of-page notification message so the user is aware they are viewing the last available users.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the User List screen and the current page number is greater than 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF7 to navigate to the previous page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the first User ID of the current page is blank or empty, the system sets the browse start position to the beginning of the user list (LOW-VALUES); otherwise, the system sets the browse start position to the first User ID displayed on the current page, and then opens a browse session on the User Security file starting at that position

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initiate Backward Paging from Current Page Position
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses PF7 to page backward, the system determines the correct starting position in the user list. If the first user ID of the current page is available, browsing starts from that user ID; otherwise, browsing starts from the very beginning of the user list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is viewing the User List screen and the current page number is 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The user presses PF7 to navigate to the previous page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system does not attempt backward navigation, displays the message 'You are already at the top of the page...' on the screen, and refreshes the current screen without erasing it

all_rules.Rule_Name: Already at Top of List - PF7 Blocked
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user attempts to page backward but is already on page 1, the system prevents further backward navigation and informs the user they are at the top of the list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has initiated a backward page navigation and attempts to open a browse session on the User Security file at the specified starting User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The User Security file browse position is not found (the specified User ID does not exist in the file)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the end-of-file indicator to TRUE, displays the message 'You are at the top of the page...' on the screen, and sends the updated User List screen to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: User File Browse Start Position Not Found - Top of List Notification
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system attempts to open a browse session on the User Security file starting at the specified User ID but the position is not found, it means the system is already at or beyond the top of the user list. The user is notified accordingly.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has successfully opened a browse session on the User Security file for backward navigation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The key pressed was not ENTER and not PF8
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system reads one record backward (skipping it) before starting to populate the screen rows, ensuring the page boundary is correctly positioned

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip One Record Backward Before Populating Previous Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating backward and the action was not triggered by ENTER or PF8, the system skips one record backward before beginning to populate the screen. This ensures the correct set of 10 records is displayed for the previous page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has successfully positioned the browse cursor on the User Security file for backward navigation and all 10 screen rows have been cleared
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads previous records from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each record successfully retrieved (up to 10), the system populates the corresponding screen row (starting from row 10 down to row 1) with the user's User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type; the User ID of the record placed in row 1 is saved as the 'First User ID on Page' and the User ID placed in row 10 is saved as the 'Last User ID on Page'; reading continues until 10 rows are filled or the top of the file is reached

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Previous Page Screen Rows in Reverse Order
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system reads up to 10 user records backward from the User Security file and populates the screen rows in reverse order (from row 10 down to row 1), so that the final display shows users in correct ascending order.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is reading user records backward from the User Security file to populate the previous page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reaches the beginning of the User Security file (no more previous records exist)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the end-of-file indicator to TRUE and displays the message 'You have reached the top of the page...' on the User List screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Top of User File Reached During Backward Read - Notification
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system is reading records backward to populate the previous page and reaches the beginning of the User Security file, it sets the end-of-file indicator and notifies the user that the top of the list has been reached.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has finished reading records backward and populating the screen rows for the previous page
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether additional records exist before the current page position
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the NEXT-PAGE-YES flag is set AND more previous records exist AND the current page number is greater than 1, the system subtracts 1 from the current page number; otherwise the system sets the page number to 1; the updated page number is then displayed on the User List screen and the screen is sent to the user

all_rules.Rule_Name: Page Number Decrement on Successful Backward Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After successfully reading records for the previous page, the system adjusts the page number. If more records exist before the current page and the page number is greater than 1, the page number is decremented by 1; otherwise it is reset to 1.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has successfully opened a browse session on the User Security file and the end-of-file indicator is not set and no error flag is active
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system is about to populate the screen rows for the previous page
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears all 10 screen rows by setting User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type fields to spaces for each row (rows 1 through 10) before reading and populating any user data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All Screen Rows Before Populating Previous Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the screen with the previous page of users, all 10 display rows are cleared to spaces to prevent stale data from a prior page from remaining visible.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user is navigating the User List screen and a page operation (forward or backward) has been performed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A forward page navigation completes successfully with at least one user record read, the page number is incremented by 1 and stored; when a backward page navigation completes and a previous record exists and the current page is greater than 1, the page number is decremented by 1; when navigating backward and no previous record exists or the page is already 1, the page number is set to 1
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The updated page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is saved into the communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) and carried forward to the next user interaction, ensuring the screen displays the correct page number on re-entry

all_rules.Rule_Name: Preserve Current Page Number in Session State
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system tracks and saves the current page number in the session communication area so that when the user returns to the User List screen, the correct page context is maintained.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered an action code ('U', 'u', 'D', or 'd') next to one of the 10 displayed users on the User List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system scans selection fields SEL0001I through SEL0010I in order from row 1 to row 10, and the first non-blank, non-low-value selection field is found at row N (where N is 1 through 10)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The corresponding User ID from field USRID0NI (e.g., USRID01I for row 1, USRID02I for row 2, up to USRID10I for row 10) is moved into CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED and packaged into the communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) for use by the invoked program; if no selection is made, CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED is set to spaces

all_rules.Rule_Name: Preserve Selected User ID in Session State
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user selects one of the displayed users by entering an action code, the selected user's ID is captured and saved in the session communication area so it is available to the target program (Update or Delete).

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has entered an action code in one of the selection fields (SEL0001I through SEL0010I) on the User List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system identifies the first non-blank, non-low-value selection field among SEL0001I through SEL0010I
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The value of that selection field (expected to be 'U', 'u', 'D', or 'd') is moved into CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG and saved in the communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA); if no selection field contains a value, CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG is set to spaces

all_rules.Rule_Name: Preserve User Action Selection Flag in Session State
all_rules.Rule_Description: The action code entered by the user ('U' for Update or 'D' for Delete) is saved in the session communication area alongside the selected user ID, so the target program knows which operation to perform.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is populating the User List screen with user records retrieved from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The first user record (row index WS-IDX = 1) is being populated on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID (SEC-USR-ID) of that first record is saved into CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST within the communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), so that when PF7 is pressed, the backward browse starts from this User ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Preserve First User ID on Current Page for Backward Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The User ID of the first user displayed on the current page is saved in the session state. This anchor point is used when the user presses PF7 to navigate backward, ensuring the previous page is retrieved correctly relative to the current page's starting position.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is populating the User List screen with user records retrieved from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The tenth user record (row index WS-IDX = 10) is being populated on the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID (SEC-USR-ID) of that tenth record is saved into CDEMO-CU00-USRID-LAST within the communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), so that when PF8 is pressed, the forward browse starts from this User ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Preserve Last User ID on Current Page for Forward Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The User ID of the last user displayed on the current page is saved in the session state. This anchor point is used when the user presses PF8 to navigate forward, ensuring the next page is retrieved correctly relative to the current page's ending position.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has finished loading up to 10 user records for the current page during a forward or backward page operation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: During forward navigation: after populating up to 10 rows, the system attempts to read one additional record — if that record exists, the Next Page flag is set to YES (NEXT-PAGE-YES); if no additional record exists or an end-of-file condition is reached, the flag is set to NO (NEXT-PAGE-NO); during backward navigation: the Next Page flag is initialized to YES (NEXT-PAGE-YES) at the start of PF7 processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Next Page availability flag is saved in the communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA); on the next interaction, if the flag is NO and the user presses PF8, the message 'You are already at the bottom of the page...' is displayed and no navigation occurs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Preserve Next Page Availability Flag in Session State
all_rules.Rule_Description: After loading a page of users, the system checks whether additional user records exist beyond the current page and saves this availability indicator in the session state. This flag controls whether PF8 (next page) navigation is permitted on the next interaction.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is being accessed for the first time within the current session (the re-entry marker CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is not yet set)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program detects that CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is FALSE (NOT CDEMO-PGM-REENTER), indicating this is the initial entry
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: CDEMO-PGM-REENTER is set to TRUE and saved in the communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA); on all subsequent interactions, the program bypasses screen initialization and proceeds directly to receiving and processing user input

all_rules.Rule_Name: Preserve Program Re-Entry Marker in Session State
all_rules.Rule_Description: A re-entry marker is set in the session communication area on the first visit to the User List screen. On all subsequent interactions, this marker signals that the screen has already been initialized, directing the program to receive user input rather than re-initializing the screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All screen processing for the current user interaction has completed, including any page navigation, user selection, or error handling
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program prepares to return control to the CICS transaction manager
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA) contains the fully updated session state including: current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM), selected user ID (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED), user action flag (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG), first user ID on page (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST), last user ID on page (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-LAST), next page availability flag (NEXT-PAGE-YES/NO), and re-entry marker (CDEMO-PGM-REENTER); this packaged state is passed as the COMMAREA in the CICS RETURN command

all_rules.Rule_Name: Package All Session State into Communication Area
all_rules.Rule_Description: All session state elements — including page number, selected user ID, selection flag, first and last user IDs on the page, next page availability flag, and re-entry marker — are collectively stored within the communication area (CARDDEMO-COMMAREA), which serves as the session state container passed between interactions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All business processing for the current user interaction on the User List screen has been completed — including page navigation, user selection handling, error messaging, and screen display
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reaches the end of the main processing logic (MAIN-PARA)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Control is returned to the CICS transaction identified by WS-TRANID, with the fully updated CARDDEMO-COMMAREA passed as the communication area, preserving all session state (page number, selected user, selection flag, first/last user IDs, next page flag, re-entry marker) so the next user interaction resumes correctly from the current state

all_rules.Rule_Name: Return Control to Transaction with Updated Session State
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all screen processing is complete, the program returns control to the CICS transaction manager, passing the fully updated communication area. This ensures the session remains active and all state is available when the user performs the next action.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is displaying up to 10 users, each with a selectable action field (SEL) and a corresponding User ID field (USRID), and the user has pressed the Enter key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system scans selection fields SEL0001 through SEL0010 in sequential order from row 1 to row 10 and finds the first row where the selection field contains a value that is neither blank (spaces) nor empty (low-values)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system captures the selection code from that row into the User Selection Flag (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG) and the User ID from the same row into the Selected User ID (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED); if no row has a non-blank selection code, both the User Selection Flag and Selected User ID are set to spaces

all_rules.Rule_Name: Capture First Non-Blank User Selection from List
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses Enter on the User List screen, the system scans all 10 displayed user rows in order (row 1 through row 10) and captures the selection code and corresponding User ID from the first row where a non-blank selection code has been entered. If no row has a selection code entered, both the selection flag and selected user ID are cleared.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed scanning all 10 selection rows after the user pressed Enter
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether the User Selection Flag (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG) is not blank or empty AND the Selected User ID (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED) is not blank or empty
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If both the User Selection Flag and the Selected User ID contain valid non-blank, non-empty values, the system proceeds to evaluate the selection code for action routing; if either value is blank or empty, the system skips action routing and continues directly to search and page processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate That Both Selection Code and User ID Are Present Before Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before routing the user to an action screen, the system verifies that both a selection code and a User ID have been successfully captured. If either is missing or blank, the system bypasses action routing and proceeds directly to search and page processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Both the User Selection Flag and the Selected User ID have been captured with valid non-blank values, and the User Selection Flag contains the value 'U' or 'u' (case-insensitive)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the User Selection Flag and matches it to 'U' or 'u'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the target program to 'COUSR02C' (Update User), records the current transaction ID as the originating transaction, records the current program name as the originating program, sets the program context to 0, and transfers full control to the Update User program (COUSR02C) passing the complete session communication area including the selected User ID; the current program ends and does not continue further processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Navigate to Update User Screen When 'U' Is Selected
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters 'U' or 'u' as the selection code next to a user on the list, the system transfers control to the Update User program, passing the selected User ID and current session context so the administrator can update that user's details.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Both the User Selection Flag and the Selected User ID have been captured with valid non-blank values, and the User Selection Flag contains the value 'D' or 'd' (case-insensitive)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the User Selection Flag and matches it to 'D' or 'd'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system sets the target program to 'COUSR03C' (Delete User), records the current transaction ID as the originating transaction, records the current program name as the originating program, sets the program context to 0, and transfers full control to the Delete User program (COUSR03C) passing the complete session communication area including the selected User ID; the current program ends and does not continue further processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Navigate to Delete User Screen When 'D' Is Selected
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters 'D' or 'd' as the selection code next to a user on the list, the system transfers control to the Delete User program, passing the selected User ID and current session context so the administrator can delete that user.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Both the User Selection Flag and the Selected User ID have been captured with valid non-blank values, and the User Selection Flag contains a value other than 'U', 'u', 'D', or 'd'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the User Selection Flag and finds no match to any valid selection code
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system displays the error message 'Invalid selection. Valid values are U and D' on the screen, sets the cursor focus to the User ID input field, and continues to search and page processing without transferring control to any other program

all_rules.Rule_Name: Display Error for Invalid Selection Code Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user enters a selection code that is not 'U', 'u', 'D', or 'd', the system rejects the action, displays an error message informing the user of the valid options, and continues to search and page processing without navigating away from the User List screen.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The user has pressed the Enter key on the User List screen and all 10 selection fields (SEL0001 through SEL0010) are blank or empty
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines that the User Selection Flag (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SEL-FLG) is blank or empty OR the Selected User ID (CDEMO-CU00-USR-SELECTED) is blank or empty after scanning all rows
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system does not attempt any action routing, clears both the User Selection Flag and the Selected User ID to spaces, and proceeds directly to search and page processing to load and display the user list

all_rules.Rule_Name: Bypass Action Routing and Proceed to Page Processing When No Selection Is Made
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the user presses Enter without entering any selection code next to any of the displayed users, the system skips all action routing logic and proceeds directly to search and page processing to refresh or filter the user list.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is about to load a forward page of users onto the User List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The page-forward loading process begins
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The row counter is set to 1, ensuring user records will be populated starting from the first display row

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Row Counter Before Loading User List Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before loading users onto the screen, the row counter must be initialized to position 1 so that user records are populated starting from the first row of the display.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is in the process of loading user records onto the User List screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: Each iteration of the loading loop is evaluated
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the row counter has exceeded 10 (all rows filled) OR the end of the user security file has been reached, the loading loop stops; otherwise the loop continues reading the next user record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Continue Loading Users Until 10 Rows Filled or End of File Reached
all_rules.Rule_Description: The user list page loading loop must continue reading and displaying user records until either all 10 display rows are filled or there are no more user records available in the user security file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The loading loop is active and fewer than 10 rows have been filled and the end of file has not been reached
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system attempts to read the next user record from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The next sequential user record (containing User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type) is retrieved from the User Security file; if no more records exist, the end-of-file condition is set and the loading loop terminates

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Next User Record Sequentially from User Security File
all_rules.Rule_Description: During forward page loading, the system reads user records one at a time in sequential order from the User Security file to populate the display rows.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file and the current row number is between 2 and 9 (inclusive)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates the current display row
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type from the retrieved record are written to the corresponding fields of the current screen row (rows 2 through 9)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Screen Row with Retrieved User Record Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a user record is successfully retrieved from the User Security file, the system populates the corresponding screen display row with the user's details including User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file and the current row counter is at position 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates display row 1
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type are written to screen row 1, AND the User ID is additionally saved as the FIRST User ID on the current page (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-FIRST) to serve as the backward navigation anchor

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Row 1 and Save as First User ID for Backward Pagination
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the first user record is loaded onto the screen (row 1), the system must save that user's ID as the pagination anchor so that the system knows where to start when the user navigates backward to the previous page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully retrieved from the User Security file and the current row counter is at position 10
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system populates display row 10
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type are written to screen row 10, AND the User ID is additionally saved as the LAST User ID on the current page (CDEMO-CU00-USRID-LAST) to serve as the forward navigation anchor

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Row 10 and Save as Last User ID for Forward Pagination
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the tenth user record is loaded onto the screen (row 10), the system must save that user's ID as the pagination anchor so that the system knows where to start when the user navigates forward to the next page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A user record has been successfully retrieved and its data has been populated onto the current screen row
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The row population for the current record is complete
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The row counter is incremented by 1 (e.g., from row N to row N+1), positioning the system to populate the next display row on the subsequent loop iteration

all_rules.Rule_Name: Advance Row Counter After Each Successfully Populated Row
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each user record is successfully retrieved and its data is populated onto the current screen row, the row counter must be incremented by 1 to move to the next available display row.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is loading user records onto the User List screen and a read attempt on the User Security file returns no record because the end of the file has been reached
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end-of-file condition is detected during the loading loop
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The end-of-file flag (USER-SEC-EOF) is set to TRUE, the loading loop terminates immediately, and the screen is displayed with only the rows that were successfully populated (remaining rows stay blank)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Stop Page Loading When End of User File is Reached
all_rules.Rule_Description: When there are no more user records available in the User Security file during forward page loading, the loading process must stop regardless of how many rows have been filled, and the page is displayed with however many users were retrieved.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A forward page load has been triggered (by Enter, PF7, PF8, or First Load), and a starting User ID boundary position has been set (either a specific User ID entered by the user, LOW-VALUES for start of file, or the last User ID from the current page)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates the forward page data loading process
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system opens a browse session on the User Security File positioned at the specified starting User ID, making records available for sequential forward reading from that position onward

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open User List Browse from Specified Starting Position
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a forward page load is triggered, the system opens a browse session on the User Security File starting at the User ID that was specified as the boundary position, enabling sequential forward reading of user records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A browse session has been successfully opened on the User Security File at the specified starting User ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the navigation key that triggered the forward page load
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the triggering key was PF8 (Next Page) or First Load (any key other than Enter, PF7, or PF3), the system proceeds to skip one record forward to advance past the boundary position; if the triggering key was Enter, PF7, or PF3, the system proceeds directly to check record availability without skipping any record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine Record Skip Requirement Based on Navigation Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system evaluates which navigation key triggered the forward page load to determine whether the browse position needs to advance past the current boundary record before loading the page, or whether it is already at the correct starting position.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A browse session is open on the User Security File, and the forward page load was triggered by PF8 (Next Page) or by First Load (i.e., the triggering key was not Enter, PF7, or PF3)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines it must advance past the current boundary position
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system reads the next record from the User Security File (READNEXT), advancing the browse cursor one position forward past the boundary User ID; this record is not displayed but serves only to reposition the browse cursor so the subsequent page load begins at the correct next record

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip One Record Forward to Advance Past Boundary Position
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the forward page load is triggered by PF8 (Next Page) or First Load, the system reads and discards one record to advance the browse cursor past the current boundary User ID, ensuring the new page begins with the record immediately following the boundary position.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The browse cursor has been positioned either directly at the starting User ID (Enter/PF7/PF3 path) or advanced one record past the boundary (PF8/First Load path)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system checks whether more user records are available at the current browse position
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If records are available (end-of-file has not been reached and no error condition exists), the system proceeds to clear all 10 user display rows and load the next page of users; if no records are available (end-of-file reached), the system ends the forward page load with no records to display and the screen rows remain as previously shown

all_rules.Rule_Name: Verify Record Availability Before Loading Page Data
all_rules.Rule_Description: After positioning the browse cursor (with or without skipping), the system checks whether any user records are available to be loaded onto the screen before proceeding to clear and populate the display rows.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Records are confirmed to be available for the new page (end-of-file not reached and no error condition), and the system is about to load a new set of user records onto the screen
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the display rows for the new page of user data
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system clears all 10 user display rows by setting the following fields to spaces for each row 1 through 10: User ID (USRID01I–USRID10I), First Name (FNAME01I–FNAME10I), Last Name (LNAME01I–LNAME10I), and User Type (UTYPE01I–UTYPE10I), after which the system proceeds to load the available user records into the now-empty rows

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear All Ten User Display Rows Before Loading New Page
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before populating the screen with the new page of user records, the system clears all 10 display rows (User ID, First Name, Last Name, and User Type) to spaces, ensuring no stale data from the previous page remains visible when fewer than 10 records are available for the new page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has successfully opened a browse session on the User Security file starting at the current boundary User ID, and the backward page loading process has begun
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The navigation source is evaluated: (1) The user pressed PF7 to navigate backward, OR (2) The user pressed Enter or PF8 which triggered a backward page load
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the user pressed PF7: the system reads one record backward from the current boundary position to skip past the boundary record and correctly reposition the file cursor before loading the previous page of users; If the user pressed Enter or PF8: the system skips the repositioning step entirely and proceeds directly to clear all 10 user display rows and load the previous page data in reverse order

all_rules.Rule_Name: Backward Page Navigation Repositioning Based on Key Pressed
all_rules.Rule_Description: When navigating backward through the user list, the system determines whether to skip the current boundary record before loading the previous page. If the user pressed PF7, the system reads one record backward to reposition past the current boundary user, ensuring the correct set of previous users is loaded. If the user pressed Enter or PF8, no repositioning is needed and the system proceeds directly to load the previous page data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The User List screen is being populated in a forward page navigation, the row index has reached 11 (all 10 rows filled), and the end of the User Security file has NOT been reached
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system determines that a full page of 10 user records was successfully loaded
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is incremented by 1

all_rules.Rule_Name: Full Page Loaded – Increment Page Number
all_rules.Rule_Description: When all 10 user rows on the current page have been successfully populated from the User Security file without reaching the end of file, the current page number is incremented by 1 to reflect the newly loaded page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All 10 user rows have been successfully populated and the page number has been incremented by 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system performs a forward read of one additional record from the User Security file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The result of this read (record found or end of file) is used exclusively to set the Next Page availability flag, and the record itself is not displayed on screen

all_rules.Rule_Name: Full Page Loaded – Attempt to Read Additional Record to Determine Next Page Availability
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a full page of 10 users is loaded and the page number is incremented, the system attempts to read one additional record from the User Security file solely to determine whether a next page of users exists, without displaying that record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All 10 user rows have been populated, the page number has been incremented, and an attempt to read one additional record from the User Security file is made
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The additional record read is successful (a record is found beyond the current page)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Next Page Flag (NEXT-PAGE-YES) is set to TRUE, indicating more pages of users are available for forward navigation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Additional Record Found – Enable Next Page Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: If an additional record is successfully read from the User Security file after a full page of 10 users is loaded, the Next Page flag is set to YES, indicating that more users are available and the PF8 (page forward) navigation should be enabled.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All 10 user rows have been populated, the page number has been incremented, and an attempt to read one additional record from the User Security file is made
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The additional record read reaches the end of the User Security file (no further records exist)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Next Page Flag (NEXT-PAGE-NO) is set to TRUE, indicating no more pages of users are available and forward navigation is disabled

all_rules.Rule_Name: No Additional Record Found – Disable Next Page Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: If no additional record is found after a full page of 10 users is loaded (end of file is reached), the Next Page flag is set to NO, indicating that the current page is the last page and PF8 (page forward) navigation should be disabled.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A forward page navigation is in progress, the end of the User Security file was reached before 10 rows were filled, and the row index (WS-IDX) is greater than 1 indicating at least one user record was successfully loaded
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the partial page condition after the read loop exits due to end of file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) is incremented by 1, AND the Next Page Flag (NEXT-PAGE-NO) is set to TRUE, indicating this partial page is the last page and no further forward navigation is possible

all_rules.Rule_Name: Partial Page Loaded – Increment Page Number and Disable Next Page Navigation
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the end of the User Security file is reached before all 10 rows are filled, but at least 1 user record was loaded (row index advanced beyond its starting value of 1), the page number is incremented by 1 and the Next Page flag is set to NO, indicating this is the last partial page.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A forward page navigation is in progress, the end of the User Security file was reached before any rows were filled, and the row index (WS-IDX) is NOT greater than 1 (equals 1, meaning zero records were loaded)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the empty page condition after the read loop exits due to end of file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Next Page Flag (NEXT-PAGE-NO) is set to TRUE indicating no forward navigation is possible, AND the current page number (CDEMO-CU00-PAGE-NUM) remains unchanged (is NOT incremented)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Zero Records Loaded – Disable Next Page Navigation Without Incrementing Page Number
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the end of the User Security file is reached immediately with no user records loaded at all (row index remains at its initial value of 1, meaning it never advanced), the Next Page flag is set to NO and the page number is left unchanged.

description:
COUSR00C is a CICS online program within the CardDemo application that displays a paginated list of users from the USRSEC security file, showing up to 10 users per page with their ID, name, and type. The program allows administrators to navigate through user records using PF7 (backward) and PF8 (forward) keys, and to select a user for update (U) or delete (D) operations by transferring control to the respective programs (COUSR02C or COUSR03C). It is a main/driver program that manages its own screen flow and communicates with other programs via a shared communication area.
- **Execution Environment**: Online (CICS) - **Database Access**: VSAM/CICS File - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main/Driver module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Program Initialization - Initialize all flags and variables to their default states, including error flag (off), end-of-file flag (not EOF), next-page flag (no), and erase flag (yes). Clear message and error message fields. 2: Session Validation - Check if a valid user session exists (communication area length). If no session exists, redirect the user to the sign-on screen (COSGN00C). 3: First-Time Screen Display - On the first entry into the program, mark the program as re-entered, clear the screen output area, and load the first page of users to display. 4: User Input Reception - Receive the user list screen input, capturing any selection flags, user ID search criteria, and function key pressed by the user. 5: Function Key Routing - Evaluate which key the user pressed (Enter, PF3, PF7, PF8, or other) and route to the appropriate processing logic. 6: Invalid Key Handling - If an unsupported key is pressed, set an error flag and display the message 'Invalid key' on the user list screen. 7: Navigation to Admin Menu - When PF3 is pressed, transfer control back to the administration menu screen (COADM01C). 8: User Selection Detection - When Enter is pressed, scan all 10 rows on the screen to identify if the user has entered a selection code (U or D) next to any listed user. 9: Navigate to Update User - If the user selects 'U' or 'u' next to a user record, transfer control to the Update User program (COUSR02C) passing the selected user ID. 10: Navigate to Delete User - If the user selects 'D' or 'd' next to a user record, transfer control to the Delete User program (COUSR03C) passing the selected user ID. 11: Invalid Selection Validation - If the user enters a selection code other than U or D, display the message 'Invalid selection. Valid values are U and D'. 12: User ID Search Criteria Handling - Capture the user ID entered in the search field; if blank, start browsing from the beginning of the user file. 13: Page Forward Navigation (Enter Key) - Reset the page number to zero and load the next page of users starting from the specified or default user ID. 14: Page Backward Navigation (PF7) - When PF7 is pressed, check if the current page number is greater than 1. If yes, navigate to the previous page of users. If already on the first page, display 'You are already at the top of the page...'. 15: Page Forward Navigation (PF8) - When PF8 is pressed, check if a next page exists. If yes, navigate to the next page of users. If already on the last page, display 'You are already at the bottom of the page...'. 16: Forward Page Data Loading - Open a browse on the user security file starting at the specified user ID, read up to 10 user records sequentially, populate the screen rows, and determine if a further next page exists. 17: Backward Page Data Loading - Open a browse on the user security file starting at the specified user ID, read up to 10 user records in reverse order, populate the screen rows in reverse, and adjust the page number accordingly. 18: Screen Row Initialization - Clear all 10 user rows on the screen (user ID, first name, last name, user type) before populating with new data. 19: User Record Population - For each user record read, populate the corresponding screen row with the user's ID, first name, last name, and user type. Track the first and last user IDs displayed for pagination purposes. 20: Page Number Tracking - Maintain and display the current page number on the screen, incrementing when moving forward and decrementing when moving backward. 21: Next Page Availability Indicator - After loading a page, attempt to read one additional record to determine if more records exist beyond the current page, setting the next-page flag accordingly. 22: First and Last User ID Tracking - Store the user ID of the first record and the last record displayed on the current page to support forward and backward pagination. 23: Screen Header Population - Populate the screen header with the application title, transaction ID, program name, current date (MM/DD/YY), and current time (HH:MM:SS). 24: User List Screen Display - Send the populated user list screen to the terminal, displaying up to 10 users with their IDs, names, and types, along with the page number and any messages. 25: End of File Notification - When the bottom of the user list is reached while paging forward, display the message 'You have reached the bottom of the page...'. 26: Top of File Notification - When the top of the user list is reached while paging backward, display the message 'You have reached the top of the page...'. 27: Session State Preservation - Return control to the transaction with the updated communication area, preserving page state, selected user, pagination flags, and first/last user IDs for the next interaction.
